# Web sign-up and FamCal in the browser (item 6c-1) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A new person creates a FamCal account on famcal.bot with Google or an email code and uses the calendar, Google Calendar, the partner link and Settings in any browser with no messenger; later they connect Telegram without ending up with two accounts.

**Architecture:** Sign-up is the end of 6b's sign-in: when Google or an email code proves an identity that no account holds, a one-time `signup` flow record (behind the same `famcal_signin` cookie) carries it to `/signup`, where a name and consent create the account through one shared creation step (`createAccount`) that the bot and WhatsApp also use. Cloudflare Turnstile and budget shares protect the email path; bans gain Google and email identifiers. A browser-only account connects Telegram through a one-time bot link, and an accidental second account joins the first only after Add Google or Add email proves the way, through one merge rule set (`mergePlan`) that both the question and the merge read.

**Tech Stack:** Next.js 16 route handlers and pages (next-intl), Prisma + Neon, Upstash Redis, Cloudflare Turnstile (siteverify over `fetchAndReadWithRetry`, a hand-written explicit-render loader), Resend, node-telegram-bot-api, the repo's smoke tests (`scripts/smoke-*.ts`, tsx).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md` (approved by the owner 2026-11-04, the §7 legal wording included). It builds on 6b: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-web-sign-in-design.md`.

## Global Constraints

- **Before-blocks:** a before-block is the file at edd9d72e plus every earlier task's edits (tasks run in order 1–14). Re-read the file before each edit; when a block doesn't match, make the same change on the current text and keep the earlier tasks' code. Never re-create what an earlier task's Interfaces say it produced.
- **One smoke:** `$RUN` = `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-razielgershoni-development-famcalbot/0d239296-a217-49f9-8833-757c9d9a2df6/scratchpad/6c1/run-smoke.sh <name>` (Task 1 Step 1.0 writes it: the fake env of `scripts/ci-smokes.sh`, every local `.env*` name blanked, never read). After every task: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`, `npm run lint` and `bash scripts/ci-smokes.sh`, all green, not only the task's own smokes.
- Branch `feat/web-sign-up` off main; fast-forward to main and push once, at the end, after the CI mirror (`CI_OUT=<dir> bash <scratchpad>/ci-local.sh <sha>`). Never `npm run build`; use `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`, `npm run lint`, the smokes and `npx next build`.
- Everything new stays hidden and harmless while its env vars are unset: email sign-up needs `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET` and `RESEND_API_KEY`; Google sign-up needs 6b's `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET`. Startup checks warn, never fail. The Turnstile site key reaches the page at request time, never as `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.
- Never match a person by a typed address, a name or a phone number: Google by `sub`, an email by the code mailed to it, Telegram by the bot's sender id. `findWayByAddress` is a check on a verified address only, never a sign-in.
- Limits exactly as spec §5: Turnstile on every email-code request (when configured); sign-up codes 30 a UTC day inside the 90 and 3 per IP per day; security notices their own 10 a day above the 90, of which one account takes at most 3 a day; 5 new accounts per IPv4 address or IPv6 /48 per day (none counted without an address, logged); Connect links 5 an hour per account, a sign-in within the hour, 10 minutes and one use; the bot's Connect press and a Join: 10 minutes, once, bound to who started it.
- The name: trimmed, 1–60 characters; control, bidi and zero-width characters refused.
- Join is offered only after Add Google or Add email proves the way, only for an account with no chat that isn't the person's partner; W's trial never replaces T's plan; `mergePlan` is the one rule set for the question and the merge.
- Every new POST: `refuseCrossSite` (Origin `https://famcal.bot`, JSON).
- No console line or Sentry field holds an email address, a code, a token (Turnstile, connect, join, invite), a state or a name; log the user id, the way and the status. Every catch logs; `captureError` where the repo does.
- Retries only through `googleFetch` (Google) and `fetchWithRetry`/`fetchAndReadWithRetry` (Cloudflare, Telegram, Resend); no own retries or timeouts.
- Idle Neon: nothing new runs on a timer; every query runs because a person acted.
- Senders: the connect replies, the sign-up code and the notice emails are replies to the person's own action, `NOT_PAUSED` in `scripts/smoke-pause.ts`. Writers of FamCal calendars/events/pairings (the creation step, the merge) are classified in `scripts/smoke-alerts-gate-writers.ts`.
- All copy in `messages/{he,en,ru}.json`: Hebrew gender-neutral, Russian formal, natural; site pages' client strings in `site`. Lucide icons only, except Google's "G" mark. Inputs 16px. Mobile first, light/dark, RTL.
- Legal texts (`legal.*`) change in all three languages at once with `LEGAL_UPDATED` = the day of the fast-forward to main (Task 14 writes the day it runs; the controller corrects it at the merge), checked by the lawyer review; plan numbers stay hand-written.

  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
  `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017Qxen88HvHhmznBZG7Yo31`

## Review Focus

The spec doesn't spell these inputs out, and a person will meet them. Each line's test lives in the task named:

1. A visitor who is already signed in opens `/signup` (a bookmark, or Back after Create account). They go to their calendar; no form, and no second account (Task 5).
2. An address typed with capitals or spaces at sign-up, sign-in or Add email is the same way. An address an account already holds never starts a sign-up, and a new account's address is found again in any case (Task 4).
3. A name holding `<`, `&` or quotes arrives escaped in every HTML it lands in: the bot's Connect welcome (Task 6) and the notice email (Task 8).
4. A partner invite revoked or used by someone else while its visitor signs up. The account is made, with no pairing, and lands on the invite page's invalid state (Task 11).
5. A sign-up code requested in one browser and typed in another (no flow cookie there) answers restart and creates nothing; the first browser can still use the code within its 10 minutes (Task 4).

#### One creation step (`src/services/user-service.ts`, Task 1)
- `export type NewAccount =`
  `| { via: 'telegram'; telegramId: number; profile?: TelegramUserInfo }`
  `| { via: 'whatsapp'; identifier: string; profileName?: string; bsuid?: string; phone?: string; initialLanguage?: Locale }`
  `| { via: 'web'; way: { kind: IdentityKind; subject: string; address: string }; name: string; language: Locale };`
- `export class AccountBlockedError extends Error` (message names no identifier).
- `export async function createAccount(input: NewAccount): Promise<UserConfig>` — in order: the ban check for that identifier (`isIdentifierBlocked`, throws `AccountBlockedError`); one `prisma.$transaction`: `prisma.user.create` with the shared defaults (gender 'male', culture 'default', location '', googleRefreshToken '', the language, the name) and, for `via: 'web'`, `writeIdentityInTx` (a P2002 on (kind, subject) propagates: the caller answers `taken`); then `ensurePrimaryNativeCalendar(user.id)` (a failure is logged and `captureError`ed, the account stands); one line `[account] created user <id> via <telegram|whatsapp|web-google|web-email>`; `trackActivityAsync(id, 'web_signup', …)` for the web.
- `getOrCreateUser` and `getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp` keep their lookups and call `createAccount`. `scripts/smoke-account-create.ts` fails on any other `prisma.user.create` in `src/` and `app/`.

- Task 4: `export async function findWayByAddress(normalized: string): Promise<{ kind: IdentityKind; userId: number } | null>` — an email way whose subject is the address, or a Google way whose stored address lower-cased equals it. A check on a verified address only, never a sign-in.

#### Bans (`src/lib/user-moderation.ts`, Task 2)
- `BlockArgs` becomes `{ telegramId?: number | bigint | null; whatsappPhone?: string | null; googleSub?: string | null; email?: string | null }` (email normalised) and is exported.
- `isIdentifierBlocked(args: BlockArgs)`: same cache pattern; new keys `REDIS_KEYS.blockedGoogleSub(sub)` = `blocked:google:<sub>` and `REDIS_KEYS.blockedEmail(emailKey)` = `blocked:email:<emailKey>` (emailKey from `email-address.ts`).

Strings in he/en/ru.

#### Turnstile (`src/services/web-signin/turnstile.ts`, Task 3)
- `export function turnstileConfigured(): boolean` (both `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` and `TURNSTILE_SECRET` set)
- `export function turnstileSiteKey(): string | null` (read at request time by the server page and passed to the client; never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`)
- `export const TURNSTILE_ACTION = 'email-code';`
- `export async function verifyTurnstile(token: unknown, ip: string | null): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; why: 'missing' | 'refused' | 'hostname' | 'action' | 'unavailable' }>` — POST `https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify` (form: secret, response, remoteip when known, idempotency_key = one `crypto.randomUUID()` per call, reused on its retries) through `fetchAndReadWithRetry` with `wholeJson`; `hostname` must equal `new URL(getBaseUrl()).hostname`; `action` must equal `TURNSTILE_ACTION`; a token over 2048 chars is `missing`. Logs only `why` and Cloudflare's error codes, never the token.
- Client: `components/site/TurnstileWidget.tsx` (`'use client'`; loads `https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit` once, `turnstile.render` with `{ sitekey, action: 'email-code', theme: 'auto', language: <page locale>, callback, 'error-callback', 'expired-callback', 'timeout-callback' }`, `reset` after each request, `remove` on unmount; visible retry message on error/timeout). The email request body gains `token`.
- `POST /api/auth/email/request` reads `token` first and answers `{ ok: false, error: 'check' }` when Turnstile is configured and the check fails; the form shows `site.signin.emailCheck` (`site.signin.email` is already a string; "We couldn't check this browser. Try again, or use Google.").
- `SIGN_IN_ENV` (`scripts/smoke-signin-setup.ts`) gains `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET`; startup warnings and README rows likewise (Task 14 writes README/startup; Task 3 adds the smoke's names).

### Global rules for every part
- Read the spec in full, then the code you change; follow the real code over this contract and note corrections at the top of your part ("Contract notes").
- One code path per piece of logic; reuse: `getBaseUrl`, `appKey`, `fetchWithRetry`/`fetchAndReadWithRetry` + `wholeJson`, `googleFetch`, `captureError`, `notifyAdminWarning` (or what 6b's daily budget uses), `isIdentifierBlocked`, `getUserById`, `redis` (`src/utils/redis`), `prisma` (`src/utils/prisma`), `refuseCrossSite`, `clientAddress`, `startFlow`/`takeFlow`/`peekFlow`, `finishSignIn`, `verifyUserAuth`, `trackActivityAsync`.
- No silent failures: every catch logs (and `captureError` where the repo does). No console line or Sentry field holds an email address, a code, a token, a Turnstile token, a state or a name; log the user id, the method, the kind and the status.
- No timeouts or retry loops of our own (CLAUDE.md retry rules).
- Neon: no timer path queries; everything new runs only when a person acts.

Before (`:255-267`):

```ts
const models: Record<string, Row> = {};
export const fakePrisma: Row = new Proxy({} as Row, {
  get(_t, prop) {
    if (typeof prop !== 'string' || prop === 'then') return undefined;
    if (prop === '$transaction') {
      return async (arg: unknown) => {
        prismaCalls.push('$transaction');
        return typeof arg === 'function' ? arg(fakePrisma) : Promise.all(arg as Promise<unknown>[]);
      };
    }
    if (prop.startsWith('$')) return async () => undefined;
    return (models[prop] ??= model(prop));
  },
});
```

After:

```ts
const models: Record<string, Row> = {};
/** Every table's rows as they are now (a copy of each row), and putting them back: a transaction's rollback. */
const snapshotDB = (): Record<string, Row[]> => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(DB).map(([k, rows]) => [k, rows.map(r => ({ ...r }))]));
function restoreDB(saved: Record<string, Row[]>): void {
  for (const k of Object.keys(DB)) delete DB[k];
  Object.assign(DB, saved);
}
export const fakePrisma: Row = new Proxy({} as Row, {
  get(_t, prop) {
    if (typeof prop !== 'string' || prop === 'then') return undefined;
    if (prop === '$transaction') {
      return async (arg: unknown) => {
        prismaCalls.push('$transaction');
        if (typeof arg !== 'function') return Promise.all(arg as Promise<unknown>[]);
        // An interactive transaction: a throw undoes its writes, as Postgres rolls back
        const saved = snapshotDB();
        try {
          return await arg(fakePrisma);
        } catch (error) {
          restoreDB(saved);
          throw error;
        }
      };
    }
    if (prop.startsWith('$')) return async () => undefined;
    return (models[prop] ??= model(prop));
  },
});
```

```ts
//     deploy (additions only, safe to run twice), and the generated client that knows them;
//   - the scan: no other User create (create, createMany, upsert) in src/ or app/; getOrCreateUser and
//     getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp keep their lookups and create only through createAccount;
//   - each path's row:
//     - the shared defaults;
//     - Telegram's name and language, WhatsApp's ids and language, the web's typed name and page language;
//     - one primary calendar;
//     - an existing account is returned, never made again;
//   - the web:
//     - one user, one way and one calendar, the user and the way in one transaction, after the ban check;
//     - a way someone took meanwhile (P2002) rolls the user back and makes no calendar;
//     - web_signup is recorded;
//   - the ban check:
//     - AccountBlockedError for a banned Telegram id, WhatsApp number, Google account or address, and for a Google
//       sign-up whose verified address is banned;
//     - its message names no identifier;
//     - isIdentifierBlocked reads the new columns and primes their cache keys (blocked:google:<sub>,
//       blocked:email:<emailKey>);
//   - accountWays: the account's Google id and sign-in address;
//   - hasChat (src/lib/has-chat.ts): a Telegram id, a WhatsApp phone or a BSUID is a chat, for a database row (null) and a
//     UserConfig (undefined) alike; nothing is not;
//   - no log line holds a name, an address, a Telegram id, a phone or a Google id.
//
// Real: user-service, user-moderation, identities, onboarding, analytics. Faked at the boundaries
// (scripts/lib/signin-world.ts): Prisma (in memory; a transaction's writes are undone when it throws) and Redis in
// memory, error capture, the chats. No network, no DB.
//
// Run with the fake env of scripts/ci-smokes.sh:
//   bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-razielgershoni-development-famcalbot/0d239296-a217-49f9-8833-757c9d9a2df6/scratchpad/6c1/run-smoke.sh smoke-account-create

import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';
import { Prisma } from '@prisma/client';
import {
  assert, baseUser, captured, check, DB, everyLog, fakePrisma, identityRow, installSigninWorld, load, logs, prismaCalls,
  redisStore, report, resetWorld, ROOT, show, type Row,
} from './lib/signin-world';

const MIGRATION = '20261104000000_web_sign_up';
const read = (rel: string) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8');

/** Every .ts/.tsx file under src/ and app/, relative to the repo. */
function sourceFiles(): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const walk = (dir: string) => {
    for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir)) {
      if (entry === 'node_modules' || entry.startsWith('.')) continue;
      const full = path.join(dir, entry);
      if (fs.statSync(full).isDirectory()) walk(full);
      else if (/\.(ts|tsx)$/.test(entry)) out.push(path.relative(ROOT, full));
    }
  };
  for (const root of ['src', 'app']) walk(path.join(ROOT, root));
  return out.sort();
}

/** A top-level function's text (exported or not, async or not), from its line to the closing brace at the start of a line. */
function functionBody(source: string, name: string): string {
  const match = new RegExp(`^(?:export )?(?:async )?function ${name}\\(`, 'm').exec(source);
  assert(match, `no function ${name}`);
  const end = source.indexOf('\n}\n', match.index);
  return source.slice(match.index, end + 2);
}

/** Every write that makes a User row. */
const USER_CREATE = /\.user\s*\.\s*(create|createMany|createManyAndReturn|upsert)\s*\(/g;

/** The names and identifiers of the run: none may reach a log line. */
const SECRETS = [
  'Dana', 'Levi', 'Avi', 'Mira', 'dana@example.com', 'Dana@Gmail.com', 'dana@gmail.com', 'mira@example.com', '5550001', '5550002',
  '+972500000001', 'IL.123', 'g-sub-1', 'banned@example.com', 'Banned@Example.com', 'g-banned', 'g-fresh', '5550009', '+972500000009', 'taken@example.com',
];

const OLD = 77;
function seed(): void {
  resetWorld();
  DB.user = [baseUser({ id: OLD, name: 'Old', telegramId: BigInt(5550077) })];
  DB.signInIdentity = [identityRow({ userId: OLD, kind: 'email', subject: 'taken@example.com', address: 'taken@example.com' })];
  DB.nativeCalendar = [];
  DB.blockedIdentifier = [];
}
const newest = (): Row => DB.user[DB.user.length - 1];
const calendarsOf = (id: number): Row[] => (DB.nativeCalendar ?? []).filter(c => c.ownerUserId === id);
const createdLines = (): string[] => logs.filter(l => l.startsWith('[account] created user '));
const tick = () => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
const SHARED = { englishName: '', gender: 'male', location: '', culture: 'default', googleRefreshToken: '' };
const sharedOf = (row: Row) => ({ englishName: row.englishName, gender: row.gender, location: row.location, culture: row.culture, googleRefreshToken: row.googleRefreshToken });

async function main() {
  await installSigninWorld();
  const users = await load('src/services/user-service.ts');
  const moderation = await load('src/lib/user-moderation.ts');
  const identities = await load('src/services/web-signin/identities.ts');
  const { emailKey } = await load('src/services/web-signin/email-address.ts');

  await check('#1 the data: BlockedIdentifier has googleSub and email, each unique; the migration adds exactly those, only adds, and is safe to run twice; the generated client knows them', () => {
    const schema = read('prisma/schema.prisma');
    const model = /model BlockedIdentifier \{([\s\S]*?)\n\}/.exec(schema)?.[1] ?? '';
    const lines = model.split('\n').map(l => l.replace(/\/\/.*$/, '').trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ')).filter(Boolean);
    for (const want of ['googleSub String? @unique', 'email String? @unique']) assert(lines.includes(want), `BlockedIdentifier lacks "${want}": ${show(lines)}`);
    const file = path.join(ROOT, 'prisma/migrations', MIGRATION, 'migration.sql');
    assert(fs.existsSync(file), `no prisma/migrations/${MIGRATION}/migration.sql`);
    const sql = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(l => !l.trim().startsWith('--')).join(' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    for (const want of [
      'ALTER TABLE "BlockedIdentifier" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "googleSub" TEXT;',
      'ALTER TABLE "BlockedIdentifier" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "email" TEXT;',
      'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "BlockedIdentifier_googleSub_key" ON "BlockedIdentifier"("googleSub");',
      'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "BlockedIdentifier_email_key" ON "BlockedIdentifier"("email");',
    ]) assert(sql.includes(want), `the migration lacks: ${want}`);
    assert(!/\b(DROP|DELETE|UPDATE|RENAME|TRUNCATE)\b/i.test(sql), `the migration does more than add: ${sql}`);
    const fields = Object.values((Prisma as unknown as Record<string, Record<string, string> | undefined>).BlockedIdentifierScalarFieldEnum ?? {});
    assert(fields.includes('googleSub') && fields.includes('email'), `the generated client's BlockedIdentifier: ${show(fields)} (run prisma generate)`);
  });

  await check('#2 one creation step: the only User create in src/ and app/ is createAccount\'s; getOrCreateUser and getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp keep their lookups and create only through it', () => {
    const service = read('src/services/user-service.ts');
    const body = functionBody(service, 'createAccount');
    const start = service.indexOf(body);
    const stray: string[] = [];
    for (const file of sourceFiles()) {
      const text = read(file);
      for (const m of text.matchAll(USER_CREATE)) {
        const inside = file === 'src/services/user-service.ts' && m.index! >= start && m.index! < start + body.length;
        if (!inside) stray.push(`${file}:${text.slice(0, m.index).split('\n').length}`);
      }
    }
    assert(stray.length === 0, `a User row is made outside createAccount: ${show(stray)}`);
    assert((body.match(USER_CREATE) ?? []).length === 1, 'createAccount makes the row more than once, or not at all');
    const telegram = functionBody(service, 'getOrCreateUser');
    const whatsapp = functionBody(service, 'getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp');
    assert(/createAccount\(\{\s*via: 'telegram'/.test(telegram) && telegram.includes('findUnique'), `getOrCreateUser: ${telegram}`);
    assert(/createAccount\(\{\s*via: 'whatsapp'/.test(whatsapp) && (whatsapp.match(/findUnique/g) ?? []).length === 4, `getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp: ${whatsapp}`);
  });

  await check('#3 /start: a new Telegram id gets one account with the shared defaults, its Telegram name and language, messagingPlatform telegram and one primary FamCal calendar; the same id again gets the same account and makes nothing; no web_signup', async () => {
    seed();
    const dana = await users.getOrCreateUser(5550001, { first_name: 'Dana', last_name: 'Levi', language_code: 'he-IL' });
    const row = newest();
    assert(row.id === dana.id && DB.user.length === 2, `rows ${show(DB.user.map(u => u.id))}`);
    const got = { telegramId: String(row.telegramId), name: row.name, language: row.language, messagingPlatform: row.messagingPlatform, ...sharedOf(row) };
    const want = { telegramId: '5550001', name: 'Dana Levi', language: 'he', messagingPlatform: 'telegram', ...SHARED };
    assert(show(got) === show(want), `the row ${show(got)}`);
    const calendars = calendarsOf(row.id);
    assert(calendars.length === 1 && show(calendars[0].labels) === show(['primary', 'yours']), `calendars ${show(calendars)}`);
    assert(show(createdLines()) === show([`[account] created user ${row.id} via telegram`]), `log ${show(createdLines())}`);
    const again = await users.getOrCreateUser(5550001, { first_name: 'Other' });
    assert(again.id === dana.id && DB.user.length === 2 && calendarsOf(row.id).length === 1 && createdLines().length === 1, 'the same Telegram id made a second account');
    await users.getOrCreateUser(5550002);
    assert(newest().name === 'User' && newest().language === 'en', `no profile: ${show({ name: newest().name, language: newest().language })}`);
    await tick();
    assert(!(DB.userActivity ?? []).some(a => a.action === 'web_signup'), 'a /start recorded web_signup');
  });

  await check('#4 a first WhatsApp message: a number gets its account (phone, language, messagingPlatform whatsapp, the defaults, one calendar), a BSUID alone gets one with no phone; each found again by its lookup', async () => {
    seed();
    const avi = await users.getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp('+972500000001', 'Avi', undefined, '+972500000001', 'ru');
    const row = newest();
    const got = { telegramId: row.telegramId, whatsappPhone: row.whatsappPhone, whatsappBsuid: row.whatsappBsuid, name: row.name, language: row.language, messagingPlatform: row.messagingPlatform, ...sharedOf(row) };
    const want = { telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: '+972500000001', whatsappBsuid: null, name: 'Avi', language: 'ru', messagingPlatform: 'whatsapp', ...SHARED };
    assert(row.id === avi.id && show(got) === show(want), `the row ${show(got)}`);
    assert(calendarsOf(row.id).length === 1 && createdLines().includes(`[account] created user ${row.id} via whatsapp`), `calendar ${calendarsOf(row.id).length}, log ${show(createdLines())}`);
    const mira = await users.getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp('IL.123', 'Mira', 'IL.123');
    assert(newest().id === mira.id && newest().whatsappBsuid === 'IL.123' && newest().whatsappPhone === null && newest().language === 'en', `BSUID only: ${show({ phone: newest().whatsappPhone, bsuid: newest().whatsappBsuid })}`);
    const count = DB.user.length;
    assert((await users.getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp('+972500000001')).id === avi.id && (await users.getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp('IL.123', undefined, 'IL.123')).id === mira.id && DB.user.length === count, 'a known number or BSUID made another account');
  });

  await check('#5 a sign-up on famcal.bot: after the ban check, one transaction makes the user (the typed name, the page language, the defaults, no chat) and its way (used now), then one primary calendar; the log says via web-email / web-google; web_signup is recorded with the way', async () => {
    seed();
    prismaCalls.length = 0;
    const dana = await users.createAccount({ via: 'web', way: { kind: 'email', subject: 'dana@example.com', address: 'dana@example.com' }, name: 'Dana', language: 'he' });
    const row = DB.user.find(u => u.id === dana.id) as Row;
    const got = { telegramId: row.telegramId, whatsappPhone: row.whatsappPhone, whatsappBsuid: row.whatsappBsuid, name: row.name, language: row.language, messagingPlatform: row.messagingPlatform, ...sharedOf(row) };
    const want = { telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null, whatsappBsuid: null, name: 'Dana', language: 'he', messagingPlatform: 'telegram', ...SHARED };
    assert(show(got) === show(want), `the row ${show(got)}`);
    const ways = DB.signInIdentity.filter(i => i.userId === dana.id);
    assert(ways.length === 1 && ways[0].kind === 'email' && ways[0].subject === 'dana@example.com' && ways[0].address === 'dana@example.com' && ways[0].lastUsedAt instanceof Date, `ways ${show(ways)}`);
    assert(calendarsOf(dana.id).length === 1, `calendars ${calendarsOf(dana.id).length}`);
    const at = (call: string) => prismaCalls.indexOf(call);
    assert(at('blockedIdentifier.findFirst') >= 0 && at('blockedIdentifier.findFirst') < at('$transaction') && at('$transaction') < at('user.create') && at('user.create') < at('signInIdentity.create') && at('signInIdentity.create') < at('nativeCalendar.create'), `order ${show(prismaCalls)}`);
    assert(show(createdLines()) === show([`[account] created user ${dana.id} via web-email`]), `log ${show(createdLines())}`);
    await tick();
    const activity = (DB.userActivity ?? []).filter(a => a.userId === dana.id && a.action === 'web_signup');
    assert(activity.length === 1 && activity[0].metadata?.way === 'email' && !show(activity[0]).includes('dana@example.com'), `activity ${show(DB.userActivity)}`);
    const google = await users.createAccount({ via: 'web', way: { kind: 'google', subject: 'g-sub-1', address: 'Dana@Gmail.com' }, name: 'Dana G', language: 'en' });
    const gWays = DB.signInIdentity.filter(i => i.userId === google.id);
    assert(gWays.length === 1 && gWays[0].kind === 'google' && gWays[0].subject === 'g-sub-1' && gWays[0].address === 'Dana@Gmail.com', `Google way ${show(gWays)}`);
    assert(createdLines().includes(`[account] created user ${google.id} via web-google`), `log ${show(createdLines())}`);
  });

  await check('#6 a way another account took meanwhile fails the unique (kind, subject) with P2002: createAccount throws it, and the user row is rolled back, with no way and no calendar', async () => {
    seed();
    const before = { users: DB.user.length, ways: DB.signInIdentity.length };
    let thrown: unknown = null;
    try {
      await users.createAccount({ via: 'web', way: { kind: 'email', subject: 'taken@example.com', address: 'taken@example.com' }, name: 'Mira', language: 'en' });
    } catch (error) {
      thrown = error;
    }
    assert((thrown as Row | null)?.code === 'P2002', `thrown ${show(thrown)}`);
    assert(DB.user.length === before.users && DB.signInIdentity.length === before.ways && (DB.nativeCalendar ?? []).length === 0, `left ${show({ users: DB.user.length, ways: DB.signInIdentity.length, calendars: DB.nativeCalendar })}`);
    assert(createdLines().length === 0, `log ${show(createdLines())}`);
  });

  await check('#7 a banned identifier gets AccountBlockedError and no account on every path: a Telegram id, a WhatsApp number, a Google account, an address, and a Google sign-up whose verified address is banned; the message names none of them; isIdentifierBlocked reads googleSub and email and primes their keys', async () => {
    seed();
    const ban = (o: Row): Row => ({ id: DB.blockedIdentifier.length + 1, telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null, googleSub: null, email: null, bannedBy: 9, bannedReason: null, createdAt: new Date(), ...o });
    DB.blockedIdentifier.push(ban({ telegramId: BigInt(5550009) }));
    DB.blockedIdentifier.push(ban({ whatsappPhone: '+972500000009' }));
    DB.blockedIdentifier.push(ban({ googleSub: 'g-banned' }));
    DB.blockedIdentifier.push(ban({ email: 'banned@example.com' }));
    const tries: [string, () => Promise<unknown>][] = [
      ['a banned Telegram id', () => users.getOrCreateUser(5550009, { first_name: 'Dana' })],
      ['a banned WhatsApp number', () => users.getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp('+972500000009', 'Avi', undefined, '+972500000009')],
      ['a banned Google account', () => users.createAccount({ via: 'web', way: { kind: 'google', subject: 'g-banned', address: 'dana@gmail.com' }, name: 'Dana', language: 'en' })],
      ['a banned address', () => users.createAccount({ via: 'web', way: { kind: 'email', subject: 'banned@example.com', address: 'banned@example.com' }, name: 'Dana', language: 'en' })],
      ['a Google sign-up whose verified address is banned', () => users.createAccount({ via: 'web', way: { kind: 'google', subject: 'g-fresh', address: 'Banned@Example.com' }, name: 'Dana', language: 'en' })],
    ];
    for (const [label, run] of tries) {
      let thrown: unknown = null;
      try {
        await run();
      } catch (error) {
        thrown = error;
      }
      assert(thrown instanceof users.AccountBlockedError && (thrown as Error).name === 'AccountBlockedError', `${label}: ${show(thrown)}`);
      const message = (thrown as Error).message;
      assert(!SECRETS.some(s => message.includes(s)), `${label}: the message names it: ${message}`);
    }
    assert(DB.user.length === 1 && (DB.nativeCalendar ?? []).length === 0 && DB.signInIdentity.length === 1 && createdLines().length === 0, `made ${show({ users: DB.user.length, calendars: DB.nativeCalendar, log: createdLines() })}`);
    assert(!('IdentifierBlockedError' in users), 'IdentifierBlockedError is still exported');
    redisStore.clear();
    assert((await moderation.isIdentifierBlocked({ googleSub: 'g-banned' })) === true, 'a banned Google account reads as not blocked');
    assert((await moderation.isIdentifierBlocked({ email: 'banned@example.com' })) === true, 'a banned address reads as not blocked');
    assert((await moderation.isIdentifierBlocked({ googleSub: 'g-other', email: 'other@example.com' })) === false, 'an unknown Google account and address read as blocked');
    assert((await moderation.isIdentifierBlocked({})) === false, 'nothing given reads as blocked');
    const keys = [...redisStore.keys()];
    assert(keys.includes('blocked:google:g-banned') && keys.includes(`blocked:email:${emailKey('banned@example.com')}`) && !keys.some(k => k.includes('banned@example.com')), `cache keys ${show(keys)}`);
  });

  await check('#8 the first calendar failing is logged and reported by its kind only (user id, no message: it can hold the name), and the account stands with its way', async () => {
    seed();
    const calendars = (fakePrisma as Row).nativeCalendar as Row;
    const real = calendars.create;
    calendars.create = async () => {
      throw Object.assign(new Error('Invalid `prisma.nativeCalendar.create()` invocation: name: "Mira"'), { code: 'P1001' });
    };
    try {
      const mira = await users.createAccount({ via: 'web', way: { kind: 'email', subject: 'mira@example.com', address: 'mira@example.com' }, name: 'Mira', language: 'ru' });
      assert(DB.user.some(u => u.id === mira.id) && DB.signInIdentity.some(i => i.userId === mira.id), 'the account did not stand');
      const sentry = captured.find(c => c.context === 'account-calendar');
      assert(sentry && sentry.extra.user_id === mira.id && !sentry.message.includes('Mira'), `Sentry ${show(captured)}`);
      assert(logs.some(l => l.startsWith(`[account] user ${mira.id}: making the first FamCal calendar failed`)), `logs ${show(logs)}`);
      assert(show(createdLines()) === show([`[account] created user ${mira.id} via web-email`]), `log ${show(createdLines())}`);
    } finally {
      calendars.create = real;
    }
  });

  await check('#9 accountWays: the account\'s Google account id and sign-in address (the email way\'s subject), null for each it lacks', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: OLD, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-old', address: 'old@gmail.com' }));
    assert(show(await identities.accountWays(OLD)) === show({ googleSub: 'g-old', email: 'taken@example.com' }), 'both ways');
    assert(show(await identities.accountWays(12345)) === show({ googleSub: null, email: null }), 'no ways');
  });

  await check('#10 no log line of the run holds a name, an address, a Telegram id, a phone or a Google id', () => {
    const leaks = everyLog.filter(l => SECRETS.some(s => l.includes(s)));
    assert(leaks.length === 0, `leaks ${show(leaks)}`);
  });

  await check('#11 hasChat: a Telegram id, a WhatsApp phone or a BSUID is a chat; a row with null ids and a UserConfig with undefined ones (a browser-only account) is not', async () => {
    const { hasChat } = await load('src/lib/has-chat.ts');
    assert(hasChat({ telegramId: 5 }) === true && hasChat({ telegramId: BigInt(5) }) === true, 'a Telegram id');
    assert(hasChat({ telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: '+972500000001', whatsappBsuid: null }) === true, 'a WhatsApp phone');
    assert(hasChat({ telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null, whatsappBsuid: 'IL.123' }) === true, 'a BSUID');
    assert(hasChat({ telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null, whatsappBsuid: null }) === false, 'a database row with no chat');
    assert(hasChat({ telegramId: undefined, whatsappPhone: undefined, whatsappBsuid: undefined }) === false && hasChat({ telegramId: null }) === false, 'a UserConfig with no chat');
    assert(hasChat({ telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: '', whatsappBsuid: '' }) === false, 'empty ids');
  });

  report();
}

main().catch(err => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

Note: `console.error` in the last lines is the world's recorded console. A crash still exits 1, and `report()` prints the reason of each check.

- [ ] **Step 1.3: Run it and see it fail**

```bash
$RUN smoke-account-create
```

Expected: exit 1, with these failing:

- `FAIL  #2 … no function createAccount`
- `#3`, `#4` (the log line is `[User] Created new …`, not `[account] created user …`)
- `#5`, `#6`, `#7`, `#8` (`users.createAccount is not a function`)
- `#9` (`identities.accountWays is not a function`)
- `#10` (`[User] Created new user: Dana Levi (Telegram ID: 5550001)` leaks a name and an id)
- `#11` (`Cannot find module '…/src/lib/has-chat.ts'`)

- [ ] **Step 1.4: The schema, the migration, the generated client**

Before (`prisma/schema.prisma:137-149`):

```prisma
// Persistent blocklist for telegramId / whatsappPhone.
// Survives hard delete so banned identifiers cannot re-register.
model BlockedIdentifier {
  id            Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  telegramId    BigInt?  @unique
  whatsappPhone String?  @unique
  bannedBy      Int // Admin User.id who banned
  bannedReason  String?  @db.Text
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([telegramId])
  @@index([whatsappPhone])
}
```

After:

```prisma
// Persistent blocklist: Telegram ids, WhatsApp numbers, Google account ids (sub) and sign-in email addresses
// (normalizeEmail's form), one identifier per row. Survives hard delete so a banned identifier cannot sign up again.
model BlockedIdentifier {
  id            Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  telegramId    BigInt?  @unique
  whatsappPhone String?  @unique
  googleSub     String?  @unique // Google's account id, never the address
  email         String?  @unique // The normalised address
  bannedBy      Int // Admin User.id who banned
  bannedReason  String?  @db.Text
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([telegramId])
  @@index([whatsappPhone])
}
```

Create `prisma/migrations/20261104000000_web_sign_up/migration.sql`:

```sql
-- Web sign-up on famcal.bot (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md §2.8, §3.8).
--
-- "BlockedIdentifier"."googleSub": a banned Google account, by Google's account id (never the address).
-- "BlockedIdentifier"."email": a banned sign-in address, in normalizeEmail's form. Each is unique, like the Telegram id
-- and the WhatsApp number, so a ban is one row per identifier and a second ban of the same one updates its reason.
--
-- Additions only, so one push is enough: the previous build, still serving while this runs, never reads or writes
-- them. Hand-written and idempotent, like the other recent migrations: each is made only when missing, so a re-run is
-- a no-op.

ALTER TABLE "BlockedIdentifier" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "googleSub" TEXT;
ALTER TABLE "BlockedIdentifier" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "email" TEXT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "BlockedIdentifier_googleSub_key" ON "BlockedIdentifier"("googleSub");
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "BlockedIdentifier_email_key" ON "BlockedIdentifier"("email");
```

```ts
// ============================================
// BLOCKLIST
// ============================================

interface BlockArgs {
  telegramId?: number | bigint | null;
  whatsappPhone?: string | null;
}

/**
 * Returns true if either identifier is currently blocked.
 * Cached in Redis for 1h; the cache is primed/cleared by ban/unban.
 */
export async function isIdentifierBlocked({ telegramId, whatsappPhone }: BlockArgs): Promise<boolean> {
  // Quick path: check Redis caches first
  if (telegramId) {
    try {
      const cached = await redis.get<string>(REDIS_KEYS.blockedTelegramId(telegramId.toString()));
      if (cached === '1') return true;
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('[Moderation] Reading the blocklist cache failed; asking the database', err);
    }
  }
  if (whatsappPhone) {
    try {
      const cached = await redis.get<string>(REDIS_KEYS.blockedWhatsAppPhone(whatsappPhone));
      if (cached === '1') return true;
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('[Moderation] Reading the blocklist cache failed; asking the database', err);
    }
  }

  // DB fallback
  const filters: Array<{ telegramId?: bigint } | { whatsappPhone?: string }> = [];
  if (telegramId) filters.push({ telegramId: BigInt(telegramId) });
  if (whatsappPhone) filters.push({ whatsappPhone });
  if (filters.length === 0) return false;

  const blocked = await prisma.blockedIdentifier.findFirst({
    where: { OR: filters },
  });

  if (blocked) {
    // Re-prime cache
    const reprimeFailed = (err: unknown) => console.warn('[Moderation] Re-priming the blocklist cache failed', err);
    if (blocked.telegramId !== null) {
      redis.set(REDIS_KEYS.blockedTelegramId(blocked.telegramId.toString()), '1', { ex: BLOCK_CACHE_TTL }).catch(reprimeFailed);
    }
    if (blocked.whatsappPhone) {
      redis.set(REDIS_KEYS.blockedWhatsAppPhone(blocked.whatsappPhone), '1', { ex: BLOCK_CACHE_TTL }).catch(reprimeFailed);
    }
    return true;
  }

  return false;
}
```

After:

```ts
// ============================================
// BLOCKLIST
// ============================================

/**
 * The identifiers a ban names, one row each (web sign-up spec §2.8, §3.8): a Telegram id, a WhatsApp number, a Google
 * account id (`sub`) and a sign-in address (normalizeEmail's form). Any may be absent.
 */
export interface BlockArgs {
  telegramId?: number | bigint | null;
  whatsappPhone?: string | null;
  googleSub?: string | null;
  email?: string | null;
}

/** The blocklist rows that name any of them. */
function blockFilters(args: BlockArgs): Prisma.BlockedIdentifierWhereInput[] {
  const filters: Prisma.BlockedIdentifierWhereInput[] = [];
  if (args.telegramId) filters.push({ telegramId: BigInt(args.telegramId) });
  if (args.whatsappPhone) filters.push({ whatsappPhone: args.whatsappPhone });
  if (args.googleSub) filters.push({ googleSub: args.googleSub });
  if (args.email) filters.push({ email: args.email });
  return filters;
}

/**
 * An email ban's cache key, blocked:email:<emailKey>: the keyed hash the other sign-in keys use, never the address.
 * null (logged) when SESSION_SECRET is unset, so the database answers instead (no email way can exist then).
 */
function emailCacheKey(email: string): string | null {
  try {
    return REDIS_KEYS.blockedEmail(emailKey(email));
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`[Moderation] No sign-in key for an email ban's cache; the database answers (${err instanceof Error ? err.name : typeof err})`);
    return null;
  }
}

/** The cache key of each identifier given. */
function blockCacheKeys(args: BlockArgs): string[] {
  const keys: string[] = [];
  if (args.telegramId) keys.push(REDIS_KEYS.blockedTelegramId(args.telegramId.toString()));
  if (args.whatsappPhone) keys.push(REDIS_KEYS.blockedWhatsAppPhone(args.whatsappPhone));
  if (args.googleSub) keys.push(REDIS_KEYS.blockedGoogleSub(args.googleSub));
  const mailKey = args.email ? emailCacheKey(args.email) : null;
  if (mailKey) keys.push(mailKey);
  return keys;
}

/** A blocklist row's identifier, as BlockArgs. */
function argsOfRow(row: BlockedIdentifier): BlockArgs {
  return { telegramId: row.telegramId, whatsappPhone: row.whatsappPhone, googleSub: row.googleSub, email: row.email };
}

/**
 * Whether any identifier given is blocked. Cached in Redis for 1h per identifier: a ban and a hit here prime the
 * cache, and an unban clears it.
 */
export async function isIdentifierBlocked(args: BlockArgs): Promise<boolean> {
  // Quick path: the cache of each identifier given
  for (const key of blockCacheKeys(args)) {
    try {
      const cached = await redis.get<string>(key);
      if (cached === '1') return true;
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('[Moderation] Reading the blocklist cache failed; asking the database', err);
    }
  }

  // The database
  const filters = blockFilters(args);
  if (filters.length === 0) return false;
  const blocked = await prisma.blockedIdentifier.findFirst({ where: { OR: filters } });
  if (!blocked) return false;

  // Re-prime the cache of the entry found
  const reprimeFailed = (err: unknown) => console.warn('[Moderation] Re-priming the blocklist cache failed', err);
  for (const key of blockCacheKeys(argsOfRow(blocked))) {
    redis.set(key, '1', { ex: BLOCK_CACHE_TTL }).catch(reprimeFailed);
  }
  return true;
}
```

(`banIdentifier`, `unbanIdentifier` and `listBlockedIdentifiers` stay as they are until Task 2. They read only `telegramId` and `whatsappPhone`, so they still compile.)

```ts

/**
 * The first way of an account made on famcal.bot, written inside createAccount's transaction (user-service.ts), so the
 * account and its way are made together or not at all. The sign-up signs in with it at once, so its last use is now.
 * A way another account took meanwhile fails the unique (kind, subject) with P2002, which rolls the account back; the
 * caller answers 'taken'.
 */
export async function writeIdentityInTx(
  tx: Prisma.TransactionClient,
  userId: number,
  kind: IdentityKind,
  subject: string,
  address: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await tx.signInIdentity.create({ data: { userId, kind, subject, address, lastUsedAt: new Date() } });
}

/**
 * The account's Google account id and its sign-in address (the email way's normalised subject), null for each it
 * lacks: what a ban records (user-moderation.ts) and what signInRefusal checks (web-session.ts).
 */
export async function accountWays(userId: number): Promise<{ googleSub: string | null; email: string | null }> {
  const rows = await prisma.signInIdentity.findMany({ where: { userId }, select: { kind: true, subject: true } });
  return {
    googleSub: rows.find(r => r.kind === 'google')?.subject ?? null,
    email: rows.find(r => r.kind === 'email')?.subject ?? null,
  };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Whether an account has a chat FamCal can write to (web sign-up spec §3.11): Telegram, or WhatsApp by its phone or its
 * BSUID. An account made on famcal.bot has none until it connects Telegram. One rule for the server and the pages.
 *
 * A row from the database has null for a missing id; a UserConfig (convertPrismaUserToConfig) has undefined for the
 * WhatsApp ones. Both count as missing. Client-safe: no import.
 */
export function hasChat(user: {
  telegramId: number | bigint | null | undefined;
  whatsappPhone?: string | null;
  whatsappBsuid?: string | null;
}): boolean {
  return user.telegramId != null || Boolean(user.whatsappPhone) || Boolean(user.whatsappBsuid);
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Telegram user info for registration
 */
export interface TelegramUserInfo {
  first_name?: string;
  last_name?: string;
  language_code?: string;
}

/**
 * Get or create user by Telegram ID
 * Auto-registers new users with minimal defaults from Telegram profile
 */
export async function getOrCreateUser(
  telegramId: number,
  telegramUser?: TelegramUserInfo
): Promise<UserConfig> {
  // Try to find existing user
  const existingUser = await prisma.user.findUnique({
    where: { telegramId: BigInt(telegramId) }
  });

  if (existingUser) {
    return convertPrismaUserToConfig(existingUser);
  }

  // Defense-in-depth: never silently materialize a banned identifier.
  // Webhook handlers gate this path already, but this catches any other call site.
  if (await isIdentifierBlocked({ telegramId })) {
    throw new IdentifierBlockedError(`Telegram ID ${telegramId} is blocked`);
  }

  // Map Telegram language code to our locale
  const language = mapTelegramLanguage(telegramUser?.language_code);

  // Build name from Telegram data
  const name = [telegramUser?.first_name, telegramUser?.last_name]
    .filter(Boolean).join(' ') || 'User';

  // Create new user with defaults. calendarSource defaults to NATIVE in the
  // schema; new users land in the in-bot calendar unless they connect Google.
  const newUser = await prisma.user.create({
    data: {
      telegramId: BigInt(telegramId),
      name,
      englishName: '',
      gender: 'male',  // Where everyone starts; the person picks "Address me as" in Settings (app/api/settings)
      language,
      location: '',
      culture: 'default',
      messagingPlatform: 'telegram',
      googleRefreshToken: '',  // Empty for NATIVE users; OAuth fills this for GOOGLE.
    }
  });

  // Best-effort primary calendar bootstrap so voice CRUD works on first event.
  // Failure is non-fatal — it'll be retried lazily on next CRUD or settings load.
  try {
    const { ensurePrimaryNativeCalendar } = await import('./native-calendar/onboarding');
    await ensurePrimaryNativeCalendar(newUser.id);
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`[User] Failed to bootstrap primary native calendar for ${newUser.id}:`, err);
  }

  console.log(`[User] Created new user: ${name} (Telegram ID: ${telegramId})`);
  return convertPrismaUserToConfig(newUser);
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Telegram user info for registration
 */
export interface TelegramUserInfo {
  first_name?: string;
  last_name?: string;
  language_code?: string;
}

/** What a new account is made from: the bot's /start, a first WhatsApp message, or a sign-up on famcal.bot. */
export type NewAccount =
  | { via: 'telegram'; telegramId: number; profile?: TelegramUserInfo }
  | { via: 'whatsapp'; identifier: string; profileName?: string; bsuid?: string; phone?: string; initialLanguage?: Locale }
  | { via: 'web'; way: { kind: IdentityKind; subject: string; address: string }; name: string; language: Locale };

type WhatsAppAccount = Extract<NewAccount, { via: 'whatsapp' }>;

/** A WhatsApp sender's phone and BSUID: the ones given, else the identifier as whichever it looks like. */
function whatsAppIds(input: WhatsAppAccount): { phone: string | undefined; bsuid: string | undefined } {
  const isBsuid = !/^\+?\d+$/.test(input.identifier);
  return {
    phone: input.phone || (isBsuid ? undefined : input.identifier),
    bsuid: input.bsuid || (isBsuid ? input.identifier : undefined),
  };
}

/** How the account was made, for the one log line. */
function createdVia(input: NewAccount): 'telegram' | 'whatsapp' | 'web-google' | 'web-email' {
  return input.via === 'web' ? `web-${input.way.kind}` : input.via;
}

/**
 * The identifiers the blocklist is asked about: the Telegram id; the WhatsApp phone when one is known (the blocklist
 * holds no BSUID); a Google way's account id and its verified address (spec §2.8: a Google sign-up is checked against
 * the email bans too); an email way's address.
 */
function blockArgsOf(input: NewAccount): BlockArgs {
  switch (input.via) {
    case 'telegram':
      return { telegramId: input.telegramId };
    case 'whatsapp':
      return { whatsappPhone: whatsAppIds(input).phone ?? null };
    case 'web':
      return input.way.kind === 'google'
        ? { googleSub: input.way.subject, email: normalizeEmail(input.way.address) }
        : { email: input.way.subject };
  }
}

/** The row a new account starts with: the shared defaults (the person changes them in Settings) and what its way gives. */
function accountData(input: NewAccount): Prisma.UserCreateInput {
  const shared = {
    englishName: '',
    gender: 'male', // Where everyone starts; the person picks "Address me as" in Settings (app/api/settings)
    location: '',
    culture: 'default',
    // Empty until Google is connected. calendarSource defaults to NATIVE in the schema: a new account starts in FamCal's own calendar.
    googleRefreshToken: '',
  };
  switch (input.via) {
    case 'telegram':
      return {
        ...shared,
        telegramId: BigInt(input.telegramId),
        name: [input.profile?.first_name, input.profile?.last_name].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || 'User',
        language: mapTelegramLanguage(input.profile?.language_code),
        messagingPlatform: 'telegram',
      };
    case 'whatsapp': {
      const ids = whatsAppIds(input);
      return {
        ...shared,
        whatsappPhone: ids.phone,
        whatsappBsuid: ids.bsuid,
        name: input.profileName || 'User',
        language: normalizeLocale(input.initialLanguage),
        messagingPlatform: 'whatsapp',
      };
    }
    case 'web':
      // No chat. "Has a chat" is read from the ids (telegramId, whatsappPhone, whatsappBsuid), never from
      // messagingPlatform, which keeps the schema's default.
      return { ...shared, name: input.name, language: input.language, messagingPlatform: 'telegram' };
  }
}

/**
 * The one creation step (web sign-up spec §2.7, §3.5). Every new account is made here: the bot's /start
 * (getOrCreateUser), a first WhatsApp message (getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp) and a sign-up on famcal.bot (Task 5's
 * completeSignUp). In order:
 * 1. The blocklist, for that way's identifiers. A banned one throws AccountBlockedError. The webhook handlers gate the
 *    chat paths already; this is the defense in depth for every caller.
 * 2. One transaction: the user row with the shared defaults and, for the web, its sign-in way (writeIdentityInTx). A
 *    way someone took meanwhile throws P2002 out of here with nothing made; the caller answers 'taken'.
 * 3. Its first FamCal calendar (ensurePrimaryNativeCalendar), so the first event has somewhere to go. A failure is
 *    logged and reported by its kind only (an error message can hold the calendar's name, which is the person's), and
 *    the account stands: the calendar is made again on the next calendar use.
 * 4. One log line with the user id and how the account was made, never a name or an identifier; and web_signup for the web.
 */
export async function createAccount(input: NewAccount): Promise<UserConfig> {
  const via = createdVia(input);
  if (await isIdentifierBlocked(blockArgsOf(input))) {
    console.warn(`[account] a new account via ${via} was refused: an identifier is on the blocklist`);
    throw new AccountBlockedError();
  }

  // Loaded only for the web: the chat paths never need the sign-in module
  const writeWay = input.via === 'web' ? (await import('./web-signin/identities')).writeIdentityInTx : null;
  const user = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    const created = await tx.user.create({ data: accountData(input) });
    if (input.via === 'web' && writeWay) await writeWay(tx, created.id, input.way.kind, input.way.subject, input.way.address);
    return created;
  });

  try {
    const { ensurePrimaryNativeCalendar } = await import('./native-calendar/onboarding');
    await ensurePrimaryNativeCalendar(user.id);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`[account] user ${user.id}: making the first FamCal calendar failed; it is made on the next calendar use`);
    captureSignInFailure(err, 'account-calendar', { user_id: user.id });
  }

  console.log(`[account] created user ${user.id} via ${via}`);
  if (input.via === 'web') trackActivityAsync(user.id, 'web_signup', { language: user.language, way: input.way.kind });
  return convertPrismaUserToConfig(user);
}

/**
 * Get or create user by Telegram ID
 * Auto-registers new users with minimal defaults from Telegram profile (createAccount)
 */
export async function getOrCreateUser(
  telegramId: number,
  telegramUser?: TelegramUserInfo
): Promise<UserConfig> {
  // Try to find existing user
  const existingUser = await prisma.user.findUnique({
    where: { telegramId: BigInt(telegramId) }
  });

  if (existingUser) {
    return convertPrismaUserToConfig(existingUser);
  }

  return createAccount({ via: 'telegram', telegramId, profile: telegramUser });
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Get or create user by WhatsApp identifier (phone or BSUID)
 * Auto-registers new WhatsApp users with minimal defaults. `initialLanguage` is the language a new user starts
 * in (English when unset); a user who already exists keeps theirs.
 */
export async function getOrCreateUserByWhatsApp(
  identifier: string,
  profileName?: string,
  bsuid?: string,
  phone?: string,
  initialLanguage?: Locale
): Promise<UserConfig> {
  // Try lookup by BSUID first, then phone
  if (bsuid) {
    const byBsuid = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { whatsappBsuid: bsuid } });
    if (byBsuid) return convertPrismaUserToConfig(byBsuid);
  }
  if (phone) {
    const byPhone = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { whatsappPhone: phone } });
    if (byPhone) return convertPrismaUserToConfig(byPhone);
  }
  // Also try the raw identifier
  const isBsuid = !identifier.match(/^\+?\d+$/);
  if (!isBsuid) {
    const byPhone = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { whatsappPhone: identifier } });
    if (byPhone) return convertPrismaUserToConfig(byPhone);

    const byBsuid = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { whatsappBsuid: identifier } });
    if (byBsuid) return convertPrismaUserToConfig(byBsuid);

  // Defense-in-depth: refuse to create a fresh user for a blocked phone.
  const phoneToCheck = phone || (isBsuid ? null : identifier);
  if (phoneToCheck && await isIdentifierBlocked({ whatsappPhone: phoneToCheck })) {
    throw new IdentifierBlockedError(`WhatsApp phone ${phoneToCheck} is blocked`);
  }

  const name = profileName || 'User';

  const newUser = await prisma.user.create({
    data: {
      whatsappPhone: phone || (isBsuid ? undefined : identifier),
      whatsappBsuid: bsuid || (isBsuid ? identifier : undefined),

    console.warn(`[User] Failed to bootstrap primary native calendar for ${newUser.id}:`, err);
  }

  console.log(`[User] Created new WhatsApp user: ${name} (ID: ${identifier})`);
  return convertPrismaUserToConfig(newUser);
}
```

```ts
  } else if (!bsuid) {
    const byBsuid = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { whatsappBsuid: identifier } });
    if (byBsuid) return convertPrismaUserToConfig(byBsuid);
  }

  return createAccount({ via: 'whatsapp', identifier, profileName, bsuid, phone, initialLanguage });
}
```

```ts
// Smoke test for bans that cover web accounts (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.8, §2.15, §3.8; plan 6c-1 Task 2).
//
// What it pins:
//   - a ban by the account's database id:
//     - records each identifier the account has, one row each (Telegram id, WhatsApp number, Google account id,
//       sign-in address);
//     - ends the web sessions of the account and primes the cache keys;
//   - a bare ban of a Google id or an address signs out the account that holds it;
//   - isIdentifierBlocked and signInRefusal see the new kinds, and finishSignIn refuses them;
//   - an unban (by the account, or by one entry of the list) clears the rows and the keys;
//   - the list shows a Google id by its last 4 and an address masked;
//   - the admin route:
//     - takes { user_id } for a browser-only account;
//     - refuses the admin's own account (SELF_BAN) and answers NOT_FOUND for no such account;
//     - unbans by an entry's id;
//   - the users list says Web for an account with no chat;
//   - adding a way (Add Google, Add email) refuses a banned Google account or address;
//   - no log line or Sentry report holds an identifier or a name, and user-moderation prints no argument object.
//
// Real: user-moderation, identities, web-session, add-google, the blocklist, user-overrides and Add email routes, the
// panel's reachLabel. Faked at the boundaries (scripts/lib/signin-world.ts): Prisma and Redis in memory, error capture,
// the chats, fetch (Resend recorded). No network, no DB.
//
// Run with the fake env of scripts/ci-smokes.sh:
//   bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-razielgershoni-development-famcalbot/0d239296-a217-49f9-8833-757c9d9a2df6/scratchpad/6c1/run-smoke.sh smoke-ban-web

  assert, baseUser, body, check, DB, everyCapture, everyLog, identityRow, initDataFor, installSigninWorld, load, logs, mails,

} from './lib/signin-world';

const ADMIN = 9;
const ADMIN_TG = 111111111;
const W = 50; // made on famcal.bot: a Google way and an email way, no chat
const T = 60; // Telegram and WhatsApp, and an email way
const T_TG = 666000060;
const T_PHONE = '+972500000060';
const V = 70; // made on famcal.bot with an email code only
const Q = 80; // Telegram only; adds ways in Settings
const Q_TG = 800000080;
/** The identifiers and names of the run: none may reach a log line or a Sentry report. */
const VALUES = [
  'g-web-0050', 'web@example.com', 'web@gmail.com', String(T_TG), T_PHONE, 't@example.com', 'v@example.com', 'g-gone-0001',
  'gone@example.com', 'Gone@Example.com', 'g-fresh-0080', 'fresh@gmail.com', 'other@gmail.com', 'Wren', 'Vera', 'Quinn',
];

const read = (rel: string) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8');
const user = (id: number): Row => DB.user.find(u => u.id === id) as Row;
const blockedKeys = (): string[] => [...redisStore.keys()].filter(k => k.startsWith('blocked:')).sort();

function seed(): void {
  resetWorld();
  DB.user = [
    baseUser({ id: ADMIN, name: 'Admin', telegramId: BigInt(ADMIN_TG), isAdmin: true }),
    baseUser({ id: W, name: 'Wren' }),
    baseUser({ id: T, name: 'Tom', telegramId: BigInt(T_TG), whatsappPhone: T_PHONE, messagingPlatform: 'all' }),
    baseUser({ id: V, name: 'Vera' }),
    baseUser({ id: Q, name: 'Quinn', telegramId: BigInt(Q_TG) }),
  ];
  DB.signInIdentity = [
    identityRow({ userId: W, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-web-0050', address: 'web@gmail.com' }),
    identityRow({ userId: W, kind: 'email', subject: 'web@example.com', address: 'web@example.com' }),
    identityRow({ userId: T, kind: 'email', subject: 't@example.com', address: 't@example.com' }),

    return { status: res.status, body: await body(res) };
  };

  await check('#1 a ban by the database id of a browser-only account records its Google account and its sign-in address, one row each; its web sessions end; both cache keys are set; the log names the user and the kinds only', async () => {

    const rows = DB.blockedIdentifier;
    assert(rows.length === 2 && rows.some(r => r.googleSub === 'g-web-0050' && r.email === null) && rows.some(r => r.email === 'web@example.com' && r.googleSub === null), `rows ${show(rows)}`);
    assert(rows.every(r => r.telegramId === null && r.whatsappPhone === null && r.bannedBy === ADMIN && r.bannedReason === 'spam'), `rows ${show(rows)}`);
    assert(user(W).sessionsValidAfter instanceof Date && user(T).sessionsValidAfter === null && user(V).sessionsValidAfter === null, 'not only W was signed out');
    assert(show(blockedKeys()) === show(['blocked:google:g-web-0050', mailKey('web@example.com')].sort()), `keys ${show(blockedKeys())}`);
    assert(logs.includes(`[Moderation] Admin ${ADMIN} banned user ${W}: google, email`), `logs ${show(logs)}`);
  });

  await check('#2 a ban by the database id of a chat account records its Telegram id, WhatsApp number and address; a second ban updates the reason and adds no row', async () => {

    assert((await moderation.isIdentifierBlocked({ googleSub: 'g-other', email: 'other@example.com' })) === false, 'others');
    assert(show(blockedKeys()) === show(['blocked:google:g-web-0050', mailKey('web@example.com')].sort()), `primed ${show(blockedKeys())}`);
  });

    assert(asked.status === 200, `add ${asked.status} ${show(await body(asked))}`);
    const code = /\b(\d{6})\b/.exec(JSON.stringify(mails[mails.length - 1]?.body ?? {}))?.[1] ?? '';
    assert(code !== '', 'no code was mailed');
    const sentBefore = sent.length;

    assert(confirmed.status === 403 && (await body(confirmed)).error === 'blocked', `confirm ${confirmed.status} ${show(await body(confirmed))}`);
    assert(!DB.signInIdentity.some(i => i.userId === Q && i.kind === 'email') && sent.length === sentBefore, 'a banned address became a way, or a notice went out');
  });

  await check('#10 no log line or Sentry report of the run holds an identifier or a name, and user-moderation prints no argument object', () => {

}

main().catch(err => {
```

```ts
export async function banIdentifier(
  args: BlockArgs,
  adminId: number,
  reason: string | null
): Promise<void> {
  if (!args.telegramId && !args.whatsappPhone) {
    throw new Error('At least one of telegramId or whatsappPhone is required');
  }

  // Use upsert keyed by whichever identifier is present.
  // If the same admin tries to ban a tg+wa pair, write two rows (one per unique key).
  const ops: Promise<unknown>[] = [];

  if (args.telegramId) {
    const tg = BigInt(args.telegramId);
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.upsert({
      where: { telegramId: tg },
      update: { bannedBy: adminId, bannedReason: reason },
      create: { telegramId: tg, bannedBy: adminId, bannedReason: reason },
    }));
    ops.push(redis.set(REDIS_KEYS.blockedTelegramId(tg.toString()), '1', { ex: BLOCK_CACHE_TTL }));
  }

  if (args.whatsappPhone) {
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.upsert({
      where: { whatsappPhone: args.whatsappPhone },
      update: { bannedBy: adminId, bannedReason: reason },
      create: { whatsappPhone: args.whatsappPhone, bannedBy: adminId, bannedReason: reason },
    }));
    ops.push(redis.set(REDIS_KEYS.blockedWhatsAppPhone(args.whatsappPhone), '1', { ex: BLOCK_CACHE_TTL }));
  }

  // A ban ends the web sessions of the accounts it names (web sign-in spec §2.13): their sessionsValidAfter moves to
  // now, in the row every request already reads, so a live cookie is refused at its next request.
  const owners: Array<{ telegramId: bigint } | { whatsappPhone: string }> = [];
  if (args.telegramId) owners.push({ telegramId: BigInt(args.telegramId) });
  if (args.whatsappPhone) owners.push({ whatsappPhone: args.whatsappPhone });
  ops.push(prisma.user.updateMany({ where: { OR: owners }, data: { sessionsValidAfter: new Date() } }).then(({ count }) => {
    console.log(`[Moderation] Ban by admin ${adminId}: ${count} account(s) signed out on the web`);
  }));

  await Promise.all(ops);
  console.log(`[Moderation] Admin ${adminId} banned identifier`, args);
}

export async function unbanIdentifier(args: BlockArgs, adminId: number): Promise<void> {
  if (!args.telegramId && !args.whatsappPhone) {
    throw new Error('At least one of telegramId or whatsappPhone is required');
  }

  const ops: Promise<unknown>[] = [];

  if (args.telegramId) {
    const tg = BigInt(args.telegramId);
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.deleteMany({ where: { telegramId: tg } }));
    ops.push(redis.del(REDIS_KEYS.blockedTelegramId(tg.toString())));
  }

  if (args.whatsappPhone) {
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.deleteMany({ where: { whatsappPhone: args.whatsappPhone } }));
    ops.push(redis.del(REDIS_KEYS.blockedWhatsAppPhone(args.whatsappPhone)));
  }

  await Promise.all(ops);
  console.log(`[Moderation] Admin ${adminId} unbanned identifier`, args);
}

export async function listBlockedIdentifiers(): Promise<Array<{
  id: number;
  telegramId: number | null;
  whatsappPhone: string | null;
  bannedBy: number;
  bannedReason: string | null;
  createdAt: Date;
}>> {
  const rows = await prisma.blockedIdentifier.findMany({
    orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },
  });
  return rows.map(r => ({
    id: r.id,
    telegramId: r.telegramId !== null ? Number(r.telegramId) : null,
    whatsappPhone: r.whatsappPhone,
    bannedBy: r.bannedBy,
    bannedReason: r.bannedReason,
    createdAt: r.createdAt,
  }));
}
```

After:

```ts
/** What a blocklist entry blocks. */
export type BlockKind = 'telegram' | 'whatsapp' | 'google' | 'email';

/** A ban or unban the admin can't do: no such account or entry, or nothing to block. Its message names no identifier. */
export class BanTargetError extends Error {
  constructor(readonly code: 'NOT_FOUND' | 'NO_IDENTIFIER') {
    super(`ban target: ${code}`);
    this.name = 'BanTargetError';
  }
}

/** The kinds given, in this order. */
function kindsOf(args: BlockArgs): BlockKind[] {
  const kinds: BlockKind[] = [];
  if (args.telegramId) kinds.push('telegram');
  if (args.whatsappPhone) kinds.push('whatsapp');
  if (args.googleSub) kinds.push('google');
  if (args.email) kinds.push('email');
  return kinds;
}

/**
 * Everything an account signs in with: its Telegram id, its WhatsApp number, and its Google account id and sign-in
 * address (accountWays). The blocklist holds no BSUID, as before.
 */
async function identifiersOf(userId: number): Promise<BlockArgs> {
  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId }, select: { telegramId: true, whatsappPhone: true } });
  if (!user) throw new BanTargetError('NOT_FOUND');
  const { accountWays } = await import('../services/web-signin/identities');
  const ways = await accountWays(userId);
  return { telegramId: user.telegramId, whatsappPhone: user.whatsappPhone, googleSub: ways.googleSub, email: ways.email };
}

/**
 * Ban, so none of it can sign up or sign in again (web sign-up spec §2.8, §3.8).
 * - `{ userId }` (the admin panel, any account, a browser-only one included) reads the account's identifiers and records
 *   each one. A bare BlockArgs records what it names.
 * - One row per identifier, each column unique, so a second ban of the same one updates its reason.
 * - Every account that holds one of them is signed out on the web (web sign-in spec §2.13): sessionsValidAfter moves to
 *   now, in the row every request already reads, so a live cookie is refused at its next request.
 * - The cache keys are primed for an hour.
 * The log names the account (or "identifiers") and the kinds, never a value.
 */
export async function banIdentifier(
  target: { userId: number } | BlockArgs,
  adminId: number,
  reason: string | null
): Promise<{ kinds: BlockKind[] }> {
  const accountId = 'userId' in target ? target.userId : null;
  const args = accountId !== null ? await identifiersOf(accountId) : (target as BlockArgs);
  const kinds = kindsOf(args);
  if (kinds.length === 0) throw new BanTargetError('NO_IDENTIFIER');

  const record = { bannedBy: adminId, bannedReason: reason };
  const ops: Promise<unknown>[] = [];
  if (args.telegramId) {
    const telegramId = BigInt(args.telegramId);
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.upsert({ where: { telegramId }, update: record, create: { telegramId, ...record } }));
  }
  if (args.whatsappPhone) {
    const whatsappPhone = args.whatsappPhone;
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.upsert({ where: { whatsappPhone }, update: record, create: { whatsappPhone, ...record } }));
  }
  if (args.googleSub) {
    const googleSub = args.googleSub;
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.upsert({ where: { googleSub }, update: record, create: { googleSub, ...record } }));
  }
  if (args.email) {
    const email = args.email;
    ops.push(prisma.blockedIdentifier.upsert({ where: { email }, update: record, create: { email, ...record } }));
  }
  for (const key of blockCacheKeys(args)) ops.push(redis.set(key, '1', { ex: BLOCK_CACHE_TTL }));

  const owners: Prisma.UserWhereInput[] = [];
  if (accountId !== null) owners.push({ id: accountId });
  if (args.telegramId) owners.push({ telegramId: BigInt(args.telegramId) });
  if (args.whatsappPhone) owners.push({ whatsappPhone: args.whatsappPhone });
  if (accountId === null && (args.googleSub || args.email)) {
    const { accountsHoldingWays } = await import('../services/web-signin/identities');
    const holders = await accountsHoldingWays({ googleSub: args.googleSub, email: args.email });
    if (holders.length > 0) owners.push({ id: { in: holders } });
  }
  if (owners.length > 0) {
    ops.push(prisma.user.updateMany({ where: { OR: owners }, data: { sessionsValidAfter: new Date() } }).then(({ count }) => {
      console.log(`[Moderation] Ban by admin ${adminId}: ${count} account(s) signed out on the web`);
    }));
  }

  await Promise.all(ops);
  console.log(`[Moderation] Admin ${adminId} banned ${accountId !== null ? `user ${accountId}` : 'identifiers'}: ${kinds.join(', ')}`);
  return { kinds };
}

/**
 * Unban: one entry of the list by its id (the panel, which shows a Google account and an address masked), every
 * identifier an account has (`{ userId }`), or what a bare BlockArgs names. The rows and their cache keys go. The log
 * names the entry or the account and the kinds, never a value.
 */
export async function unbanIdentifier(
  target: BlockArgs | { userId: number } | { entryId: number },
  adminId: number
): Promise<{ kinds: BlockKind[] }> {
  let args: BlockArgs;
  let who: string;
  if ('entryId' in target) {
    const row = await prisma.blockedIdentifier.findUnique({ where: { id: target.entryId } });
    if (!row) throw new BanTargetError('NOT_FOUND');
    args = argsOfRow(row);
    who = `entry ${row.id}`;
  } else if ('userId' in target) {
    args = await identifiersOf(target.userId);
    who = `user ${target.userId}`;
  } else {
    args = target;
    who = 'identifiers';
  }
  const kinds = kindsOf(args);
  if (kinds.length === 0) throw new BanTargetError('NO_IDENTIFIER');

  const keys = blockCacheKeys(args);
  await Promise.all([
    prisma.blockedIdentifier.deleteMany({ where: { OR: blockFilters(args) } }),
    ...(keys.length > 0 ? [redis.del(...keys)] : []),
  ]);
  console.log(`[Moderation] Admin ${adminId} unbanned ${who}: ${kinds.join(', ')}`);
  return { kinds };
}

/** One entry of the admin's blocked list. */
export interface BlockedEntry {
  id: number;
  kind: BlockKind;
  /** The Telegram id and the WhatsApp number in full; a Google account by the last 4 of its id; an address masked (maskEmail) */
  shown: string;
  bannedBy: number;
  bannedReason: string | null;
  createdAt: Date;
}

/** What a row blocks, as the list shows it; null for a row with no identifier (none is ever written). */
function shownOf(row: BlockedIdentifier): { kind: BlockKind; shown: string } | null {
  if (row.telegramId !== null) return { kind: 'telegram', shown: row.telegramId.toString() };
  if (row.whatsappPhone) return { kind: 'whatsapp', shown: row.whatsappPhone };
  if (row.googleSub) return { kind: 'google', shown: `•••${row.googleSub.slice(-4)}` };
  if (row.email) return { kind: 'email', shown: maskEmail(row.email) };
  return null;
}

/** The blocked list, newest first. A Google account id and an address never leave the server whole. */
export async function listBlockedIdentifiers(): Promise<BlockedEntry[]> {
  const rows = await prisma.blockedIdentifier.findMany({ orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } });
  const entries: BlockedEntry[] = [];
  for (const row of rows) {
    const what = shownOf(row);
    if (!what) {
      console.warn(`[Moderation] Blocklist entry ${row.id} names no identifier; it is left out of the list`);
      continue;
    }
    entries.push({ id: row.id, ...what, bannedBy: row.bannedBy, bannedReason: row.bannedReason, createdAt: row.createdAt });
  }
  return entries;
}
```

```ts

/**
 * The accounts that sign in with this Google account or this (normalised) address: what a ban of a bare identifier
 * signs out (user-moderation.ts). At most one each, by the unique (kind, subject).
 */
export async function accountsHoldingWays(ways: { googleSub?: string | null; email?: string | null }): Promise<number[]> {
  const or: Array<{ kind: IdentityKind; subject: string }> = [];
  if (ways.googleSub) or.push({ kind: 'google', subject: ways.googleSub });
  if (ways.email) or.push({ kind: 'email', subject: ways.email });
  if (or.length === 0) return [];
  const rows = await prisma.signInIdentity.findMany({ where: { OR: or }, select: { userId: true } });
  return [...new Set(rows.map(r => r.userId))];
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Why this account may not sign in, or null: 'suspended' (checked first), or 'blocked' (its Telegram id or WhatsApp
 * number is on the blocklist). The one rule: finishSignIn uses it, and so do Add Google and the calendar match before
 * they attach a way or send a notice (they answer with finishSignIn, which refuses the same way). It throws when the
 * blocklist can't be read; callers inside finishSignIn are covered by its catch.
 */
export async function signInRefusal(user: SignInAccount): Promise<'suspended' | 'blocked' | null> {
  if (user.suspendedAt) return 'suspended';
  if (await isIdentifierBlocked({ telegramId: user.telegramId, whatsappPhone: user.whatsappPhone ?? null })) return 'blocked';
  return null;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Why this account may not sign in, or null: 'suspended' (checked first), or 'blocked' (its Telegram id, WhatsApp
 * number, Google account or sign-in address is on the blocklist; its ways are read by accountWays, identities.ts). The
 * one rule: finishSignIn uses it, and so do Add Google and the calendar match before they attach a way or send a
 * notice (they answer with finishSignIn, which refuses the same way). It throws when the blocklist or the ways can't be
 * read; callers inside finishSignIn are covered by its catch.
 */
export async function signInRefusal(user: SignInAccount): Promise<'suspended' | 'blocked' | null> {
  if (user.suspendedAt) return 'suspended';
  const { accountWays } = await import('../services/web-signin/identities');
  const ways = await accountWays(user.id);
  const banned = await isIdentifierBlocked({
    telegramId: user.telegramId,
    whatsappPhone: user.whatsappPhone ?? null,
    googleSub: ways.googleSub,
    email: ways.email,
  });
  return banned ? 'blocked' : null;
}
```

Before (`:59-84`):

```ts
/**
 * Google's callback for an 'add-google' flow (Task 4's handleOidcCallback has proved the token and cleared the flow
 * cookie): attach the Google account (sub, the verified address) to the account that made the link, send the notice,
 * and sign this browser in as that account. A sub another account holds is refused (status=taken), and so is a second
 * Google account (status=has-one). A suspended or banned account gets no way and no notice: signInRefusal answers
 * before anything is added, and finishSignIn shows the person its page. The same account adding the same Google account
 * again ('kept') is signed in without a second notice. The caller has checked the address is verified.
 */
export async function finishAddGoogle(flow: OidcFlow, claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<NextResponse> {
  const user = flow.userId ? await getUserById(flow.userId) : null;
  if (!user || !claims.email) {
    console.warn(`[signin] add-google: ${user ? `user ${user.id}: Google gave no address` : `the account that made the link is not there (${flow.userId ?? 'none'})`}`);
    return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'failed'));
  }
  const refusal = await signInRefusal(user);
  if (refusal) {
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google refused: the account is ${refusal}`);
    return finishSignIn(user, 'google');
  }
  const added = await addIdentity(user.id, 'google', claims.sub, claims.email, { usedNow: true });
```

After:

```ts
/**
 * Google's callback for an 'add-google' flow (Task 4's handleOidcCallback has proved the token and cleared the flow
 * cookie): attach the Google account (sub, the verified address) to the account that made the link, send the notice,
 * and sign this browser in as that account.
 * - A sub another account holds is refused (status=taken), and so is a second Google account (status=has-one).
 * - A suspended or banned account gets no way and no notice: signInRefusal answers before anything is added, and
 *   finishSignIn shows the person its page.
 * - A Google account, or a verified address, on the blocklist is not added either (status=blocked; web sign-up spec
 *   §2.8: adding a way checks it).
 * - The same account adding the same Google account again ('kept') is signed in without a second notice.
 * The caller has checked the address is verified.
 */
export async function finishAddGoogle(flow: OidcFlow, claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<NextResponse> {
  const user = flow.userId ? await getUserById(flow.userId) : null;
  if (!user || !claims.email) {
    console.warn(`[signin] add-google: ${user ? `user ${user.id}: Google gave no address` : `the account that made the link is not there (${flow.userId ?? 'none'})`}`);
    return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'failed'));
  }
  const refusal = await signInRefusal(user);
  if (refusal) {
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google refused: the account is ${refusal}`);
    return finishSignIn(user, 'google');
  }
  if (await isIdentifierBlocked({ googleSub: claims.sub, email: normalizeEmail(claims.email) })) {
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google refused: the Google account or its address is on the blocklist`);
    return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'blocked'));
  }
  const added = await addIdentity(user.id, 'google', claims.sub, claims.email, { usedNow: true });
```

```ts
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'blocked' }, 403);
    }
    const added = await addIdentity(user.id, 'email', result.address, result.address);
```
