- [ ] **Step 2.7: The admin route (`app/api/admin/users/blocklist/route.ts`, whole file)**

```ts
/**
 * Admin Identifier Blocklist API (web sign-up spec §2.8, §3.8)
 * GET: every blocked identifier, as the list shows it: { id, kind, shown, bannedBy, bannedReason, createdAt } (a Google
 *   account by the last 4 of its id, an address masked; never the whole id or address).
 * POST { action: 'ban', user_id, reason? }: blocks everything that account signs in with (its Telegram id, WhatsApp
 *   number, Google account and sign-in address; a browser-only account included) → { success, kinds }.
 * POST { action: 'ban', telegramId?, whatsappPhone?, reason? }: a bare Telegram id or WhatsApp number, as before.
 * POST { action: 'unban', entryId } (one entry of the list), or { user_id }, or a bare telegramId / whatsappPhone.
 * A ban of the acting admin's own account, Telegram id or WhatsApp number answers 400 { error: 'SELF_BAN' }, as the
 * moderation route refuses an admin's own account. No such account or entry: 404 { error: 'NOT_FOUND' }; an account
 * with nothing to block: 400 { error: 'NO_IDENTIFIER' }.
 *
 * The blocklist persists independently of User rows, so a banned identifier cannot sign up again, even after a hard
 * delete.
 */

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { prisma } from '@/src/utils/prisma';
import { verifyAdminAccess } from '@/src/lib/admin-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { banIdentifier, unbanIdentifier, listBlockedIdentifiers, BanTargetError } from '@/src/lib/user-moderation';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

/** A database id the body names (user_id, entryId), or null. */
const positiveId = (value: unknown): number | null => (typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value > 0 ? value : null);

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  try {
    const initData = requestInitData(request);
    const auth = await verifyAdminAccess(initData);
    if (!auth.authorized) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { error: auth.error },
        { status: auth.error === 'Admin access required' ? 403 : 401 }
      );
    }

    const blocklist = await listBlockedIdentifiers();
    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, blocklist });
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'admin-users-blocklist-get', { api_route: '/api/admin/users/blocklist' });
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to fetch blocklist' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  try {
    const body = await request.json();
    const { initData, action, telegramId, whatsappPhone, reason } = body;

    const auth = await verifyAdminAccess(initData);
    if (!auth.authorized) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { error: auth.error },
        { status: auth.error === 'Admin access required' ? 403 : 401 }
      );
    }

    const userId = positiveId(body.user_id);
    const entryId = positiveId(body.entryId);
    const tgId: number | null = typeof telegramId === 'number' ? telegramId
      : typeof telegramId === 'string' && telegramId.trim() ? Number(telegramId)
      : null;
    const phone: string | null = typeof whatsappPhone === 'string' && whatsappPhone.trim() ? whatsappPhone.trim() : null;

    if (tgId !== null && Number.isNaN(tgId)) {
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'telegramId must be a number' }, { status: 400 });
    }
    if (userId === null && entryId === null && !tgId && !phone) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { error: 'An account (user_id), an entry (entryId), or a telegramId or whatsappPhone is required' },
        { status: 400 }
      );
    }

    switch (action) {
      case 'ban': {
        if (userId !== null) {
          if (userId === auth.adminId) {
            return NextResponse.json({ error: 'SELF_BAN' }, { status: 400 });
          }
          const { kinds } = await banIdentifier({ userId }, auth.adminId!, reason ?? null);
          return NextResponse.json({ success: true, message: 'Account banned', kinds });
        }
        if (!tgId && !phone) {
          return NextResponse.json({ error: 'A ban takes user_id, or a telegramId or whatsappPhone' }, { status: 400 });
        }
        const own = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: auth.adminId! }, select: { telegramId: true, whatsappPhone: true } });
        const digits = (value: string) => value.replace(/\D/g, '');
        const banningSelf =
          (tgId !== null && own?.telegramId != null && String(own.telegramId) === String(tgId)) ||
          (phone !== null && own?.whatsappPhone != null && digits(own.whatsappPhone) === digits(phone));
        if (banningSelf) {
          return NextResponse.json({ error: 'SELF_BAN' }, { status: 400 });
        }
        const { kinds } = await banIdentifier({ telegramId: tgId, whatsappPhone: phone }, auth.adminId!, reason ?? null);
        return NextResponse.json({ success: true, message: 'Identifier banned', kinds });
      }
      case 'unban': {
        const target = entryId !== null ? { entryId } : userId !== null ? { userId } : { telegramId: tgId, whatsappPhone: phone };
        const { kinds } = await unbanIdentifier(target, auth.adminId!);
        return NextResponse.json({ success: true, message: 'Identifier unbanned', kinds });
      }
      default:
        return NextResponse.json({ error: 'action must be "ban" or "unban"' }, { status: 400 });
    }
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof BanTargetError) {
      console.warn(`[admin-blocklist] refused: ${error.code}`);
      return NextResponse.json({ error: error.code }, { status: error.code === 'NOT_FOUND' ? 404 : 400 });
    }
    captureError(error, 'admin-users-blocklist-post', { api_route: '/api/admin/users/blocklist' });
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to update blocklist' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

`app/[locale]/(app)/admin-panel/data/use-blocklist.ts` (whole file):

```ts
'use client';

// The blocklist: Telegram ids, WhatsApp numbers, Google accounts and sign-in emails that cannot sign up again (GET
// users/blocklist; it survives a delete of the person; a Google account and an email come masked). `load` asks for the
// whole list. `unban` takes one entry off by its id (POST users/blocklist, action unban, entryId), reloads the list when
// it worked, and answers an Outcome the screen words; one unban runs at a time (`unbanning` is its entry's id).

import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { adminGet, adminPost, BUSY, outcomeOf, type Outcome } from './admin-api';
import type { BlocklistAnswer, BlocklistEntry } from './types';
import type { LoadStatus } from './use-users';

export function useBlocklist() {
  const [entries, setEntries] = useState<BlocklistEntry[]>([]);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<LoadStatus>('idle');
  const [unbanning, setUnbanning] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const latest = useRef(0);
  const running = useRef(false);
  useEffect(
    () => () => {
      latest.current++;
    },
    [],
  );

  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    const mine = ++latest.current;
    setStatus((s) => (s === 'ready' ? s : 'loading'));
    const result = await adminGet<BlocklistAnswer>('users/blocklist');
    if (mine !== latest.current) return;
    if (result.ok) {
      setEntries(result.data.blocklist ?? []);
      setStatus('ready');
    } else {
      setStatus((s) => (s === 'ready' ? s : 'failed'));
    }
  }, []);

  const unban = useCallback(
    async (entry: BlocklistEntry): Promise<Outcome> => {
      if (running.current) return BUSY;
      running.current = true;
      setUnbanning(entry.id);
      try {
        const outcome = outcomeOf(await adminPost('users/blocklist', { action: 'unban', entryId: entry.id }));
        if (outcome.ok) await load();
        return outcome;
      } finally {
        running.current = false;
        setUnbanning(null);
      }
    },
    [load],
  );

  return { entries, status, unbanning, load, unban };
}
```

`app/[locale]/(app)/admin-panel/views/BlockedView.tsx` (whole file):

```tsx
'use client';

// The blocked: Telegram ids, WhatsApp numbers, Google accounts and sign-in emails that cannot sign up again (plan
// docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-app-ui-A-admin-panel.md, Design > Blocked; web sign-up spec §2.8). A row is the entry as the
// server shows it (always left to right: the id or number in full, a Google account by the last 4 of its id, an email masked),
// what kind it is and why; a tap opens a sheet with the reason and the date and one button, Unblock, which works at once. A
// failure is said in the sheet, which stays; success closes it and the list says so. (Blocking someone is done from their profile.)

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useLocale, useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Notice } from '@/components/app-ui/Notice';
import { ScreenHeader } from '@/components/app-ui/ScreenHeader';
import { FormCard } from '@/components/app-ui/form-kit';
import { ListRow } from '@/components/app-ui/ListRow';
import { isBusy } from '../data/admin-api';
import { dateTime24 } from '../data/format';
import type { BlocklistEntry } from '../data/types';
import type { useBlocklist } from '../data/use-blocklist';
import { ConfirmSheet } from '../sheets';
import { LoadFailed, Waiting } from './parts';

/** The word for each kind of entry (admin.blocked.*). */
const KIND_LABEL = { telegram: 'blocked.telegram', whatsapp: 'blocked.whatsapp', google: 'blocked.google', email: 'blocked.email' } as const;

export function BlockedView({ blocklist, onBack }: { blocklist: ReturnType<typeof useBlocklist>; onBack: () => void }) {
  const t = useTranslations('admin');
  const ui = useTranslations('ui');
  const locale = useLocale();
  const { load, unban } = blocklist;
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<BlocklistEntry | null>(null);
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(false);
  const [done, setDone] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    void load();
  }, [load]);

  const kind = (entry: BlocklistEntry) => t(KIND_LABEL[entry.kind]);
  const reasonOf = (entry: BlocklistEntry) => entry.bannedReason?.trim() || t('blocked.reasonNone');
  const working = open !== null && blocklist.unbanning === open.id;

  const close = () => {
    if (working) return;
    setOpen(null);
    setFailed(false);
  };
  const confirm = async () => {
    if (!open) return;
    setFailed(false);
    const outcome = await unban(open);
    if (outcome.ok) {
      setOpen(null);
      setDone(true);
    } else if (!isBusy(outcome)) {
      setFailed(true);
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
      <ScreenHeader title={t('blocked.title')} backLabel={ui('back')} onBack={onBack} />
      <div className="ch-form-page ch-form-page-grouped">
        {done ? <Notice>{t('blocked.unblocked')}</Notice> : null}
        <p className="ch-form-fixed">{t('blocked.intro')}</p>
        {blocklist.status === 'failed' ? <LoadFailed onRetry={() => void load()} /> : null}
        {blocklist.status === 'loading' ? <Waiting /> : null}
        {blocklist.status === 'ready' && blocklist.entries.length === 0 ? <p className="ch-form-fixed">{t('blocked.empty')}</p> : null}
        {blocklist.entries.length > 0 ? (
          <FormCard>
            {blocklist.entries.map((entry) => (
              <ListRow
                key={entry.id}
                title={<bdi dir="ltr">{entry.shown}</bdi>}
                meta={
                  <>
                    <span className="ch-admin-line">{kind(entry)}</span>
                    <span className="ch-admin-line ch-admin-clamp">
                      <bdi dir="auto">{reasonOf(entry)}</bdi>
                    </span>
                  </>
                }
                onClick={() => {
                  setDone(false);
                  setFailed(false);
                  setOpen(entry);
                }}
              />
            ))}
          </FormCard>
        ) : null}
      </div>

      {open ? (
        <ConfirmSheet
          title={open.shown}
          body={kind(open)}
          confirmLabel={t('blocked.unblock')}
          cancelLabel={ui('cancel')}
          working={working}
          error={failed ? t('errors.unban') : null}
          onConfirm={() => void confirm()}
          onClose={close}
        >
          <p className="ch-admin-text" dir="auto">
            {reasonOf(open)}
          </p>
          <p className="ch-form-fixed">{t('blocked.blockedOn', { date: dateTime24(open.createdAt, locale) })}</p>
        </ConfirmSheet>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

`app/[locale]/(app)/admin-panel/views/profile/Account.tsx` (whole file):

```tsx
'use client';

// What an admin can do to the account itself (plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-app-ui-A-admin-panel.md, Design > User profile 7),
// last on the page and none of it without asking:
// - Suspend (optional reason, asks first), or Unsuspend (it works at once and says so);
// - Block everything they sign in with, so they cannot sign up again (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.8): a sheet that names the
//   Telegram id and WhatsApp number they have (the body says their Google account and email go too; the server reads all of them by
//   the database id), a reason, a confirm. It shows for every account but the viewer's own, a browser-only one included;
// - Delete for good: a sheet in which the person types DELETE, which is what the server requires (so it is Latin in every language).
//   While it works nothing closes the sheet. When it is done the profile is gone and the panel goes back to the people list, which says
//   whose account was deleted.
// The viewer's own account offers none of these (the routes refuse them), and says so.

import { useState } from 'react';
import { useLocale, useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { FormCard, FormRow, TextField } from '@/components/app-ui/form-kit';
import { Notice } from '@/components/app-ui/Notice';
import { SectionLabel } from '@/components/app-ui/ScreenHeader';
import { isBusy } from '../../data/admin-api';
import { dateTime24 } from '../../data/format';
import { ActionSheet, failureText, type Message, type SectionProps } from './shared';

/** The word the route requires before it deletes a person. */
const CONFIRMATION = 'DELETE';
/** A Latin id or number inside a Hebrew line keeps its own order. */
const isolate = (text: string) => `⁦${text}⁩`;

export function Account({ person, profile, isSelf, onDeleted }: SectionProps & { onDeleted: (name: string) => void }) {
  const t = useTranslations('admin');
  const locale = useLocale();
  const [sheet, setSheet] = useState<'suspend' | 'block' | 'delete' | null>(null);
  const [reason, setReason] = useState('');
  const [typed, setTyped] = useState('');
  const [message, setMessage] = useState<Message | null>(null);

  const open = (which: 'suspend' | 'block' | 'delete') => {
    setMessage(null);
    setReason('');
    setTyped('');
    setSheet(which);
  };
  const close = () => setSheet(null);
  const done = (text: string) => {
    setSheet(null);
    setMessage({ tone: 'info', text });
  };

  const unsuspend = async () => {
    setMessage(null);
    const outcome = await profile.unsuspend();
    if (outcome.ok) setMessage({ tone: 'info', text: t('profile.account.unsuspended', { name: person.name }) });
    else if (!isBusy(outcome)) setMessage({ tone: 'error', text: failureText(t as unknown as (key: string) => string, 'unsuspend', outcome) });
  };

  return (
    <>
      <SectionLabel>{t('profile.account.title')}</SectionLabel>
      {isSelf ? (
        <Notice>{t('profile.self')}</Notice>
      ) : (
        <FormCard>
          {person.suspendedAt ? (
            <>
              <div className="ch-form-row">
                <span className="ch-form-label">
                  <span>{t('profile.account.suspendedOn', { date: dateTime24(person.suspendedAt, locale) })}</span>
                  {person.suspendedReason ? (
                    <span className="ch-form-hint" dir="auto">
                      {t('profile.account.suspendedReason', { reason: person.suspendedReason })}
                    </span>
                  ) : null}
                </span>
              </div>
              <button type="button" className="ch-form-row ch-action-row" disabled={profile.working !== null} aria-busy={profile.working === 'unsuspend' || undefined} onClick={() => void unsuspend()}>
                <span className="ch-form-label">{t('profile.account.unsuspend')}</span>
                {profile.working === 'unsuspend' ? <span className="ch-form-spinner" aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
              </button>
            </>
          ) : (
            <button type="button" className="ch-form-row ch-action-row" aria-haspopup="dialog" onClick={() => open('suspend')}>
              <span className="ch-form-label">{t('profile.account.suspend')}</span>
            </button>
          )}
          <button type="button" className="ch-form-row ch-action-row" aria-haspopup="dialog" onClick={() => open('block')}>
            <span className="ch-form-label">{t('profile.account.block')}</span>
          </button>
          <button type="button" className="ch-form-row ch-danger-row" aria-haspopup="dialog" onClick={() => open('delete')}>
            {t('profile.account.delete')}
          </button>
        </FormCard>
      )}
      {message ? <Notice tone={message.tone}>{message.text}</Notice> : null}

      {sheet === 'suspend' ? (
        <ActionSheet
          action="suspend"
          title={t('profile.account.suspendTitle', { name: person.name })}
          body={t('profile.account.suspendBody')}
          confirmLabel={t('profile.account.suspendConfirm')}
          tone="danger"
          run={() => profile.suspend(reason)}
          onDone={() => done(t('profile.account.suspended', { name: person.name }))}
          onClose={close}
        >
          <FormCard>
            <TextField label={t('profile.account.reason')} placeholder={t('profile.account.reason')} value={reason} onChange={setReason} />
          </FormCard>
        </ActionSheet>
      ) : null}
      {sheet === 'block' ? (
        <ActionSheet
          action="ban"
          title={t('profile.account.blockTitle', { name: person.name })}
          body={t('profile.account.blockBody')}
          confirmLabel={t('profile.account.blockConfirm')}
          tone="danger"
          run={() => profile.ban(reason)}
          onDone={() => done(t('profile.account.blockedDone'))}
          onClose={close}
        >
          <FormCard>
            {person.telegramId !== null ? <FormRow label={t('profile.account.blockTelegram')} hint={isolate(String(person.telegramId))} /> : null}
            {person.whatsappPhone ? <FormRow label={t('profile.account.blockWhatsapp')} hint={isolate(person.whatsappPhone)} /> : null}
            <TextField label={t('profile.account.reason')} placeholder={t('profile.account.reason')} value={reason} onChange={setReason} />
          </FormCard>
        </ActionSheet>
      ) : null}
      {sheet === 'delete' ? (
        <ActionSheet
          action="hardDelete"
          title={t('profile.account.deleteTitle', { name: person.name })}
          body={t('profile.account.deleteBody')}
          confirmLabel={t('profile.account.deleteConfirm')}
          tone="danger"
          confirmDisabled={typed !== CONFIRMATION}
          run={() => profile.hardDelete(typed)}
          onDone={() => onDeleted(person.name)}
          onClose={close}
        >
          <p className="ch-form-fixed">{t('profile.account.deleteType')}</p>
          <FormCard>
            <TextField label={t('profile.account.deleteType')} placeholder={CONFIRMATION} value={typed} onChange={setTyped} />
          </FormCard>
        </ActionSheet>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

```ts
    // No person open: an action sends nothing
    await both.run((x) => x.profile.clear());
    reset();
    const none = await both.run((x) => x.profile.suspend(''));
    assert(!none.ok && none.code === 'NO_TARGET' && sent() === 0, `no person: ${canon(none)}`);
    both.unmount();

    // A browser-only person (no Telegram id, no WhatsApp number) is blocked by their database id like anyone else
    reset();

      const url = new URL(call.url, 'http://localhost');
      return url.pathname.endsWith('user-overrides') && url.searchParams.has('user_id') ? ok({ user: { ...detail(TARGET), telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null } }) : defaultRespond(call);
    };
    await openProfile(solo);
    reset();

    assert(web.ok, `a ban of a browser-only person: ${canon(web)}`);
    expectCall(calls[0], 'POST', '/api/admin/users/blocklist', { action: 'ban', user_id: TARGET, reason: null }, 'a ban of a browser-only person');
    solo.unmount();
```

## Part B: Task 3 (Turnstile) and Task 4 (the sign-up code and the email budget)

### Task 3: Turnstile on the email-code form

#### Notes for Tasks 3–4 (read first)

Code read at main `edd9d72e`; a file:line below is from that commit. `$RUN` (the header's runner) does not blank the two Turnstile names by itself, so every smoke below that reads them sets or deletes them itself. `bash scripts/ci-smokes.sh` globs `scripts/smoke-*.ts`, so new smoke files need no registration.

1. **String key.** `site.signin.email.check` can't exist, because `site.signin.email` is already a string ("Email me a code", `messages/en.json:1824`). The key is **`site.signin.emailCheck`**. The other new client strings sit beside it: `site.signin.turnstileWaiting`, `turnstileProblem`, `turnstileRetry` (Task 3), and `emailSentOpen` (Task 4).
2. **`takeSignUpSend` doesn't call `takeDailySend()`.** `issueCode` already takes from the 90 for every code (`email-code.ts:64`), so calling it here too would count each sign-up code twice. A sign-up code still counts inside the 90, through `issueCode`. `takeSignUpSend` counts only its own two shares: 3 per client address, then 30 a day.
3. **`'store-down'` in the return types.** `takeSignUpSend`, `takeNoticeSend` and `allowNewAccount` can also answer `{ ok: false, reason: 'store-down' }`. A Redis failure fails closed and is reported, like every 6b limit (`limits.ts:147-150`). Callers treat any `!ok` as a refusal (Task 5's `completeSignUp` included).
4. **Turnstile gets the client's real address.** `clientAddress` gives an IPv6 address as its /64 (`a:b:c:d::/64`), which isn't an address, so it can't be Turnstile's `remoteip`. Task 3 adds **`clientIp(request): string | null`** in `client-address.ts`. It reads the same `x-real-ip` header as it came, checked with `isIP`. `verifyTurnstile(token, ip)` sends `remoteip` only when `ip` is an address.
5. **Task 4 owns the sign-up flow's shared pieces (rulings #2, #3).** Step 8 writes, once: `SignUpFlow` (with its doc and `startedAt?: number`, which `startFlow` stores on every flow) and its place in the `SignInFlow` union; the `signup` branch of `asFlow`; `src/lib/invite-token.ts` with `cleanInviteToken` (client-safe, no import: the invite page and `/signin` need it, and `flow.ts` is server-only); the exported `inviteOf` in `flow.ts`, the one reader of `invite` from a stored record; `signUpHref` in `src/site/signin.ts`; and `signUpPageUrl` in `web-session.ts`, built from `signUpHref`. Why: one definition, so Task 5's and Task 11's edits build on it instead of adding a second. Task 5 then adds only the `peekFlow` overloads, `invite?` on `OidcFlow` and `EmailFlow` (read with `...inviteOf(v)`), `SIGNUP_NAME_MAX`, `SignUpWays` and `signUpWays`. **Task 11 Step 8 adds `...(flow.invite ? { invite: flow.invite } : {})` to the `startFlow` call in `signUpNext` (verify route, Task 4 Step 10)**, so an invite survives the email sign-up.
6. **The `/signup` redirect is absolute.** `signUpPageUrl(locale)` gives `https://famcal.bot/<locale>/signup` with the prefix even for English. That prefix rule is `prefixed`'s (`web-session.ts:36-46`): it pins next-intl's locale cookie. Task 5's Google callback redirects through the same helper.
7. **The Turnstile names land in Task 3, not Task 14.** `smoke-signin-setup` checks four things together: the names in `SIGN_IN_ENV`, a README row for each, an `.env.example` placeholder for each, and that the code reads each one. So Task 3 adds all four for `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` and `TURNSTILE_SECRET`, and the startup warning's wording ("web sign-up with an email code is off: …"). Task 14 then writes only the README's "Web sign-up" note.
8. **The verify route's `exists` answer is the route's only (ruling #6).** It is `{ ok: false, error: 'exists', way: 'google' }` (`way: 'email'` only in a race, because an account that signs in with the address is signed in first). Task 4 adds no words or branch for it in `SignInClient`: until Task 5 it falls to the form's `requestFailed` line, and Task 5 navigates to `/signin?status=exists-google` (or `exists-email`). Why: one owner of the client's answer; the route's answer is pinned by U7.
9. **The sign-up code is checked only when the address has no live sign-in code.** That covers the sign-in check answering `expired`, which includes an address with no account. So a wrong code for an account's address still counts one try, and `smoke-signin-email` #7 holds.
10. **The email flow is used once.** A right sign-up code takes the email flow (`takeFlow(['email'])`, a GETDEL) before the sign-up flow starts under a new cookie. A code entered in another browser (no `famcal_signin` cookie) answers `restart` before the code is touched, so the first browser can still use it (U11).
11. **Scrubbers, verified:**
    - Sentry already drops a body's `token` (`src/lib/sentry-scrub.ts:56`, `SECRET_BODY_FIELDS`) and a `token=` query value (`:53-54`).
    - The console scrub covers `TURNSTILE_SECRET` through `SECRET` in `SECRET_NAME` (`src/lib/console-scrub.ts:17`).
    - `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` doesn't match that pattern and isn't a secret: every page shows it.
12. **Sign-up email body ends with a colon.** It reads "Enter this code on famcal.bot to create your account:", because in the email layout the code comes right after the body, as the sign-in and Add email bodies do (`messages/en.json:2982`, `:2988`).
13. **`smoke-zmanim-pages` Z10.** That smoke forbids site files from loading scripts. It now names `components/site/TurnstileWidget.tsx` as the one site file that may create a `<script>` element (Cloudflare's, on a person's action).
14. **`takeNoticeSend(userId)` (ruling #16).** It takes the account's share first, 3 a UTC day (`REDIS_KEYS.signinLimit('notice-account-day', signinHash('account', String(userId)))`, alive to the next 00:00 UTC), then the day's 10 for everyone. It answers `{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'notice-account-day' | 'notice-budget' | 'store-down' }`, so Task 8's `sendNoticeEmail` can log the account's refusal as its SECURITY line with `(the account's notices are spent)` and the day's with its own wording. Why: spec §1, strangers (or one account repeating Add Google) can't use up the notices' budget.
15. **`request(url, { ip })` in `scripts/lib/signin-world.ts` is Task 3's (ruling #11).** Task 5 adds only `advanceRedis` and the Redis expiry clock.
16. **Sign-up codes with no `x-real-ip` share 6b's `none` key (ruling #24).** `takeSignUpSend(null)` counts as every 6b per-address limit does, so without the header all such sign-up codes together get 3 a day; the new-accounts cap skips the count instead (spec §2.6). Why: it matches 6b's sign-in codes, and the `x-real-ip` probe gates announcing sign-up.
17. **A banned address still gets a sign-up code**; Task 5's ban check refuses the sign-up itself. Checking `isIdentifierBlocked` before mailing would add a database query to every sign-up code.
18. **The sent line (ruling #6).** With a site key, an address on no account gets a code too, so the code screen says `emailSentOpen` ("Check your email for a 6-digit code…") for every address; 6b's `emailSent` ("If this email is on a FamCal account…") stays for the no-Turnstile case. Task 5 adds no sent line of its own.

```ts
      assert(siteverifyCalls.length === 0, `${show(on)}: Cloudflare was asked`);
    }
    configure({ siteKey: true, secret: true });
    assert(turnstile.turnstileConfigured() === true && turnstile.turnstileSiteKey() === SITE_KEY, 'both set');
    assert(turnstile.TURNSTILE_ACTION === 'email-code' && turnstile.SITEVERIFY_URL === 'https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify', 'the action or the endpoint');
  });

  await check('T2 a pass: one siteverify POST with the secret, the token, the client\'s own address (IPv6 whole; none without the header) and a UUID idempotency key; then the limits and { ok: true } with the flow', async () => {
    configure({ siteKey: true, secret: true });
    resetWorld();
    const r = await ask({ token: TOKEN });
    assert(r.status === 200 && show(r.body) === show({ ok: true }) && r.cookie, `${r.status} ${show(r.body)}`);
    assert(siteverifyCalls.length === 1, `calls ${siteverifyCalls.length}`);
    const form = siteverifyCalls[0].form;
    assert(form.get('secret') === SECRET && form.get('response') === TOKEN && form.get('remoteip') === '203.0.113.9', `the form's fields: ${show([...form.keys()])}`);
    assert(UUID.test(form.get('idempotency_key') ?? ''), 'no UUID idempotency key');
    assert(limitKeys().length > 0, 'the limits were not counted after the pass');
    resetWorld();
    await ask({ token: TOKEN }, { ip: '2001:db8:1:2::9' });
    assert(siteverifyCalls[0]?.form.get('remoteip') === '2001:db8:1:2::9', `IPv6: ${siteverifyCalls[0]?.form.get('remoteip')}`);
    resetWorld();
    const none = await ask({ token: TOKEN }, { ip: null });
    assert(none.body.ok === true && siteverifyCalls[0] && !siteverifyCalls[0].form.has('remoteip'), 'remoteip without an address');
  });

  await check('T3 every failure answers { ok: false, error: "check" } (403) with no flow cookie, before anything is counted, looked up or mailed; a token that is none, empty, not text or over 2048 characters asks Cloudflare nothing; a refused secret is reported', async () => {
    configure({ siteKey: true, secret: true });
    const four = <T>(x: T): T[] => [x, x, x, x];
    const cases: [string, unknown, (Row | number | string | Error)[], number][] = [
      ['no token', undefined, [], 0],
      ['an empty token', '', [], 0],
      ['a token that is not text', 12345, [], 0],
      ['a token over 2048 characters', 'x'.repeat(2049), [], 0],
      ['a refused token', TOKEN, [siteverifyAnswer({ success: false, 'error-codes': ['invalid-input-response'] })], 1],
      ['timeout-or-duplicate', TOKEN, [siteverifyAnswer({ success: false, 'error-codes': ['timeout-or-duplicate'] })], 1],
      ['another hostname', TOKEN, [siteverifyAnswer({ hostname: 'famcal.bot.evil.example' })], 1],
      ['another action', TOKEN, [siteverifyAnswer({ action: 'login' })], 1],
      ['no action', TOKEN, [siteverifyAnswer({ action: undefined })], 1],
      ['a 5xx to the end of the retries', TOKEN, four(503), 4],
      ['no answer to the end of the retries', TOKEN, four(new TypeError('fetch failed')), 4],
      ['an answer that is not JSON', TOKEN, four('{"success":tr'), 4],
      ['a 400 (not retried)', TOKEN, [400], 1],
      ['a secret Cloudflare refuses', TOKEN, [siteverifyAnswer({ success: false, 'error-codes': ['invalid-input-secret'] })], 1],
    ];
    const problems: string[] = [];
    for (const [label, token, answers, calls] of cases) {
      resetWorld();
      world.siteverify = [...answers];
      const r = await ask(token === undefined ? {} : { token });
      if (r.status !== 403 || show(r.body) !== show({ ok: false, error: 'check' }) || r.cookie !== null) problems.push(`${label}: ${r.status} ${show(r.body)} cookie ${r.cookie}`);
      if (siteverifyCalls.length !== calls) problems.push(`${label}: ${siteverifyCalls.length} siteverify calls, want ${calls}`);
      if (limitKeys().length !== 0) problems.push(`${label}: counted ${show(limitKeys())}`);
      await drainAfter();
      if (mails.length !== 0 || prismaCalls.length !== 0) problems.push(`${label}: mailed ${mails.length}, queried ${show(prismaCalls)}`);
      if (label === 'a secret Cloudflare refuses' && !captured.some((c) => c.context === 'turnstile')) problems.push(`${label}: not reported (${show(captured)})`);
    }
    assert(problems.length === 0, problems.join('; '));
  });

  await check('T4 a retry repeats the request\'s idempotency key and another request gets a new one; the hostname is the app\'s (getBaseUrl), so another base URL refuses famcal.bot\'s answer', async () => {
    configure({ siteKey: true, secret: true });
    resetWorld();
    world.siteverify = [503, siteverifyAnswer()];
    const r = await ask({ token: TOKEN });
    assert(r.body.ok === true, `after a 503 and a pass: ${show(r.body)}`);
    const [first, second] = siteverifyCalls.map((c) => c.form.get('idempotency_key'));
    assert(siteverifyCalls.length === 2 && first && UUID.test(first) && first === second, `the keys ${show([first, second])}`);
    await ask({ token: TOKEN });
    const third = siteverifyCalls[2]?.form.get('idempotency_key');
    assert(third && UUID.test(third) && third !== first, `another request's key ${third}`);
    // verifyTurnstile takes no request, so the hostname it wants can only be the app's
    resetWorld();
    assert(show(await turnstile.verifyTurnstile(TOKEN, null)) === show({ ok: true }), 'famcal.bot on famcal.bot');
    const base = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL;
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL = 'https://staging.famcal.bot';
    try {
      const other = await turnstile.verifyTurnstile(TOKEN, null);
      assert(show(other) === show({ ok: false, why: 'hostname' }), `famcal.bot's answer on staging: ${show(other)}`);
    } finally {
      process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL = base;
    }
  });

  await check('T5 no console line or error report holds the token or the secret; the Sentry scrubber drops a body\'s token; the console scrubber covers TURNSTILE_SECRET', async () => {
    const leakedLines = everyLog.filter((l) => l.includes(TOKEN) || l.includes(SECRET) || l.includes('XXXX.DUMMY'));
    assert(leakedLines.length === 0, `console lines: ${show(leakedLines)}`);
    const leakedReports = everyCapture.filter((c) => show(c).includes(TOKEN) || show(c).includes(SECRET));
    assert(leakedReports.length === 0, `error reports: ${show(leakedReports)}`);
    const { scrubServerEvent } = await load('src/lib/sentry-scrub.ts');
    for (const data of [JSON.stringify({ email: 'x@example.com', locale: 'en', token: TOKEN }), { email: 'x@example.com', locale: 'en', token: TOKEN }]) {
      const event = scrubServerEvent({ request: { url: `https://famcal.bot/api/auth/email/request?token=${TOKEN}`, data } });
      assert(!show(event).includes(TOKEN), `Sentry keeps the token: ${show(event)}`);
    }
    const { secretValues } = await load('src/lib/console-scrub.ts');
    assert(secretValues({ TURNSTILE_SECRET: SECRET, TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: SITE_KEY }).includes(SECRET), 'the console scrubber misses TURNSTILE_SECRET');
  });

  report();
}

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```ts
// 6c-1 Task 3 adds sign-up's two Turnstile variables, spec 2026-11-03-web-sign-up §6).

//    SIGN_IN_ENV holds the seven variables the sign-in code reads (oidc.ts, email-send.ts, turnstile.ts), and every

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
const read = (rel: string) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8');

type Result = { name: string; ok: boolean; reason?: string };
const results: Result[] = [];
async function check(name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) {
  try {
    await fn();
    results.push({ name, ok: true });
  } catch (err) {
    results.push({ name, ok: false, reason: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
  }
}
function assert(cond: unknown, message: string): asserts cond {

}
const show = (v: unknown) => JSON.stringify(v);

];

async function main() {
  await check('S1 signInSetupWarnings names each way that is off by its variables (email sign-up without Turnstile too), and a Google sign-in client that is the calendar\'s; never a value; SIGN_IN_ENV is the seven variables the sign-in code reads, and its secrets match the console scrubber', async () => {

    const all = {

      const line = example.find((l) => l.startsWith(`# ${name}=`));
      if (!line || !/^# [A-Z_]+=your_[a-z_]+_here$/.test(line)) problems.push(`.env.example has no commented placeholder for ${name}`);
      if (example.some((l) => l.startsWith(`${name}=`))) problems.push(`.env.example sets ${name} uncommented`);

    for (const url of ['https://famcal.bot/api/auth/telegram/callback', 'https://famcal.bot/api/auth/google/callback']) if (!readme.includes(url)) problems.push(`README does not name ${url}`);
    const rule = read('CLAUDE.md').split('\n').find((l) => l.startsWith('- Every web sign-in'));
    if (!rule) problems.push('CLAUDE.md has no "- Every web sign-in" rule');
    else for (const word of ['`finishSignIn`', ...SIGNIN_IDENTITY_FILES.map((f) => path.basename(f)), 'sessionsValidAfter', '`matchCalendarAccount`', '(never `sub`)']) if (!rule.includes(word)) problems.push(`the CLAUDE.md rule does not name ${word}`);
    // The rule's file list, held: no other file reads or writes SignInIdentity rows
    const walk = (dir: string): string[] =>
      fs.readdirSync(path.join(ROOT, dir), { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((e) => {
        const rel = `${dir}/${e.name}`;
        if (e.isDirectory()) return e.name === 'node_modules' ? [] : walk(rel);

  });

    if (!r.ok) failed++;
  }
  console.log(`\n${results.length - failed}/${results.length} passed`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error(err);

});
```

```ts
      for (const n of node) {
        const hit = propsOf(n, type);
        if (hit) return hit;
      }
      return null;
```

```ts
      assert(alerts(first).includes(en.turnstileProblem) && scripts().length === 0, `a script that did not load: ${show(alerts(first))}, ${scripts().length} scripts`);
      first.click(buttonByText(first, en.turnstileRetry) as FakeElement);
      await settle();
      assert(scripts().length === 1, 'Try again did not load the script again');
      fakeWindow.turnstile = fakeTurnstile;
      await act(async () => (scripts()[0] as unknown as Row).onload());
      await settle();
      assert(ts.widgets.length === 1 && !alerts(first).includes(en.turnstileProblem), `after the load: ${show(ts.calls)} ${show(alerts(first))}`);
    } finally {
      first.unmount();
    }
    assert(ts.calls.at(-1) === 'remove:w1', `not removed on unmount: ${show(ts.calls)}`);

    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      const s = S(locale);
      ts.calls.length = 0;
      ts.widgets.length = 0;
      const m = openClient(locale, { siteKey: SITE_KEY });
      try {
        m.click(way(m, 'email') as FakeElement);
        await settle();
        assert(scripts().length === 1, `${locale}: the script was loaded again`);
        const o = lastWidget()?.options ?? {};
        assert(ts.widgets.length === 1 && o.sitekey === SITE_KEY && o.action === 'email-code' && o.theme === 'auto' && o.language === locale && o.size === 'flexible', `${locale}: the widget ${show(ts.calls)} ${show(o)}`);
        for (const cb of ['callback', 'error-callback', 'expired-callback', 'timeout-callback']) assert(typeof o[cb] === 'function', `${locale}: no ${cb}`);
        const submit = () => way(m, 'submit') as FakeElement;
        m.input(inputOf(m), 'dana@gmail.com');
        assert(submit().hasAttribute('disabled') && flat(submit()) === s.turnstileWaiting, `${locale}: Send before the token: "${flat(submit())}"`);
        await act(async () => o.callback('tok-1'));
        assert(!submit().hasAttribute('disabled') && flat(submit()) === s.emailSend, `${locale}: Send after the token: "${flat(submit())}"`);

        // The server refuses the check: said, the widget reset, Send waits for the next token
        routes = { 'POST /api/auth/email/request': () => json({ ok: false, error: 'check' }, 403) };
        m.submit(formOf(m));
        await settle();
        assert(show(lastCall('/api/auth/email/request')?.body) === show({ email: 'dana@gmail.com', locale, token: 'tok-1' }), `${locale}: the request ${show(lastCall('/api/auth/email/request')?.body)}`);
        assert(alerts(m).includes(s.emailCheck) && ts.calls.includes('reset:w1') && submit().hasAttribute('disabled'), `${locale}: a refused check: ${show(alerts(m))} ${show(ts.calls)}`);

        // An expired token makes Send wait again
        await act(async () => o.callback('tok-2'));
        await act(async () => o['expired-callback']());
        assert(submit().hasAttribute('disabled'), `${locale}: Send with an expired token`);

        // An error and a timeout: said, with Try again, which renders a fresh widget
        await act(async () => o['error-callback']('300030'));
        assert(alerts(m).includes(s.turnstileProblem), `${locale}: an error: ${show(alerts(m))}`);
        m.click(buttonByText(m, s.turnstileRetry) as FakeElement);
        await settle();
        assert(ts.calls.includes('remove:w1') && lastWidget().id === 'w2' && !alerts(m).includes(s.turnstileProblem), `${locale}: Try again after an error: ${show(ts.calls)}`);
        await act(async () => lastWidget().options['timeout-callback']());
        assert(alerts(m).includes(s.turnstileProblem), `${locale}: a timeout: ${show(alerts(m))}`);
        m.click(buttonByText(m, s.turnstileRetry) as FakeElement);
        await settle();
        assert(lastWidget().id === 'w3', `${locale}: Try again after a timeout: ${show(ts.calls)}`);

        // A pass and a sent code: the email form's widget goes, and the code screen has its own, for Send a new code
        await act(async () => lastWidget().options.callback('tok-3'));
        routes = { 'POST /api/auth/email/request': () => json({ ok: true }) };
        m.submit(formOf(m));
        await settle();
        assert(lastCall('/api/auth/email/request')?.body?.token === 'tok-3', `${locale}: the second request ${show(lastCall('/api/auth/email/request')?.body)}`);
        assert(ts.calls.includes('reset:w3') && ts.calls.includes('remove:w3') && lastWidget().id === 'w4', `${locale}: after the code was sent: ${show(ts.calls)}`);
        assert((buttonByText(m, s.codeAgain) as FakeElement).hasAttribute('disabled'), `${locale}: Send a new code before its token`);
        await act(async () => lastWidget().options.callback('tok-4'));
        assert(!(buttonByText(m, s.codeAgain) as FakeElement).hasAttribute('disabled'), `${locale}: Send a new code after its token`);
        m.click(buttonByText(m, s.codeAgain) as FakeElement);
        await settle();
        assert(lastCall('/api/auth/email/request')?.body?.token === 'tok-4' && ts.calls.includes('reset:w4'), `${locale}: Send a new code: ${show(lastCall('/api/auth/email/request')?.body)} ${show(ts.calls)}`);
      } finally {
        m.unmount();
      }
      assert(ts.calls.at(-1) === `remove:${lastWidget().id}`, `${locale}: not removed on unmount: ${show(ts.calls)}`);
    }

    // No site key: no script, no widget, and Send waits for nothing
    const callsBefore = ts.calls.length;
    const scriptsBefore = scripts().length;
    const plain = openClient('en');
    try {
      plain.click(way(plain, 'email') as FakeElement);
      await settle();
      plain.input(inputOf(plain), 'dana@gmail.com');
      assert(ts.calls.length === callsBefore && scripts().length === scriptsBefore, `a widget without a site key: ${show(ts.calls.slice(callsBefore))}`);
      assert(!(way(plain, 'submit') as FakeElement).hasAttribute('disabled') && flat(way(plain, 'submit') as FakeElement) === en.emailSend, 'Send waits without a site key');
    } finally {
      plain.unmount();
    }
    const leaked = logs.filter((l) => /tok-\d/.test(l));
    assert(leaked.length === 0, `a log line holds a token: ${show(leaked)}`);
  });
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create `src/services/web-signin/turnstile.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * Cloudflare Turnstile on the email-code form (web sign-up spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md
 * §2.4, §3.1): the check that a person, not a program, asks for an email code, on every code request (sign-in and
 * sign-up alike, so the answer still says nothing about an address).
 *
 * - On only when both TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and TURNSTILE_SECRET are set; until then the form shows no widget, the request
 *   route checks nothing, and email sign-up stays off (no sign-up code is mailed: the request route's after()).
 * - verifyTurnstile posts the token to siteverify (secret, response, remoteip when known, an idempotency_key) through the
 *   one retry loop (fetch-retry.ts's fetchAndReadWithRetry, the body read whole inside the attempt with wholeJson). A
 *   POST is safe to send again here because of the idempotency key: Cloudflare answers a repeat of the same key as it
 *   answered the first, so a retry after a cut-off answer is not a "timeout-or-duplicate". One key per call, the same
 *   on its retries.
 * - A pass is success true AND the answer's hostname equal to the app's own (new URL(getBaseUrl()).hostname, never the
 *   request's Host) AND its action equal to TURNSTILE_ACTION, as Cloudflare asks the server to check.
 * - Every refusal is one line with the reason and Cloudflare's error codes; never the token or the secret. A secret
 *   Cloudflare refuses is reported (the setup is broken for everyone); giving up after the retries is reported as a
 *   warning.
 * Server only.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import { isIP } from 'net';
import { getBaseUrl } from '../../config/urls';
import { captureError } from '../../lib/error-capture';
import { fetchAndReadWithRetry, HttpStatusError } from '../../utils/fetch-retry';
import { wholeJson } from '../../utils/whole-json';
import { SafeSignInError, safeErrorSummary } from './safe-error';

export const SITEVERIFY_URL = 'https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify';
/** The widget's action on the email form; the client sends the same string (components/site/TurnstileWidget.tsx). */
export const TURNSTILE_ACTION = 'email-code';
/** The longest token Cloudflare makes. */
const MAX_TOKEN = 2048;

export type TurnstileRefusal = 'missing' | 'refused' | 'hostname' | 'action' | 'unavailable';
export type TurnstileVerdict = { ok: true } | { ok: false; why: TurnstileRefusal };

/** The token's own fault: a person can pass a new check. */
const TOKEN_FAULTS = new Set(['missing-input-response', 'invalid-input-response', 'timeout-or-duplicate']);
/** Our setup's fault: no one can pass until the secret is fixed. */
const SETUP_FAULTS = new Set(['missing-input-secret', 'invalid-input-secret']);

/** Whether the email form has the check: both variables set. */
export function turnstileConfigured(): boolean {
  return Boolean(process.env.TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY && process.env.TURNSTILE_SECRET);
}

/** The site key the /signin page gives its form, read per request (never NEXT_PUBLIC_, so no build holds it); null while off. */
export function turnstileSiteKey(): string | null {
  return turnstileConfigured() ? (process.env.TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY as string) : null;
}

/** Cloudflare's error codes as they came, only when they look like codes (letters, digits and hyphens). */
function errorCodes(answer: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
  const raw = answer['error-codes'];
  return Array.isArray(raw) ? raw.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && /^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$/.test(c)) : [];
}

function refuse(why: TurnstileRefusal, detail = ''): TurnstileVerdict {
  console.info(`[turnstile] check refused: ${why}${detail ? ` (${detail})` : ''}`);
  return { ok: false, why };
}

/**
 * Checks a Turnstile token for an email-code request. `ip` is the client's own address (clientIp), sent as remoteip
 * when it is one. Never throws: every failure is a refusal (the route answers 'check').
 */
export async function verifyTurnstile(token: unknown, ip: string | null): Promise<TurnstileVerdict> {
  const secret = process.env.TURNSTILE_SECRET;
  if (!secret) return refuse('unavailable', 'TURNSTILE_SECRET is not set');
  if (typeof token !== 'string' || token.length === 0 || token.length > MAX_TOKEN) return refuse('missing');
  const form = new URLSearchParams({ secret, response: token, idempotency_key: crypto.randomUUID() });
  if (ip !== null && isIP(ip) !== 0) form.set('remoteip', ip);

  let answer: unknown;
  try {
    const response = await fetchAndReadWithRetry(SITEVERIFY_URL, { method: 'POST', body: form }, wholeJson, {
      label: '[turnstile]',
      onGiveUp: (error, { retried, why }) => {
        const status = error instanceof HttpStatusError ? `status ${error.status}` : 'no answer';
        console.error(`[turnstile] gave up on siteverify: ${status}, ${why} (${retried} retries)`);
      },
    });
    answer = await response.json();
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(new SafeSignInError(`turnstile siteverify: ${safeErrorSummary(error)}`), 'turnstile', {}, 'warning');
    return refuse('unavailable');
  }
  if (!answer || typeof answer !== 'object' || Array.isArray(answer)) return refuse('unavailable', 'an answer that is not an object');
  const fields = answer as Record<string, unknown>;
  const codes = errorCodes(fields);
  if (fields.success !== true) {
    if (codes.some((c) => SETUP_FAULTS.has(c))) {
      captureError(new SafeSignInError(`turnstile: Cloudflare refused the secret (${codes.join(', ')})`), 'turnstile');
      return refuse('unavailable', codes.join(', '));
    }
    if (codes.length > 0 && codes.every((c) => TOKEN_FAULTS.has(c))) return refuse('refused', codes.join(', '));
    return refuse('unavailable', codes.join(', ') || 'no error codes');
  }
  if (fields.hostname !== new URL(getBaseUrl()).hostname) return refuse('hostname');
  if (fields.action !== TURNSTILE_ACTION) return refuse('action');
  return { ok: true };
}
```

```ts
export function clientAddress(request: Request): string | null {
  const raw = request.headers.get('x-real-ip')?.trim() ?? '';

  const kind = isIP(raw);
  if (kind === 4) return raw;
  if (kind === 6) return ipv6Block(raw);
```

after:

```ts
/** The address to count by: an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64 written `a:b:c:d::/64`; null when the header is missing or not an address. */
export function clientAddress(request: Request): string | null {
  const raw = request.headers.get('x-real-ip')?.trim() ?? '';
  if (raw === '') return null;
  const kind = isIP(raw);
  if (kind === 4) return raw;
  if (kind === 6) return ipv6Block(raw);
  return null;
}

/**
 * The client's own address, as Railway's edge set it (the same x-real-ip, trimmed), for a provider that asks for it:
 * Turnstile's remoteip (web sign-up spec §3.1). Never for counting (that is clientAddress, by /64). null when the
 * header is missing or not an address.
 */
export function clientIp(request: Request): string | null {
  const raw = request.headers.get('x-real-ip')?.trim() ?? '';
  return raw !== '' && isIP(raw) !== 0 ? raw : null;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Create `components/site/TurnstileWidget.tsx`**

```tsx
'use client';

// Cloudflare Turnstile on /signin's email form (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.4, §3.1): the check that a person, not a
// program, asks for a code. No package: Cloudflare's script, injected once per page when the first widget mounts
// (explicit rendering), and one widget per mount.
//
// - The widget runs in the mode its Cloudflare widget is set to (Managed: most people see a short spinner). theme 'auto'
//   follows the device's dark mode; the language is the page's; the size is 'flexible' (the form's width), or 'compact'
//   where the form is narrower than the 300 px a flexible widget needs (a 320 px phone), so the page never scrolls
//   sideways.
// - The token goes to the parent (onToken), and null whenever there is none: before the pass, after it expired (the
//   widget then fetches a new one by itself), after an error, and on unmount. reset() (the parent calls it after each
//   request, since a token works once) asks for a new one.
// - An error, a timeout or a script that didn't load shows one line and Try again, which renders a fresh widget (and
//   loads the script again when it failed). Inside Telegram's own browser this is what the page can do: the check runs
//   in Cloudflare's iframe, uses no cookie of ours and opens no window. The live check (spec §8) confirms it there.
// - A log line holds Cloudflare's error code only, never the token. Words: site.signin.turnstile*.

import { useEffect, useImperativeHandle, useRef, useState, type Ref } from 'react';
import { useLocale, useTranslations } from 'next-intl';

export const TURNSTILE_SCRIPT = 'https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit';
/** The server's TURNSTILE_ACTION (src/services/web-signin/turnstile.ts, server only); siteverify refuses any other. */
const ACTION = 'email-code';
/** The narrowest a 'flexible' widget draws. */
const FLEXIBLE_MIN_PX = 300;
const TAG = '[turnstile]';

interface TurnstileApi {
  render(container: HTMLElement, options: Record<string, unknown>): string | null | undefined;
  reset(widgetId: string): void;
  remove(widgetId: string): void;
}

export interface TurnstileHandle {
  /** Forgets the token and asks the widget for a new one. */
  reset(): void;
}

const apiOf = (): TurnstileApi | undefined => (window as unknown as { turnstile?: TurnstileApi }).turnstile;

/** The one load of Cloudflare's script per page; a failed load is forgotten, so the next render tries again. */
let loading: Promise<TurnstileApi> | null = null;
function loadTurnstile(): Promise<TurnstileApi> {
  const ready = apiOf();
  if (ready) return Promise.resolve(ready);
  if (!loading) {
    const load = new Promise<TurnstileApi>((resolve, reject) => {
      const script = document.createElement('script');
      script.src = TURNSTILE_SCRIPT;
      script.async = true;
      script.onload = () => {
        const api = apiOf();
        if (api) resolve(api);
        else reject(new Error('the script loaded without window.turnstile'));
      };
      script.onerror = () => {
        script.parentNode?.removeChild(script);
        reject(new Error('the script did not load'));
      };
      document.head.appendChild(script);
    });
    loading = load;
    load.catch(() => {
      if (loading === load) loading = null;
    });
  }
  return loading;
}

export function TurnstileWidget({ siteKey, onToken, ref }: { siteKey: string; onToken: (token: string | null) => void; ref?: Ref<TurnstileHandle> }) {
  const t = useTranslations('site.signin');
  const locale = useLocale();
  const box = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const widgetId = useRef<string | null>(null);
  const tokenTo = useRef(onToken);
  const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState(0);
  const [problem, setProblem] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    tokenTo.current = onToken;
  }, [onToken]);

  useImperativeHandle(
    ref,
    () => ({
      reset() {
        tokenTo.current(null);
        const api = apiOf();
        if (api && widgetId.current) api.reset(widgetId.current);
      },
    }),
    [],
  );

  useEffect(() => {
    let gone = false;
    const fail = (why: string) => {
      console.warn(`${TAG} the browser check failed (${why})`);
      tokenTo.current(null);
      setProblem(true);
    };
    loadTurnstile().then(
      (api) => {
        if (gone || !box.current) return;
        const narrow = (box.current.clientWidth || FLEXIBLE_MIN_PX) < FLEXIBLE_MIN_PX;
        const id = api.render(box.current, {
          sitekey: siteKey,
          action: ACTION,
          theme: 'auto',
          language: locale,
          size: narrow ? 'compact' : 'flexible',
          callback: (token: string) => {
            setProblem(false);
            tokenTo.current(token);
          },
          'error-callback': (code: unknown) => {
            fail(`error ${String(code).replace(/[^0-9a-z]/gi, '').slice(0, 12)}`);
            return true;
          },
          'expired-callback': () => tokenTo.current(null),
          'timeout-callback': () => fail('timeout'),
        });
        widgetId.current = typeof id === 'string' ? id : null;
        if (!widgetId.current) fail('no widget');
      },
      (error: unknown) => {
        if (!gone) fail(error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'the script did not load');
      },
    );
    return () => {
      gone = true;
      const api = apiOf();
      if (api && widgetId.current) api.remove(widgetId.current);
      widgetId.current = null;
      tokenTo.current(null);
    };
  }, [siteKey, locale, attempt]);

  const retry = () => {
    setProblem(false);
    setAttempt((n) => n + 1);
  };

  return (
    <div className="site-turnstile">
      <div ref={box} />
      {problem ? (
        <>
          <p className="site-field-error" role="alert">
            {t('turnstileProblem')}
          </p>
          <button type="button" className="site-signin-link" onClick={retry}>
            {t('turnstileRetry')}
          </button>
        </>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

after:

```tsx
  const requestCode = async (event?: FormEvent) => {
    event?.preventDefault();
    const address = email.trim();
    if (busy || address === '' || waiting) return;
    setBusy('email');
    setProblem(null);
    try {
      const res = await fetch('/api/auth/email/request', {
        method: 'POST',
        credentials: 'same-origin',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify(turnstileSiteKey ? { email: address, locale, token } : { email: address, locale }),
      });
      const body = await readJsonBody(res, `${TAG} code request`);
      if (res.ok && body?.ok === true) {
        setEmail(address);
        setCode('');
        setStep('code');
        return;
      }
      if (body?.error === 'check') {
        console.warn(`${TAG} the browser check was refused (${res.status})`);
        setProblem('emailCheck');
        return;
      }
      console.warn(`${TAG} the code request answered ${res.status}`);
      setProblem('requestFailed');
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`${TAG} the code request failed:`, error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error);
      setProblem('requestFailed');
    } finally {
      setBusy(null);
      // A token works once: the check asks for the next one
      if (turnstileSiteKey) checkRef.current?.reset();
    }
  };
```

- [ ] **Step 12: The startup warning, the README rows and the `.env.example` placeholders**

`src/lib/startup-checks.ts:41-63`, before:

```ts
/**
 * The web sign-in ways and the variables each one needs (web sign-in spec §6). The owner sets them after the deploy,
 * and a way stays hidden until its own are set (oidc.ts's providerConfigured, email-send.ts's emailConfigured), so an
 * unset one is a warning (signInSetupWarnings), never a StartupProblem: no Sentry capture, not "missing" in the deploy
 * message.
 */
export const SIGN_IN_ENV: readonly { way: string; names: readonly string[] }[] = [
  { way: 'Telegram', names: ['TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID', 'TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET'] },
  { way: 'Google', names: ['GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID', 'GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET'] },
  { way: 'an email code', names: ['RESEND_API_KEY'] },
];

/**
 * One line per web sign-in way that is off, naming its unset variables (never a value), and one for a Google sign-in
 * client that is the calendar client (oidc.ts keeps that way off: a calendar-client token must never sign anyone in).
 * Pure: env in, lines out.
 */
export function signInSetupWarnings(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): string[] {
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  for (const { way, names } of SIGN_IN_ENV) {
    const unset = names.filter((name) => !env[name]);
    if (unset.length > 0) warnings.push(`web sign-in with ${way} is off: ${unset.join(' and ')} ${unset.length > 1 ? 'are' : 'is'} not set`);
  }
```

after:

```ts
/**
 * The web sign-in ways and the variables each one needs (web sign-in spec §6), and email sign-up's bot check (web
 * sign-up spec §6: Turnstile, turnstile.ts's turnstileConfigured). The owner sets them after the deploy, and a way stays
 * hidden until its own are set (oidc.ts's providerConfigured, email-send.ts's emailConfigured), so an unset one is a
 * warning (signInSetupWarnings), never a StartupProblem: no Sentry capture, not "missing" in the deploy message.
 * `off` names what is off when it is not the way's sign-in.
 */
export const SIGN_IN_ENV: readonly { way: string; names: readonly string[]; off?: string }[] = [
  { way: 'Telegram', names: ['TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID', 'TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET'] },
  { way: 'Google', names: ['GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID', 'GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET'] },
  { way: 'an email code', names: ['RESEND_API_KEY'] },
  // Email sign-in works without it; sign-up by email waits for both
  { way: 'an email code', names: ['TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY', 'TURNSTILE_SECRET'], off: 'web sign-up with an email code' },
];

/**
 * One line per web sign-in way that is off, naming its unset variables (never a value), and one for a Google sign-in
 * client that is the calendar client (oidc.ts keeps that way off: a calendar-client token must never sign anyone in).
 * Pure: env in, lines out.
 */
export function signInSetupWarnings(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): string[] {
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  for (const { way, names, off } of SIGN_IN_ENV) {
    const unset = names.filter((name) => !env[name]);
    if (unset.length > 0) warnings.push(`${off ?? `web sign-in with ${way}`} is off: ${unset.join(' and ')} ${unset.length > 1 ? 'are' : 'is'} not set`);
  }
```

```ts
// Smoke test for the email sign-up code (6c-1 plan, Task 4; spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md
// §2.2, §2.5, §3.1, §3.2, §8 "Sign-up" and "Email budget"): POST /api/auth/email/request's after() for an address on no
// account, POST /api/auth/email/verify's sign-up branch, email-code.ts's 'signup' purpose, the sign-up email, the
// limits' sign-up share (counted for real), identities.ts's findWayByAddress, and flow.ts's sign-up record with its invite
// (src/lib/invite-token.ts).

//  - U1 with Turnstile, an address on no account gets a sign-up code at the address typed (normalised), in the page's
//    language (Hebrew right to left), kept as a keyed hash with its address and no account; the answer, its cookie and
//    the work before it are those of an address on an account
//  - U2 a right sign-up code answers { ok: true, redirect: https://famcal.bot/<locale>/signup } with a new famcal_signin
//    cookie (set, not cleared) for the flow { kind: 'signup', way: 'email', subject, address, locale }; the email flow
//    is used up, no session is made, and the old cookie can't be used again
//  - U3 without Turnstile, an address on no account is mailed nothing (6b's line), and its code check is "wrong"
//  - U4 a wrong sign-up code is a wrong code (counted for the address), and the right one still works after it; a wrong
//    code for an account's address asks no sign-up code
//  - U5 the 4th sign-up code from one client address is refused (no mail, the reason logged); another address gets one
//  - U6 the 31st sign-up code of the UTC day is refused and the admin told once; a sign-in code still goes out; the
//    sign-up codes are counted inside the day's 90
//  - U7 a right sign-up code for an address an account signs in with by now signs in as that account; for one a
//    Google way shows (in another case) it answers 'exists' with way 'google', no session and no sign-up flow; the
//    request never told
//  - U8 findWayByAddress: the email way first, a Google way by its stored address in any case, nothing else
//  - U10 capitals and spaces name the same address: an account's address typed so gets its sign-in code, never a
//    sign-up; a new address typed so starts a sign-up for its normalised form, which a later request then finds
//  - U11 a sign-up code entered in another browser (no famcal_signin cookie) answers 'restart' and makes nothing; the
//    first browser can still use it
//  - U12 cleanInviteToken (src/lib/invite-token.ts) and inviteOf: a sign-up record keeps a clean invite and drops a bad one
//  - U9 (run last) no console line or error report holds an address or a code
//
// Real: both routes, turnstile.ts, email-code, email-send, limits, flow, identities, fetch-retry, the session cookie and
// finishSignIn. Faked at the boundaries (scripts/lib/signin-world.ts): Prisma and Redis in memory, error capture, the
// admin notifier, Next's after(), and fetch (siteverify passes, Resend recorded). No network, no DB.
//
// Run with the fake env (never the real one), from the repo root:
//   bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-razielgershoni-development-famcalbot/0d239296-a217-49f9-8833-757c9d9a2df6/scratchpad/6c1/run-smoke.sh smoke-signup-email

import crypto from 'crypto';
import path from 'path';
import { createRequire } from 'module';
import {
  adminWarnings, assert, baseUser, body, check, DB, drainAfter, everyCapture, everyLog, identityRow, installSigninWorld,
  load, mails, prismaCalls, redisStore, report, request, resetWorld, ROOT, show, siteverifyCalls, type Row,
} from './lib/signin-world';

const nodeRequire = createRequire(__filename);
const SITE_KEY = '1x00000000000000000000AA';
const SECRET = 'smoke-signup-turnstile-secret-0001';
const TOKEN = 'XXXX.DUMMY.TOKEN.XXXX-signup';
/** A partner invite token as pairing-service makes it: 64 lowercase hex characters. */
const INVITE = '0123456789abcdef'.repeat(4);
const MESSAGES: Row = {
  en: nodeRequire(path.join(ROOT, 'messages/en.json')),
  he: nodeRequire(path.join(ROOT, 'messages/he.json')),
  ru: nodeRequire(path.join(ROOT, 'messages/ru.json')),
};

function turnstile(on: boolean) {
  if (on) {
    process.env.TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY = SITE_KEY;
    process.env.TURNSTILE_SECRET = SECRET;
  } else {
    delete process.env.TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY;
    delete process.env.TURNSTILE_SECRET;
  }
}

/** 7 Kai (a Google way, its address as Google wrote it), 8 Noa (an email way, Hebrew). */
function seed() {
  resetWorld();
  DB.user = [
    baseUser({ id: 7, name: 'Kai', telegramId: BigInt(5550007) }),
    baseUser({ id: 8, name: 'Noa', telegramId: BigInt(5550008), language: 'he' }),

}

const wrongOf = (code: string) => String((Number(code) + 1) % 1_000_000).padStart(6, '0');

async function main() {
  turnstile(false);
  await installSigninWorld();
  const retry = await load('src/utils/fetch-retry.ts');
  retry.__useRetryForTests({ sleep: async () => undefined, random: () => 0 });
  const requestRoute = await load('app/api/auth/email/request/route.ts');
  const verifyRoute = await load('app/api/auth/email/verify/route.ts');
  const { SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
  const { SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, validateSessionToken } = await load('src/lib/session-auth.ts');
  const { emailKey } = await load('src/services/web-signin/email-address.ts');
  const { REDIS_KEYS } = await load('src/config/redis-keys.ts');
  const { findWayByAddress } = await load('src/services/web-signin/identities.ts');

    const value = res.cookies.get(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME)?.value as string | undefined;
    return { status: res.status as number, body: await body(res as Response), cookie: value ? `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${value}` : undefined };
  };
  /** Asks for a code, runs the after() work, and returns the email it sent (null when none) and the code in it. */
  const codeFor = async (email: string, o: { ip?: string | null; locale?: string } = {}) => {
    const before = mails.length;
    const asked = await ask(email, o);
    await drainAfter();
    const mail = mails.length > before ? mails[mails.length - 1] : null;
    const code = mail ? (/\b(\d{6})\b/.exec(String(mail.body.text))?.[1] ?? null) : null;
    if (code) codes.add(code);
    return { ...asked, mail, code };
  };
  const verify = async (cookie: string | undefined, code: string) => {
    const res: Row = await verifyRoute.POST(request('/api/auth/email/verify', { body: { code }, cookie }));
    return { res, status: res.status as number, body: await body(res as Response) };
  };
  const flows = () => [...redisStore.entries()].filter(([k]) => k.startsWith('signin:flow:')).map(([, v]) => JSON.parse(v) as Row);
  const sessionOf = (res: Row) => {
    const value = res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value as string | undefined;

  await check('U1 with Turnstile, an address on no account gets a sign-up code at the address typed (normalised), in the page\'s language (Hebrew right to left), kept as a keyed hash with its address and no account; the answer, its cookie and the work before it are those of an address on an account', async () => {

    assert(known.cookie && unknown.cookie, 'a flow cookie for both');
    assert(show(knownWork) === show({ prisma: 0, siteverify: 1 }) && show(unknownWork) === show(knownWork), `the work before the answer: ${show({ knownWork, unknownWork })}`);
    assert(mails.length === 0, 'mailed before the answer');

  await check('U2 a right sign-up code answers { ok: true, redirect: /<locale>/signup } with a new famcal_signin cookie (set, not cleared) for the sign-up flow; the email flow is used up, no session is made, the old cookie can\'t be used again', async () => {

  await check('U7 a right sign-up code for an address an account signs in with by now signs in as that account; for one a Google way shows (in another case) it answers "exists" with way google, no session and no sign-up flow; the request never told', async () => {

    assert(show(elsewhere.body) === show({ ok: false, error: 'restart' }) && !sessionOf(elsewhere.res), `browser B: ${show(elsewhere.body)}`);
    assert(DB.user.length === users && !flows().some((f) => f.kind === 'signup'), 'browser B made something');
    assert(redisStore.has(REDIS_KEYS.signinCode('signup', key)) && !redisStore.has(REDIS_KEYS.signinCodeTries('signup', key)), 'browser B touched the code');
    const here = await verify(sent.cookie, sent.code);
    assert(show(here.body) === show({ ok: true, redirect: 'https://famcal.bot/en/signup' }), `browser A after B: ${show(here.body)}`);
    assert(flows().some((f) => f.kind === 'signup' && f.subject === 'other.browser@example.com'), 'no sign-up flow in browser A');
  });

  await check('U12 the invite a sign-up carries: cleanInviteToken keeps 64 lowercase hex and nothing else; inviteOf reads it from a record and drops a bad one; a stored sign-up reads back with a clean invite, without a bad one, and a sign-up of an unknown way reads as nothing', async () => {
    seed();
    const { cleanInviteToken } = await load('src/lib/invite-token.ts');
    const { inviteOf, takeFlow } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
    assert(cleanInviteToken(INVITE) === INVITE, 'a real token is dropped');
    for (const bad of [INVITE.toUpperCase(), INVITE.slice(1), `${INVITE}0`, ` ${INVITE}`, `../${INVITE.slice(3)}`, 'g'.repeat(64), 64, null, undefined, [INVITE]]) {
      assert(cleanInviteToken(bad) === null, `kept ${show(bad)}`);
      assert(show(inviteOf({ invite: bad })) === '{}', `inviteOf kept ${show(bad)}`);
    }
    assert(show(inviteOf({ invite: INVITE })) === show({ invite: INVITE }) && show(inviteOf({})) === '{}', 'inviteOf');
    const flowId = 'A'.repeat(43);
    const cookie = `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${flowId}`;
    const recordKey = REDIS_KEYS.signinFlow(crypto.createHash('sha256').update(flowId).digest('hex'));
    const startedAt = Date.now();
    const base = { kind: 'signup', way: 'email', subject: 'new.person@example.com', address: 'new.person@example.com', locale: 'he' };
    const cases: [unknown, Row][] = [[INVITE, { invite: INVITE }], [`${INVITE}0`, {}], [undefined, {}]];
    for (const [invite, want] of cases) {
      redisStore.set(recordKey, JSON.stringify({ ...base, startedAt, ...(invite === undefined ? {} : { invite }) }));
      const flow = await takeFlow(request('/api/auth/signup', { cookie }), ['signup']);
      assert(show(flow) === show({ ...base, ...want, startedAt }), `the sign-up read back (invite ${show(invite)}): ${show(flow)}`);
    }
    redisStore.set(recordKey, JSON.stringify({ ...base, startedAt, way: 'telegram' }));
    assert((await takeFlow(request('/api/auth/signup', { cookie }), ['signup'])) === null, 'a sign-up of an unknown way');
  });

  await check('U9 no console line or error report holds an address or a code', () => {
    const addresses = [...new Set(typed.map((a) => a.toLowerCase()))];
    const codeRes = [...codes].map((c) => new RegExp(`\\b${c}\\b`));
    const holds = (text: string) => addresses.some((a) => text.toLowerCase().includes(a)) || codeRes.some((re) => re.test(text)) || text.includes(TOKEN) || text.includes(SECRET);
    const lines = everyLog.filter(holds);
    assert(lines.length === 0, `console lines: ${show(lines.slice(0, 5))}`);
    const reports = everyCapture.filter((c) => holds(show(c)));
    assert(reports.length === 0, `error reports: ${show(reports.slice(0, 5))}`);
  });

  report();
}

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```ts
/** The day's budget: its key (the UTC date) and the seconds to the next 00:00 UTC. */
function budget(nowMs: number): { key: string; ttlSec: number } {
  const day = new Date(nowMs).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const nextMidnight = (Math.floor(nowMs / DAY_MS) + 1) * DAY_MS;
  return { key: limitKey('daily-send', day), ttlSec: Math.max(1, Math.ceil((nextMidnight - nowMs) / 1000)) };
}
```

after:

```ts
/** A UTC day's count of `what` (the 90's 'daily-send', 'signup-send', 'notice-send'): its key (the date) and the seconds to the next 00:00 UTC. */
function dayCount(what: string, nowMs: number): { key: string; ttlSec: number } {
  const day = new Date(nowMs).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const nextMidnight = (Math.floor(nowMs / DAY_MS) + 1) * DAY_MS;
  return { key: limitKey(what, day), ttlSec: Math.max(1, Math.ceil((nextMidnight - nowMs) / 1000)) };
}

/** The day's budget of codes (the 90). */
const budget = (nowMs: number) => dayCount('daily-send', nowMs);
```

```ts

/** The one admin message when the day's sign-up codes are spent (the first refusal of a UTC day). */
async function tellAdminSignUpsPaused(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const { notifyAdminWarning } = await import('../../utils/error-notifier');
    await notifyAdminWarning(
      'signin-signup-budget',
      `Email sign-up sent its ${LIMIT.signUpCodesPerDay} sign-up codes for today (UTC), and pauses until 00:00 UTC. Sign-in codes still go out, within the day's ${LIMIT.codesSentPerDay}.`,
    );
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-signup-budget-alert', {}, 'warning');
  }
}

/**
 * May a sign-up code be mailed now (web sign-up spec §2.5)? Counts it: first the client address's 3 a day (a refusal
 * there counts nothing for the day, so one address can't spend the day's share), then the UTC day's 30. The first
 * refusal of a day tells the admin, once. The code itself still takes from the 90 in issueCode. Redis failing refuses
 * (store-down) and is reported. No line holds the address.
 */
export async function takeSignUpSend(ip: string | null): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'signup-day' | 'signup-ip-day' | 'store-down' }> {
  try {
    if ((await count(limitKey('signup-ip-day', addressId(ip)), DAY_SEC)) > LIMIT.signUpCodesPerAddressDay) {
      console.info('[signin-limits] sign-up code refused: signup-ip-day');
      return { ok: false, reason: 'signup-ip-day' };
    }
    const { key, ttlSec } = dayCount('signup-send', Date.now());
    const sent = await count(key, ttlSec);
    if (sent > LIMIT.signUpCodesPerDay) {
      if (sent === LIMIT.signUpCodesPerDay + 1) await tellAdminSignUpsPaused();
      console.warn(`[signin-limits] sign-up code refused: signup-day (the day's ${LIMIT.signUpCodesPerDay} are sent; no more until 00:00 UTC)`);
      return { ok: false, reason: 'signup-day' };
    }
    return { ok: true };
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-limits', { step: 'sign-up send' });
    return { ok: false, reason: 'store-down' };
  }
}

/**
 * Takes one security notice by email for this account (web sign-up spec §1, §2.11): first the account's own 3 a UTC
 * day (a refusal there counts nothing for the day, so one account repeating Add Google can't spend everyone's
 * notices), then the UTC day's 10, a budget of their own apart from the 90 codes, so a flood of code requests can't
 * silence a notice. Redis failing refuses (store-down) and is reported. The caller logs a refused notice as its
 * SECURITY line; no line here holds an address.
 */
export async function takeNoticeSend(userId: number): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'notice-account-day' | 'notice-budget' | 'store-down' }> {
  const now = Date.now();
  const { key, ttlSec } = dayCount('notice-send', now);
  try {
    // The account's share lives to the next 00:00 UTC too, so both counts start over together
    if ((await count(limitKey('notice-account-day', signinHash('account', String(userId))), ttlSec)) > LIMIT.noticesPerAccountDay) {
      console.warn(`[signin-limits] notice refused: notice-account-day (user ${userId}: the account's ${LIMIT.noticesPerAccountDay} security notices by email today are sent)`);
      return { ok: false, reason: 'notice-account-day' };
    }
    const sent = await count(key, ttlSec);
    if (sent > LIMIT.noticesPerDay) {
      console.warn(`[signin-limits] notice refused: notice-budget (the day's ${LIMIT.noticesPerDay} security notices by email are sent; no more until 00:00 UTC)`);
      return { ok: false, reason: 'notice-budget' };
    }
    return { ok: true };
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-limits', { step: 'notice send', user_id: userId });
    return { ok: false, reason: 'store-down' };
  }
}

/**
 * May one more account be made from this client address today (web sign-up spec §2.6)? 5 a day per IPv4 address or
 * IPv6 /48 (accountAddressKey: a /64 is easy to change). `ip` is clientAddress's value. Without one nothing is counted
 * (one shared count would let anyone block everyone), and that is logged. Redis failing refuses (store-down).
 */
export async function allowNewAccount(ip: string | null): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'accounts-ip-day' | 'store-down' }> {
  if (ip === null) {
    console.warn('[signup] no client address; the account cap is not counted');
    return { ok: true };
  }
  try {
    if ((await count(limitKey('accounts-ip-day', signinHash('ip', accountAddressKey(ip))), DAY_SEC)) > LIMIT.newAccountsPerAddressDay) {
      console.info('[signin-limits] new account refused: accounts-ip-day');
      return { ok: false, reason: 'accounts-ip-day' };
    }
    return { ok: true };
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-limits', { step: 'new account' });
    return { ok: false, reason: 'store-down' };
  }
}
```

```ts

/**
 * The key the new-accounts cap counts by (web sign-up spec §2.6), from clientAddress's value: an IPv4 address as it
 * is, an IPv6 /64 as its /48 (`a:b:c:d::/64` → `a:b:c::/48`), since a home or a phone line can pick any /64 of its /48.
 * Pure.
 */
export function accountAddressKey(address: string): string {
  const v6 = /^([0-9a-f]{1,4}):([0-9a-f]{1,4}):([0-9a-f]{1,4}):[0-9a-f]{1,4}::\/64$/.exec(address);
  return v6 ? `${v6[1]}:${v6[2]}:${v6[3]}::/48` : address;
}
```
