Replace the whole of `src/services/web-signin/email-code.ts` (135 lines) with:

```ts
/**
 * Email codes (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-web-sign-in-design.md §3 "Email", §5; the sign-up code, web
 * sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §3.1, §3.2).
 *
 *   issueCode   a 6-digit code (crypto.randomInt), kept in Upstash only as a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256 with
 *               appKey('signin')) with its account and address, for 10 minutes, one per purpose and address: a new code
 *               replaces the old one and, once it is mailed, its tries start again. That reset is safe because the
 *               new code is a fresh secret and the guesses are capped apart from it: 10 wrong codes a day per address
 *               pause the checks (recordWrongCode, limits.ts), and that count is not reset. The day's send budget
 *               (takeDailySend) is asked before the code is stored, so a spent day never replaces a code that still
 *               works. Then it is mailed; when the send fails (sendCodeEmail throws), the code that worked before is
 *               put back with its remaining time and tries, so a failed send never leaves the person with no code.
 *               A sign-in or Add email code names its account; a sign-up code names none (there is no account yet):
 *               its record is the hash and the address it went to, and nothing else.
 *   checkCode   counts the try with countWithin (limits.ts: one Lua call, INCR and the expiry together, so a count is
 *               never left without one) before it compares; the fifth wrong try voids the code; a right one is used up
 *               at once (GETDEL). A missing code is 'expired', with the same work as a wrong one. A right code gives
 *               its account (null for a sign-up code) and its address.
 *
 * The account lookups by address (findEmailSignIn, emailSignInAccount, touchEmailSignIn) are in identities.ts, the one
 * file that reads SignInIdentity.
 *
 * No line holds the address or the code. Server only.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import { appKey } from '../../lib/app-keys';
import { matchesSecret } from '../../lib/secret-compare';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '../../config/redis-keys';
import { redis } from '../../utils/redis';
import { countWithin, takeDailySend } from './limits';
import { codeOwner, sendCodeEmail, type CodePurpose } from './email-send';
import { SafeSignInError, safeErrorSummary } from './safe-error';

/** How long a code works, and how long its tries are counted (s). */
export const CODE_TTL_SEC = 10 * 60;
/** What is left of a stored code's time, from Redis's TTL answer (-1 no expiry, -2 no key), never past a code's 10 minutes. */
export function codeTimeLeftSec(ttl: number): number {
  return ttl > 0 ? Math.min(ttl, CODE_TTL_SEC) : 0;
}

/** Tries per code: the fifth wrong one voids it. */
export const CODE_MAX_TRIES = 5;

/** A stored code: its keyed hash and the address it went to; the account it signs in or adds to, except a sign-up code's. */
interface CodeRecord {
  hash: string;
  userId?: number;
  address: string;
}

/** A stored code of this purpose: a sign-up code has no account, every other code has one. */
function isCodeRecord(value: unknown, purpose: CodePurpose): value is CodeRecord {
  const v = value as Partial<CodeRecord> | null;
  if (!v || typeof v !== 'object' || typeof v.hash !== 'string' || typeof v.address !== 'string') return false;
  return purpose === 'signup' ? v.userId === undefined : typeof v.userId === 'number';
}

/** The code's keyed hash, bound to its purpose and address. Throws without SESSION_SECRET (appKey reports it). */
function codeHash(purpose: CodePurpose, emailKey: string, code: string): string {
  const key = appKey('signin');
  if (!key) throw new SafeSignInError('SESSION_SECRET is not set: no sign-in key, so no code can be made or checked');
  return crypto.createHmac('sha256', key).update(`code:${purpose}:${emailKey}:${code}`).digest('hex');
}

/**
 * Makes, stores and mails a code for `address` (the row's address for sign-in; the address being added for 'add'; the
 * normalised address typed for 'signup'). `userId` is the account, and null exactly for a sign-up code.
 */
export async function issueCode(args: { purpose: CodePurpose; emailKey: string; address: string; userId: number | null; locale: string }): Promise<void> {
  const { purpose, emailKey, address, userId, locale } = args;
  if ((purpose === 'signup') !== (userId === null)) {
    throw new SafeSignInError(`a ${purpose} code ${userId === null ? 'needs an account' : 'names no account'}`);
  }
  const code = crypto.randomInt(0, 1_000_000).toString().padStart(6, '0');
  const record: CodeRecord = { hash: codeHash(purpose, emailKey, code), address, ...(userId !== null ? { userId } : {}) };
  if (!(await takeDailySend())) {
    console.warn(`[signin-email] the day's send budget is spent: no ${purpose} code for ${codeOwner(userId)}`);
    return;
  }
  const codeKey = REDIS_KEYS.signinCode(purpose, emailKey);
  const stored = await redis.get<CodeRecord>(codeKey);
  const previous = isCodeRecord(stored, purpose) ? stored : null;
  const previousSec = previous ? await redis.ttl(codeKey) : -2;
  await redis.set(codeKey, record, { ex: CODE_TTL_SEC });
  try {
    await sendCodeEmail({ to: address, code, locale, purpose, userId });
  } catch (error) {
    await restoreAfterFailedSend(codeKey, record, previous, previousSec, purpose, userId);
    throw error;
  }
  // The tries start again only for a code that reached the person (a failed send keeps the old code's count).
  await redis.del(REDIS_KEYS.signinCodeTries(purpose, emailKey));
}

/**
 * The send failed, so the new code was never delivered: put the code that worked before back with the time it had left,
 * or drop the new one when there was none. Only while the stored code is still this one (a newer request may have
 * replaced it). A failure here is logged and the send's own error is still the one thrown.
 */
async function restoreAfterFailedSend(
  codeKey: string,
  issued: CodeRecord,
  previous: CodeRecord | null,
  previousSec: number,
  purpose: CodePurpose,
  userId: number | null
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const current = await redis.get<CodeRecord>(codeKey);
    if (!isCodeRecord(current, purpose) || current.hash !== issued.hash) return;
    const codeLeftSec = codeTimeLeftSec(previousSec);
    if (previous && codeLeftSec > 0) {
      await redis.set(codeKey, previous, { ex: codeLeftSec });
      console.warn(`[signin-email] the ${purpose} code for ${codeOwner(userId)} was not sent: the earlier code works again`);
    } else {
      await redis.del(codeKey);
    }
  } catch (restoreError) {
    console.error(`[signin-email] the ${purpose} code for ${codeOwner(userId)} was not sent, and the earlier code could not be put back: ${safeErrorSummary(restoreError)}`);
  }
}

/** Checks `code` against the address's current code of this purpose (see the file comment). */
export async function checkCode(
  purpose: CodePurpose,
  emailKey: string,
  code: string
): Promise<{ ok: true; userId: number | null; address: string } | { ok: false; reason: 'wrong' | 'expired' }> {
  const codeKey = REDIS_KEYS.signinCode(purpose, emailKey);
  const triesKey = REDIS_KEYS.signinCodeTries(purpose, emailKey);
  const given = codeHash(purpose, emailKey, code);
  const tries = await countWithin(triesKey, CODE_TTL_SEC);
  const stored = await redis.get<CodeRecord>(codeKey);
  if (!isCodeRecord(stored, purpose)) return { ok: false, reason: 'expired' };
  if (tries > CODE_MAX_TRIES) {
    await redis.del(codeKey);
    return { ok: false, reason: 'expired' };
  }
  if (!matchesSecret(given, stored.hash)) {
    if (tries === CODE_MAX_TRIES) await redis.del(codeKey);
    return { ok: false, reason: 'wrong' };
  }
  // Used up at once. Another request may have taken it, or a new code replaced it, since the read.
  const claimed = await redis.getdel<CodeRecord>(codeKey);
  if (!isCodeRecord(claimed, purpose) || !matchesSecret(given, claimed.hash)) return { ok: false, reason: 'expired' };
  await redis.del(triesKey);
  return { ok: true, userId: claimed.userId ?? null, address: claimed.address };
}
```

Insert after `src/services/web-signin/identities.ts:77` (the closing `}` of `findEmailSignIn`):

```ts

/**
 * Which way, if any, already shows this verified address (web sign-up spec §2.2): an email way whose subject is it, or
 * a Google way whose stored address is it in any case (Google gives the address as it likes). A check on an address
 * the person just proved (a right sign-up code, Google's verified email), never a sign-in: the caller only refuses a
 * second account with it. Email first. The case-blind compare is narrowed by the database and then made exact here,
 * so no character of the address acts as a pattern.
 */
export async function findWayByAddress(normalized: string): Promise<{ kind: IdentityKind; userId: number } | null> {
  const email = await prisma.signInIdentity.findUnique({
    where: { kind_subject: { kind: 'email', subject: normalized } },
    select: { userId: true },
  });
  if (email) return { kind: 'email', userId: email.userId };
  const google = await prisma.signInIdentity.findMany({
    where: { kind: 'google', address: { equals: normalized, mode: 'insensitive' } },
    select: { userId: true, address: true },
    take: 10,
  });
  const holder = google.find((row) => row.address.toLowerCase() === normalized);
  return holder ? { kind: 'google', userId: holder.userId } : null;
}
```

```ts
// A pair invite's token as it rides a sign-in (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §3.7): 64 lowercase hex characters, as
// pairing-service's createInvite makes it (32 random bytes). Anything else is no invite and is dropped, so a crafted
// value never reaches a flow record or a landing URL. Client-safe: no import (the invite page builds its /signin link
// with it; the sign-in page, the start routes and the flow records read with it).

const INVITE_TOKEN = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;

/** The token when it is one, else null. */
export function cleanInviteToken(input: unknown): string | null {
  return typeof input === 'string' && INVITE_TOKEN.test(input) ? input : null;
}
```

```ts
/**
```

```ts
 */
export function inviteOf(v: Record<string, unknown>): { invite?: string } {
  const invite = cleanInviteToken(v.invite);
  return invite ? { invite } : {};
}
```

after:

```ts
/**
 * After the answer: the account with this address gets a sign-in code at the address it stores. An address on no
 * account gets a sign-up code at the address typed (normalised, in the page's language) while email sign-up is on
 * (Turnstile configured, so this request passed the check) and within the sign-up share of the day's mail
 * (takeSignUpSend: 30 a day, 3 per client address; web sign-up spec §2.5, §3.1); otherwise nothing is mailed. The
 * answer was the same either way.
 */
async function sendCode(normalized: string, key: string, locale: string, ip: string | null): Promise<void> {
  let userId: number | undefined;
  let purpose: 'signin' | 'signup' = 'signin';
  try {
    const account = await findEmailSignIn(normalized);
    if (account) {
      userId = account.userId;
      await issueCode({ purpose: 'signin', emailKey: key, address: account.address, userId: account.userId, locale: account.language });
      return;
    }
    if (!turnstileConfigured()) {
      console.log('[signin-email] no account signs in with this address; no code sent');
      return;
    }
    const share = await takeSignUpSend(ip);
    if (!share.ok) {
      console.log(`[signin-email] no account signs in with this address; no sign-up code (${share.reason})`);
      return;
    }
    purpose = 'signup';
    await issueCode({ purpose: 'signup', emailKey: key, address: normalized, userId: null, locale });
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'signin-email-send', { api_route: ROUTE, user_id: userId, purpose });
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 10: The verify route's sign-up branch**

Replace the whole of `app/api/auth/email/verify/route.ts` (83 lines) with:

```ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { finishSignIn, signUpPageUrl, type SignInStatus } from '@/src/lib/web-session';
import { clientAddress } from '@/src/services/web-signin/client-address';
import { clearFlowCookie, peekFlow, startFlow, takeFlow, type EmailFlow } from '@/src/services/web-signin/flow';
import { codeChecksBlocked, recordWrongCode } from '@/src/services/web-signin/limits';
import { checkCode } from '@/src/services/web-signin/email-code';
import { emailSignInAccount, findEmailSignIn, findWayByAddress, touchEmailSignIn, type IdentityKind } from '@/src/services/web-signin/identities';
import { captureSignInFailure, SafeSignInError, safeErrorSummary } from '@/src/services/web-signin/safe-error';

const ROUTE = '/api/auth/email/verify';

type VerifyError = 'wrong' | 'restart' | 'limited' | 'suspended' | 'blocked' | 'failed' | 'exists';

function refusal(error: VerifyError, opts: { clearFlow?: boolean; status?: number; way?: IdentityKind } = {}): NextResponse {
  const response = NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error, ...(opts.way ? { way: opts.way } : {}) }, { status: opts.status ?? 200 });
  if (opts.clearFlow) clearFlowCookie(response);
  return response;
}

type Checked =
  | { ok: true; purpose: 'signin'; userId: number; address: string }
  | { ok: true; purpose: 'signup'; address: string }
  | { ok: false; reason: 'wrong' | 'expired' };

/**
 * The address's sign-in code, then its sign-up code (web sign-up spec §3.2). The sign-up code is tried only when the
 * address has no sign-in code to try (an address with no account): a wrong code for an account's address counts one
 * try, as before.
 */
async function checkEither(emailKey: string, code: string): Promise<Checked> {
  const signin = await checkCode('signin', emailKey, code);
  if (signin.ok) {
    if (signin.userId === null) throw new SafeSignInError('a sign-in code with no account');
    return { ok: true, purpose: 'signin', userId: signin.userId, address: signin.address };
  }
  if (signin.reason === 'wrong') return signin;
  const signup = await checkCode('signup', emailKey, code);
  return signup.ok ? { ok: true, purpose: 'signup', address: signup.address } : signup;
}

/**
 * The code screen on /signin (spec §3 "Email", §5). The flow comes from this browser's famcal_signin cookie and stays
 * for the next try (peekFlow). Wrong codes paused for the address or the IP → 'limited', before the code is touched;
 * a wrong, expired or unknown address's code → 'wrong', counted as a wrong code either way; a right sign-in code
 * finishes the sign-in as that account ({ ok: true, redirect } with the session cookie) and clears the flow cookie; a
 * right sign-up code goes on to the sign-up page (signUpNext).
 */
export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const crossSite = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (crossSite) return crossSite;
  try {
    const flow = await peekFlow(request, 'email');
    if (!flow) {
      console.log('[signin-email] a code check with no email flow in this browser: start again');
      // The cookie is left as it is: it may name this browser's newer sign-in of another way (Telegram or Google,
      // started in another tab), which must still finish; a dead one ends by itself in 10 minutes.
      return refusal('restart');
    }
    let body: { code?: unknown };
    try {
      body = await request.json();
    } catch (error) {
      console.warn(`[signin-email] a code check whose body is not JSON: ${safeErrorSummary(error)}`);
      return refusal('wrong');
    }
    const code = typeof body?.code === 'string' ? body.code.trim() : '';
    if (!/^\d{6}$/.test(code)) return refusal('wrong');

    const ip = clientAddress(request);
    if (await codeChecksBlocked({ emailKey: flow.emailKey, ip })) {
      console.log('[signin-email] a code check held back: too many wrong codes for this address or IP');
      return refusal('limited');
    }
    const checked = await checkEither(flow.emailKey, code);
    if (!checked.ok) {
      await recordWrongCode({ emailKey: flow.emailKey, ip });
      console.log(`[signin-email] a code refused (${checked.reason})`);
      return refusal('wrong');
    }
    if (checked.purpose === 'signup') return await signUpNext(request, flow, checked.address);
    return await signIn(checked.userId, checked.address);
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'signin-email-verify', { api_route: ROUTE });
    return refusal('failed', { status: 500 });
  }
}

/** A right code for an account's email way: the session as that account, the flow cookie cleared. */
async function signIn(userId: number, address: string): Promise<NextResponse> {
  const account = await emailSignInAccount(userId, address);
  if (!account) {
    console.warn(`[signin-email] user ${userId}: the email way was removed after the code was sent; no session`);
    return refusal('restart', { clearFlow: true });
  }
  const finished = await finishSignIn(account.user, 'email', { respond: 'json' });
  const outcome = (await finished.clone().json()) as { ok?: boolean; status?: SignInStatus };
  if (!outcome.ok) {
    console.log(`[signin-email] user ${userId} refused at the finish (${outcome.status ?? 'no status'})`);
    const error: VerifyError = outcome.status === 'suspended' || outcome.status === 'blocked' ? outcome.status : 'failed';
    return refusal(error, { clearFlow: true, status: error === 'failed' ? 500 : 200 });
  }
  try {
    await touchEmailSignIn(account.identityId);
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'signin-email-touch', { api_route: ROUTE, user_id: userId });
  }
  clearFlowCookie(finished);
  console.log(`[signin-email] user ${userId} signed in with an email code`);
  return finished;
}

/**
 * A right sign-up code (web sign-up spec §3.2): the person proved this address, and no account had it when the code
 * went out. Looked up again, since a way may have been added since: an account that signs in with it now signs in as
 * usual; a way that shows it (a Google way) answers 'exists' with that way, so the page says to use it; otherwise the
 * email flow is used up and the sign-up flow starts under a new famcal_signin cookie (kept: only the finished
 * sign-up clears it), and the answer names the sign-up page.
 */
async function signUpNext(request: NextRequest, flow: EmailFlow, address: string): Promise<NextResponse> {
  const account = await findEmailSignIn(address);
  if (account) {
    console.log(`[signin-email] a right sign-up code for an address user ${account.userId} signs in with now: signing in`);
    return signIn(account.userId, account.address);
  }
  const way = await findWayByAddress(address);
  if (way) {
    console.log(`[signin-email] a right sign-up code for an address user ${way.userId}'s ${way.kind} way shows: no sign-up`);
    return refusal('exists', { clearFlow: true, way: way.kind });
  }
  if (!(await takeFlow(request, ['email']))) {
    console.warn('[signin-email] a right sign-up code, but the email flow was used meanwhile: start again');
    return refusal('restart');
  }
  const response = NextResponse.json({ ok: true, redirect: signUpPageUrl(flow.locale) });
  await startFlow(response, { kind: 'signup', way: 'email', subject: address, address, locale: flow.locale });
  console.log('[signin-email] a right sign-up code: the sign-up page is next');
  return response;
}
```

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md` §2.1, §2.2, §2.3, §2.6, §2.20, §2.22, §3.3, §3.4, §3.8, §8 "Sign-up". Contract: `6c1/plan/contract.md` "Sign-up flow (Task 5)". All commands run from `/Users/razielgershoni/development/famcalbot` on `feat/web-sign-up`; `$RUN <name>` is the header's single-smoke runner (rulings Global #9). `ci-smokes.sh` runs every `scripts/smoke-*.ts` by glob, so a new smoke needs no listing.

1. **Task 4 already wrote the sign-up flow's base** (rulings #2, #3): `SignUpFlow` (with `startedAt?: number`, since `startFlow` reads it on every member of the union) and its place in `SignInFlow`, the `signup` branch of `asFlow`, `inviteOf` (the one reader of `invite` from a stored record) in `flow.ts`, `cleanInviteToken` in `src/lib/invite-token.ts`, `signUpHref` in `src/site/signin.ts` and `signUpPageUrl` in `web-session.ts` (built from `signUpHref`). This task adds only the `peekFlow` overloads, `invite?` on `OidcFlow` and `EmailFlow`, and `...inviteOf(v)` in their two `asFlow` branches (Step 3). It imports `signUpPageUrl` and defines none of these again.
2. **The `'new'` answer starts in `matchCalendarAccount`.** Its `no-account` today covers both "no holder" and "a holder that doesn't match". `CalendarMatch` gains `{ status: 'new' }`, given only when the filtered holder query finds nobody AND one `prisma.user.count({ where: { googleAccountKey: key } })` finds nobody either (a holder with its switch off or no token still blocks sign-up). No key (SESSION_SECRET unset) and no verified address stay `no-account`. `resolveGoogleSignIn` then turns `new` into `exists` (an email way shows the address) or `no-account` (a Google way of another sub shows it: not "exists", since that page would say "use Google", which is what the person just did) or keeps `new`. A calendar connected before 6b has no `googleAccountKey`, so its owner is offered sign-up until they press "Turn on"; the owner's pre-announcement step for that is in Part H's owner setup section (its Part 3, ruling #19), not here.
3. **The Google ban check is one call at the top of `resolveGoogleSignIn`:** `isIdentifierBlocked({ googleSub: claims.sub, email: normalizeEmail(verified address) })` → `{ status: 'blocked' }`, for a sign-in and a sign-up alike (contract "Bans": "A Google sign-up or sign-in also checks the verified email"). It relies on Task 4's `findWayByAddress` returning the email way when both an email way and a Google way show the address (the contract's wording order); `smoke-signin-oidc #25` pins that case.
4. **`SignInStatus` gains `'exists-email' | 'exists-google'`** (alerts above the ways on /signin, `site.signin.status.existsEmail` / `existsGoogle`). The Google callback's `exists` goes to `exists-email`. Task 4's verify answer `{ ok: false, error: 'exists', way: 'google' }` is turned into a page only here: `SignInClient` navigates to `/signin?status=exists-google` (or `exists-email`) (Step 14, ruling #6: one page for both ways, and /signup reuses its words). Task 4 adds no client handling and no `codeExistsGoogle` key. `/signup`'s exists view reuses the same two strings.
5. **The POST answers use finishSignIn's json key, `status`:** `{ ok: true, redirect }` | `{ ok: false, status: 'name' | 'restart' | 'blocked' | 'suspended' | 'limit' | 'taken' | 'failed' }` | `{ ok: false, status: 'exists', way }`. `taken` is shown on /signup with its own words (`site.signup.takenTitle`/`taken`) instead of navigating to 6b's `?status=taken`, whose words are Google-only ("This Google account is already in use") and wrong for an email sign-up. The new-accounts cap answers `limit` (429) only for a real refusal: `allowNewAccount`'s `store-down` (Redis failing) is `failed` (503), since a database outage is no rate limit (ruling #21).
6. **`POST /api/auth/signup` takes `{ name, locale }`.** The spec makes the account's language "the language of the page it signed up on"; the person may switch /signup's language after the sign-in started, so the page sends its own. An unknown `locale` falls back to the flow's.
7. **`finishSignIn` page:** this task lands on the dashboard: `const finished = await finishSignIn(user, flow.way, { respond: 'json' }); … return done(finished);`. Task 11 Step 9 changes that one call to `{ respond: 'json', page: landingPage(flow.invite) }` and keeps `done()` (ruling G #13). The invite is already carried in the record here.
8. **`onClaims` may return `{ response, keepFlowCookie: true }`** (`export type ClaimsAnswer` in `oidc-route.ts`); one call site (`done` is skipped for it).
9. **`isUniqueViolation`** (`identities.ts:47`) becomes exported so `signup.ts` reads a P2002 the one way the repo does.
10. **Client-safe helpers in `src/site/signin.ts` added here:** `SIGNUP_NAME_MAX = 60` (the server's `cleanName` and the page's length hint share it), `type SignUpWays = 'google' | 'email' | 'both'`, `signUpWays(google, email)`. They go after Task 4's `signUpHref`.
11. **/signin copy, hidden while sign-up is closed.** Sign-up is open on /signin when Google sign-in is configured, or email is and `turnstileConfigured()` (Task 3). Only then: `site.signin.newAccount` replaces `existingOnly`, and the no-account page leads with `status.noAccount.webAccount` and shows `status.noAccount.newHereSignUp` instead of `newHere`. With nothing open the page reads as today. The email form's sent line is Task 4's `emailSentOpen` (keyed on `turnstileSiteKey`, ruling #6); this task adds no sent line and no `SignInClient` prop.
12. **The `webAccount` line shows on every no-account page while sign-up is open** (ruling #23): the spec places it on the Telegram no-account page, but the page can't tell which way led to it, and the line is true for every way.
13. **A signed-in browser never sees the /signup form** (Rf1): the page sends a valid `__Host-famcal_session` to its calendar exactly as /signin does (cookie signature and age only, no database), a page the browser restores with Back (the back-forward cache) reloads so that check runs, and `POST /api/auth/signup` with a session but no sign-up record answers `restart` and makes nothing.
14. **The typed name stays out of Sentry** (ruling #15): `name` joins `SECRET_BODY_FIELDS`, `SECRET_JSON_MEMBER` and `SECRET_FORM_FIELD` in `src/lib/sentry-scrub.ts`, so every request body loses its `name` field (a calendar's name too, which is fine: no Sentry field holds a name). `smoke-sentry-scrub` #1 and #2 used `name` as their "kept" field; they keep a `color` field instead, and #13 pins `name` (Step 8a).
15. **Existing smokes whose expectations change:** `smoke-signin-calendar-match #10` (a row with no key, or an old key) and `#12` (after removing the way or the calendar row, the key is cleared) now answer `new`, since no account holds the key at all; `smoke-signin-oidc #25` (an unknown sub whose verified email is another account's email way) now lands on `status=exists-email`, still with no session; `smoke-sentry-scrub` #1, #2 and #13 (note 14). All are updated in this task.
16. **`scripts/lib/signin-world.ts` grows a fake Redis clock only** (`advanceRedis(ms)`: a key set with `ex`/`px` is gone at its next read once its time is up; nothing changes for smokes that never advance it). `request(url, { ip })` is Task 3's (ruling #11); this task only calls it.
17. **`smoke-signin-page`'s `configure()` leaves the Turnstile names alone unless `turnstile` is given:** Task 3's P9 sets them in `process.env` and then calls `configure({ google, email })`, so clearing them by default would break it. A check that needs them off says `turnstile: false`.

**Design (frontend-design, applied to mirror /signin).** The brief pins the look: /signin's own parts, so no new palette or type. Tokens used: `--ch-bg` (page), `--ch-card` (panel), `--ch-surface` (notice), `--ch-accent` (links, the address), `--ch-muted` (notes, consent), `--ch-danger` (field error); the site's system font stack; one 560 px column (`.site-signin`), left-aligned in the reading direction (logical properties, so Hebrew mirrors with no override).

```
┌ site header ───────────────────────────┐
│ Create your FamCal account        (h1) │
│ No FamCal account uses dana@gmail.com  │  ← the one emphasised element: the address the person
│ yet.                            (lead) │    proved, accent + 600, LTR-isolated (<bdi dir="ltr">),
│ ┌ notice ────────────────────────────┐ │    wrapping anywhere (no overflow at 320 px)
│ │ Already use FamCal in Telegram …   │ │
│ └────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│ ┌ panel ─────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ Your name                  (label) │ │
│ │ [_____________________] 16 px, auto│ │
│ │ Your partner sees it.       (note) │ │
│ │ (error line, danger, role=alert)   │ │
│ │ By creating an account … Terms …   │ │
│ │ [      Create account      ] 52 px │ │
│ │ Use another way             (link) │ │
│ └────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└ site footer ───────────────────────────┘
```

Principle: one memorable thing (the proved address), everything else is /signin's quiet kit. No icon beyond the Lucide `Loader2` spinner (as /signin's submit buttons), no hover, every target 44 px or more, the spinner stops under reduced motion (the existing `.site-spin` rule). Loading, failure (with Try again), expired, exists and taken each have their own state; a busy Create account clears on every failure with the reason in words.

```ts
// ---- Fake Upstash Redis (it parses JSON on read). An unknown command throws, so a smoke shows what it needs. ----

export const redisStore = new Map<string, string>();
/** The sets the capped-set Lua script (Task 3's Add email account limit) keeps; a set is no string, so it lives apart. */
const redisSets = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
const decode = (raw: string | undefined) => {
  if (raw === undefined) return null;
  try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch { return raw; }
};
const encode = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v));
const glob = (pattern: string) => new RegExp(`^${pattern.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '.*').replace(/\?/g, '.')}$`);
const incrBy = (k: string, n: number) => {
  const next = Number(redisStore.get(k) ?? 0) + n;
  redisStore.set(k, String(next));
  return next;
};
const redisImpl: Row = {
  get: async (k: string) => decode(redisStore.get(k)),
  set: async (k: string, v: unknown, o?: Row) => {
    if (o?.nx && redisStore.has(k)) return null;
    redisStore.set(k, encode(v));
    return 'OK';

  del: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().reduce((n: number, k) => n + (redisStore.delete(String(k)) ? 1 : 0), 0),

  getdel: async (k: string) => { const raw = redisStore.get(k); redisStore.delete(k); return decode(raw); },
```

After:

```ts
// ---- Fake Upstash Redis (it parses JSON on read). An unknown command throws, so a smoke shows what it needs. ----

export const redisStore = new Map<string, string>();
/** The sets the capped-set Lua script (Task 3's Add email account limit) keeps; a set is no string, so it lives apart. */
const redisSets = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
/**
 * When a key set with `ex` or `px` runs out, on the fake clock: Date.now() plus what advanceRedis() added. A key past
 * its time is gone at its next read, as Redis expires it. A smoke that never advances the clock sees no change.
 */
const redisExpiry = new Map<string, number>();
let redisOffsetMs = 0;
/** Moves the fake Redis clock on by `ms` (a 10-minute record is gone after advanceRedis(601_000)). resetWorld() sets it back. */
export function advanceRedis(ms: number): void {
  redisOffsetMs += ms;
}
/** Whether the key is there now: one past its expiry is removed first. */
const live = (k: string): boolean => {
  const at = redisExpiry.get(k);
  if (at !== undefined && at <= Date.now() + redisOffsetMs) {
    redisStore.delete(k);
    redisExpiry.delete(k);
  }
  return redisStore.has(k);
};
const decode = (raw: string | undefined) => {
  if (raw === undefined) return null;
  try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch { return raw; }
};
const encode = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v));
const glob = (pattern: string) => new RegExp(`^${pattern.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '.*').replace(/\?/g, '.')}$`);
const incrBy = (k: string, n: number) => {
  const next = Number((live(k) ? redisStore.get(k) : undefined) ?? 0) + n;
  redisStore.set(k, String(next));
  return next;
};
const redisImpl: Row = {
  get: async (k: string) => (live(k) ? decode(redisStore.get(k)) : null),
  set: async (k: string, v: unknown, o?: Row) => {
    if (o?.nx && live(k)) return null;
    redisStore.set(k, encode(v));
    // SET without EX/PX drops a key's expiry, as Redis does
    const ttlMs = typeof o?.ex === 'number' ? o.ex * 1000 : typeof o?.px === 'number' ? o.px : null;
    if (ttlMs === null) redisExpiry.delete(k);
    else redisExpiry.set(k, Date.now() + redisOffsetMs + ttlMs);
    return 'OK';
  },
  del: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().reduce((n: number, k) => { redisExpiry.delete(String(k)); return n + (redisStore.delete(String(k)) ? 1 : 0); }, 0),
  // Reads and deletes in one tick, as GETDEL does.
  getdel: async (k: string) => { const raw = live(k) ? redisStore.get(k) : undefined; redisStore.delete(k); redisExpiry.delete(k); return decode(raw); },
  incr: async (k: string) => incrBy(k, 1),
  incrby: async (k: string, n: number) => incrBy(k, Number(n)),
  decr: async (k: string) => incrBy(k, -1),
  expire: async (k: string) => (live(k) ? 1 : 0),
  pexpire: async (k: string) => (live(k) ? 1 : 0),
  expireat: async (k: string) => (live(k) ? 1 : 0),
  ttl: async (k: string) => (live(k) ? 600 : -2),
  pttl: async (k: string) => (live(k) ? 600_000 : -2),
  exists: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().filter(k => live(String(k))).length,
  mget: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().map(k => (live(String(k)) ? decode(redisStore.get(String(k))) : null)),
```

```ts
//  - S8 a way taken in the meantime: taken
//  - S9 / S10 the account: one user, one way, one primary FamCal calendar, the page's language, the session's method
//  - S11 bans at Create account (a Google sub, a Google sign-up's address, an email address)
//  - S12 5 new accounts a day per IPv4 address or IPv6 /48; no address is not counted and is logged
//  - S13 an address already in use, both ways round: exists, on GET and on Create account
//  - S14 Create account from another site is refused and the record stays
//  - S15 a sign-up record under the cookie is not a Google flow: the callback says restart and leaves it
//  - S16 a browser that holds a session but no sign-up record: GET and Create account are restart, and nothing is made
//  - S17 the new-accounts cap's store failing (Redis down) is failed (503), not limit, and nothing is made
//  - S18 a Sentry error event of POST /api/auth/signup holds no name (its body as an object, JSON, cut-off JSON or a form)
//  - S19 no console line or Sentry report holds an address, a sub, a name or a cookie value
//
// Real: the Google callback, oidc-route, google-signin, calendar-account, identities, flow, signup, the signup route,
// user-service's createAccount, the native calendar onboarding, user-moderation, limits, finishSignIn, session-auth,
// sentry-scrub.
// Faked at the boundaries (scripts/lib/signin-world.ts): Prisma and Redis in memory (Redis with its expiry clock),
// error capture, Telegram, the OIDC exchange (scripted claims), the calendar's Google account, fetch. No network, no DB.
//
// Run with the fake env of scripts/ci-smokes.sh:
//   bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-razielgershoni-development-famcalbot/0d239296-a217-49f9-8833-757c9d9a2df6/scratchpad/6c1/run-smoke.sh smoke-signup

import crypto from 'crypto';
import {
  advanceRedis, assert, baseUser, body, check, DB, everyCapture, everyLog, fakeRedis, flowCookie, identityRow,
  installSigninWorld, load, logs, redisStore, report, request, resetWorld, show, world, type Row,
} from './lib/signin-world';

const TAL = 9;
const TAL_TG = 111111111;
const NOA = 7;
const NOA_TG = 222222222;
const DANA = { sub: 'g-dana-sub-7781', email: 'dana@gmail.com' };
const NAME = 'Dana Levi';
const INVITE = 'ab'.repeat(32);

async function main() {
  await installSigninWorld();
  /** A module this task adds: null (logged) until it exists, so every check runs and says what is missing. */
  const soft = async (rel: string): Promise<Row | null> => {
    try {
      return await load(rel);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`[smoke] ${rel} did not load: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message.split('\n')[0] : String(error)}`);
      return null;
    }
  };
  const callbackRoute = await load('app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts');
  const account = await load('src/services/web-signin/calendar-account.ts');
  const { SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, createSessionToken, validateSessionToken } = await load('src/lib/session-auth.ts');
  const { SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME, peekFlow } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
  const signupRoute = await soft('app/api/auth/signup/route.ts');
  const signup = await soft('src/services/web-signin/signup.ts');
  const need = (mod: Row | null, what: string): Row => {
    assert(mod, `${what} does not exist yet`);
    return mod;
  };

  const KEY_TAL: string = account.googleAccountKey('tal@gmail.com');

  function seed(): void {
    resetWorld();
    DB.user = [
      baseUser({ id: TAL, name: 'Tal', telegramId: BigInt(TAL_TG), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-tal', googleAccountKey: KEY_TAL }),
      baseUser({ id: NOA, name: 'Noa', telegramId: BigInt(NOA_TG) }),
    ];
    DB.signInIdentity = [identityRow({ userId: NOA, kind: 'email', subject: 'noa@example.com', address: 'noa@example.com' })];
    DB.nativeCalendar = [];
    DB.blockedIdentifier = [];
    world.accounts = { 'rt-tal': 'tal@gmail.com' };
  }
  const userRow = (id: number): Row => DB.user.find(u => u.id === id) as Row;
  const usersNamed = (name: string): Row[] => DB.user.filter(u => u.name === name);
  const ban = (row: Row): void => {
    DB.blockedIdentifier = [{ id: 1, telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null, googleSub: null, email: null, reason: null, createdAt: new Date(), ...row }];
  };

  const location = (res: Row): string => res.headers.get('location') ?? '';
  const setCookie = (res: Row, name: string): string => ((res.headers.getSetCookie?.() ?? []) as string[]).find(c => c.startsWith(`${name}=`)) ?? '';
  const flowValue = (res: Row): string => setCookie(res, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME).split(';')[0].slice(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME.length + 1);
  const flowCleared = (res: Row): boolean => {
    const c = setCookie(res, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME);
    return /^famcal_signin=;/.test(c) && /Max-Age=0/i.test(c);
  };
  /** The flow record a famcal_signin value names, or null. */
  const recordOf = (value: string): Row | null => {
    const raw = redisStore.get(`signin:flow:${crypto.createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex')}`);
    return raw === undefined ? null : JSON.parse(raw);
  };
  const anySignUpRecord = (): boolean => [...redisStore.entries()].some(([k, v]) => k.startsWith('signin:flow:') && v.includes('"signup"'));
  const sessionOf = (res: Row) => {
    const value = res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value;
    return value ? validateSessionToken(value) : null;
  };

  let flows = 0;
  /** "Continue with Google" back on the callback with these claims (verified), from a sign-in begun in `locale`. */
  const googleCallback = async (claims: Row, o: { locale?: string; invite?: unknown } = {}) => {
    const state = `st-${++flows}`;
    const cookie = await flowCookie({ kind: 'google', state, nonce: `n-${flows}`, codeVerifier: 'v'.repeat(43), locale: o.locale ?? 'en', ...(o.invite !== undefined ? { invite: o.invite } : {}) });
    world.claims = { emailVerified: true, ...claims };
    return callbackRoute.GET(request(`/api/auth/google/callback?code=c-${flows}&state=${state}`, { cookie }));
  };
  /** A sign-up record as the callback or the email verify leaves it, and its cookie header. */
  const signUpFlow = (o: Row = {}) => flowCookie({ kind: 'signup', way: 'google', subject: DANA.sub, address: DANA.email, locale: 'en', ...o });
  const view = async (cookie?: string) => body(await need(signupRoute, 'GET /api/auth/signup').GET(request('/api/auth/signup', { cookie })));
  const create = (cookie: string | undefined, b: unknown, o: { ip?: string | null; origin?: string | null } = {}) =>
    need(signupRoute, 'POST /api/auth/signup').POST(request('/api/auth/signup', { body: b, cookie, ...o }));

  // ---- Google: when it asks for sign-up ----

  await check('S1 a Google sign-in no account holds in any way starts the sign-up: the callback goes to /en/signup with a live famcal_signin (43 characters, HttpOnly, Secure, Lax, Path=/api/auth, 10 minutes) whose record holds the way, the sub, the address and the language; no session, no account, no way; the invite rides along in Hebrew, and a malformed one is dropped', async () => {
    seed();
    const users = DB.user.length;
    const res = await googleCallback(DANA);
    assert(location(res) === 'https://famcal.bot/en/signup', `location ${location(res)}`);
    const cookie = setCookie(res, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME);
    const value = flowValue(res);
    assert(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(value) && /Path=\/api\/auth/i.test(cookie) && /Max-Age=600/i.test(cookie) && /HttpOnly/i.test(cookie) && /Secure/i.test(cookie) && /SameSite=lax/i.test(cookie), `famcal_signin ${cookie}`);
    const record = recordOf(value);
    assert(record?.kind === 'signup' && record.way === 'google' && record.subject === DANA.sub && record.address === DANA.email && record.locale === 'en' && typeof record.startedAt === 'number' && !('invite' in record), `record ${show(record)}`);
    assert(!sessionOf(res) && DB.user.length === users && DB.signInIdentity.length === 1, 'an account, a way or a session was made');
    const he = await googleCallback(DANA, { locale: 'he', invite: INVITE });
    assert(location(he) === 'https://famcal.bot/he/signup' && recordOf(flowValue(he))?.invite === INVITE, `he ${location(he)} ${show(recordOf(flowValue(he)))}`);
    const bad = await googleCallback(DANA, { invite: 'not-a-token' });
    const badRecord = recordOf(flowValue(bad));
    assert(badRecord?.kind === 'signup' && !('invite' in badRecord), `a malformed invite rode along: ${show(badRecord)}`);
  });

  await check('S2 a calendar holder that does not match keeps the no-account page (a live check that disagrees, its switch off, another Google way), and two holders keep several: no sign-up record, the flow cookie cleared, no session', async () => {
    const cases: [string, () => void, string][] = [
      ['a live check that disagrees', () => { world.accounts['rt-tal'] = 'someone@gmail.com'; }, 'no-account'],
      ['a holder whose sign-in switch is off', () => { userRow(TAL).googleCalendarSignIn = false; }, 'no-account'],
      ['a holder that has another Google way', () => { DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-old', address: 'old@gmail.com' })); }, 'no-account'],
      ['two holders', () => { DB.user.push(baseUser({ id: 10, name: 'Family', telegramId: BigInt(333333333), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-family', googleAccountKey: KEY_TAL })); }, 'several'],
    ];
    for (const [name, setup, status] of cases) {
      seed();
      setup();
      const res = await googleCallback({ sub: 'g-tal-new', email: 'tal@gmail.com' });
      assert(location(res) === `https://famcal.bot/en/signin?status=${status}`, `${name}: ${location(res)}`);
      assert(flowCleared(res) && !anySignUpRecord() && !sessionOf(res), `${name}: a sign-up record, a live cookie or a session`);
    }
  });

  await check('S3 a Google sign-in whose verified address is another account\'s email way lands on /signin?status=exists-email: no sign-up record, no session, and that email way is not touched', async () => {
    seed();
    const res = await googleCallback({ sub: 'g-noa', email: 'noa@example.com' });
    assert(location(res) === 'https://famcal.bot/en/signin?status=exists-email', `location ${location(res)}`);
    assert(flowCleared(res) && !anySignUpRecord() && !sessionOf(res) && DB.signInIdentity[0].lastUsedAt === null, 'a record, a session, or the way touched');
  });

  await check('S4 bans at Google: a banned Google sub and a banned address (a would-be sign-up), and a sign-in by an existing Google way whose verified address is banned, each land on status=blocked with no record and no session', async () => {
    for (const [name, row] of [['sub', { googleSub: DANA.sub }], ['address', { email: DANA.email }]] as const) {
      seed();
      ban(row);
      const res = await googleCallback(DANA);
      assert(location(res) === 'https://famcal.bot/en/signin?status=blocked' && flowCleared(res) && !anySignUpRecord() && !sessionOf(res), `${name}: ${location(res)}`);
    }
    seed();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-tal', address: 'tal.work@gmail.com' }));
    ban({ email: 'tal.work@gmail.com' });
    const res = await googleCallback({ sub: 'g-tal', email: 'tal.work@gmail.com' });
    assert(location(res) === 'https://famcal.bot/en/signin?status=blocked' && !sessionOf(res), `sign-in: ${location(res)}`);
  });

  // ---- The record ----

  await check('S5 the record: GET reads it without using it up ({ way, address }, twice, no-store); Create account takes it, so a second one, and a GET after it, are restart; no cookie is restart; another kind\'s flow under the cookie is restart and is left for its own step', async () => {
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow();
    const first = await need(signupRoute, 'GET /api/auth/signup').GET(request('/api/auth/signup', { cookie }));
    assert((first.headers.get('cache-control') ?? '').includes('no-store'), `cache ${first.headers.get('cache-control')}`);
    assert(show(await body(first)) === show({ way: 'google', address: DANA.email }) && show(await view(cookie)) === show({ way: 'google', address: DANA.email }), 'the view');
    const made = await body(await create(cookie, { name: NAME }));
    assert(made.ok === true, `made ${show(made)}`);
    const again = await body(await create(cookie, { name: NAME }));
    assert(show(again) === show({ ok: false, status: 'restart' }) && usersNamed(NAME).length === 1, `again ${show(again)}`);
    assert(show(await view(cookie)) === show({ restart: true }), 'GET after the take');
    assert(show(await view()) === show({ restart: true }) && show(await body(await create(undefined, { name: NAME }))) === show({ ok: false, status: 'restart' }), 'no cookie');
    const emailFlow = await flowCookie({ kind: 'email', emailKey: 'k'.repeat(32), locale: 'en' });
    assert(show(await view(emailFlow)) === show({ restart: true }) && show(await body(await create(emailFlow, { name: NAME }))) === show({ ok: false, status: 'restart' }), 'an email flow');
    assert((await peekFlow(request('/api/auth/email/verify', { cookie: emailFlow }), 'email'))?.emailKey === 'k'.repeat(32), 'the email flow was used up');
  });

  await check('S6 the record lives 10 minutes: after them GET and Create account are restart and no account is made', async () => {
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow();
    advanceRedis(601_000);
    assert(show(await view(cookie)) === show({ restart: true }), 'GET after 10 minutes');
    assert(show(await body(await create(cookie, { name: NAME }))) === show({ ok: false, status: 'restart' }) && usersNamed(NAME).length === 0, 'Create account after 10 minutes');
  });

  await check('S7 the name: trimmed, 1 to 60 characters (counted as characters, so 60 emoji pass); empty, blank, 61 characters, a C0 or C1 control, a direction mark, override or isolate, Arabic\'s letter mark, a zero-width character, a lone surrogate, or not text is refused with status=name (400) before the record is touched: it still answers, and a good name then works', async () => {
    const s = need(signup, 'signup.ts');
    assert(s.cleanName('  דנה לוי  ') === 'דנה לוי' && s.cleanName('x'.repeat(60)) === 'x'.repeat(60) && s.cleanName('😀'.repeat(60)) === '😀'.repeat(60) && s.cleanName('Дана') === 'Дана', 'a good name refused');
    const bad: unknown[] = [
      '', '   ', 'x'.repeat(61), '😀'.repeat(61), 'Da\u0007na', 'Da\nna', 'Da\u007Fna', 'Da\u0085na', 'Da\u202Ena', 'Da\u202Ana', 'Da\u2066na', 'Da\u2069na',
      'Da\u200Ena', 'Da\u200Fna', 'Da\u061Cna', 'Da\u200Bna', 'Da\u200Dna', 'Da\u2060na', 'Da\uFEFFna', 'Da\u2028na', 'Da\uD800na', 42, null, ['Dana'],
    ];
    for (const input of bad) assert(s.cleanName(input) === null, `cleanName accepted ${show(input)}`);
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow();
    for (const input of [...bad, undefined]) {
      const res = await create(cookie, input === undefined ? {} : { name: input });
      const answer = await body(res);
      assert(res.status === 400 && show(answer) === show({ ok: false, status: 'name' }), `${show(input)}: ${res.status} ${show(answer)}`);
    }
    assert(show(await view(cookie)) === show({ way: 'google', address: DANA.email }) && DB.user.length === 2, 'a refused name used the record or made an account');
    assert((await body(await create(cookie, { name: `  ${NAME} ` }))).ok === true && usersNamed(NAME).length === 1, 'a good name after the refusals');
  });

  await check('S8 a way taken in the meantime (another account got this Google sub, under another address) is status=taken: no session, the flow cookie cleared, still one way with that sub', async () => {
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: NOA, kind: 'google', subject: DANA.sub, address: 'dana.old@gmail.com' }));
    const res = await create(cookie, { name: NAME });
    assert(show(await body(res)) === show({ ok: false, status: 'taken' }) && !sessionOf(res) && flowCleared(res), `taken ${show(await body(res))}`);
    assert(DB.signInIdentity.filter(i => i.subject === DANA.sub).length === 1, 'a second way with that sub');
  });

  // ---- The account ----

  await check('S9 the account, Google: one user (the trimmed name, no Telegram or WhatsApp, the page\'s language he), one Google way (the sub and the address), one primary FamCal calendar; the session cookie for it with method google; the answer names /he/dashboard; the flow cookie cleared', async () => {
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow();
    const res = await create(cookie, { name: ` ${NAME} `, locale: 'he' });
    const answer = await body(res);
    const [user] = usersNamed(NAME);
    assert(user && DB.user.length === 3, `users ${show(DB.user.map(u => u.name))}`);
    assert(user.telegramId == null && user.whatsappPhone == null && user.whatsappBsuid == null && user.language === 'he', `user ${show(user)}`);
    assert(show(answer) === show({ ok: true, redirect: `https://famcal.bot/he/dashboard?user_id=${user.id}` }), `answer ${show(answer)}`);
    const session = sessionOf(res);
    assert(session?.userId === user.id && session.method === 'google', `session ${show(session)}`);
    const ways = DB.signInIdentity.filter(i => i.userId === user.id);
    assert(ways.length === 1 && ways[0].kind === 'google' && ways[0].subject === DANA.sub && ways[0].address === DANA.email, `ways ${show(ways)}`);
    const calendars = (DB.nativeCalendar ?? []).filter(c => c.ownerUserId === user.id);
    assert(calendars.length === 1, `calendars ${show(calendars)}`);
    assert(flowCleared(res), 'the flow cookie stays');
  });

  await check('S10 the account, email: one user in the sign-in\'s language when the page sends none (or one that is not ours), one email way (the normalised address as subject and address), one calendar, the session with method email', async () => {
    for (const locale of [undefined, 'xx']) {
      seed();
      const cookie = await signUpFlow({ way: 'email', subject: 'rivka@example.com', address: 'rivka@example.com', locale: 'ru' });
      const res = await create(cookie, locale === undefined ? { name: 'Rivka' } : { name: 'Rivka', locale });
      const [user] = usersNamed('Rivka');
      assert(user && user.language === 'ru' && (await body(res)).redirect === `https://famcal.bot/ru/dashboard?user_id=${user.id}`, `${show(locale)}: ${show(user)} ${show(await body(res))}`);
      const session = sessionOf(res);
      assert(session?.userId === user.id && session.method === 'email', `session ${show(session)}`);
      const ways = DB.signInIdentity.filter(i => i.userId === user.id);
      assert(ways.length === 1 && ways[0].kind === 'email' && ways[0].subject === 'rivka@example.com' && ways[0].address === 'rivka@example.com', `ways ${show(ways)}`);
      assert((DB.nativeCalendar ?? []).filter(c => c.ownerUserId === user.id).length === 1, 'calendars');
    }
  });

  // ---- Refusals ----

  await check('S11 bans at Create account (one that came in the 10 minutes): a banned Google sub, a Google sign-up whose address is banned, and a banned email address are status=blocked (403) with no account and no session, and the record is used', async () => {
    const cases: [string, Row, Row][] = [
      ['Google sub', {}, { googleSub: DANA.sub }],
      ['Google address', {}, { email: DANA.email }],
      ['email address', { way: 'email', subject: 'rivka@example.com', address: 'rivka@example.com' }, { email: 'rivka@example.com' }],
    ];
    for (const [name, flow, row] of cases) {
      seed();
      const cookie = await signUpFlow(flow);
      ban(row);
      const res = await create(cookie, { name: NAME });
      assert(res.status === 403 && show(await body(res)) === show({ ok: false, status: 'blocked' }) && usersNamed(NAME).length === 0 && !sessionOf(res), `${name}: ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
      assert(show(await view(cookie)) === show({ restart: true }), `${name}: the record survived`);
    }
  });

  await check('S12 new accounts per internet address: 5 a day from one IPv4 address, the 6th is status=limit with no account; IPv6 counts by its /48 (5 from different /64s of one /48, the 6th refused, another /48 still works); no address skips the count and logs it', async () => {
    seed();
    const make = async (i: number, ip: string | null) => {
      const cookie = await signUpFlow({ way: 'email', subject: `p${i}@example.com`, address: `p${i}@example.com` });
      return body(await create(cookie, { name: `Person ${i}` }, { ip }));
    };
    for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) assert((await make(i, '198.51.100.7')).ok === true, `IPv4 #${i}`);
    assert(show(await make(6, '198.51.100.7')) === show({ ok: false, status: 'limit' }) && usersNamed('Person 6').length === 0, 'the 6th from one IPv4 address');
    for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) assert((await make(10 + i, `2001:db8:abcd:${i}::1`)).ok === true, `IPv6 #${i}`);
    assert(show(await make(16, '2001:db8:abcd:6::1')) === show({ ok: false, status: 'limit' }) && usersNamed('Person 16').length === 0, 'the 6th from one /48');
    assert((await make(17, '2001:db8:abce:1::1')).ok === true, 'another /48');
    logs.length = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) assert((await make(20 + i, null)).ok === true, `no address #${i}`);
    assert(logs.some(l => l.includes('[signup] no client address; the account cap is not counted')), `logs ${show(logs.filter(l => l.startsWith('[signup]')))}`);
  });

  await check('S13 an address already in use, both ways round: a Google sign-up whose address another account now signs in with by email code (exists email), and an email sign-up whose address another account\'s Google way shows (exists google), on GET and on Create account, with no account', async () => {
    seed();
    const google = await signUpFlow();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: NOA, kind: 'email', subject: DANA.email, address: DANA.email }));
    assert(show(await view(google)) === show({ exists: 'email' }), `GET ${show(await view(google))}`);
    assert(show(await body(await create(google, { name: NAME }))) === show({ ok: false, status: 'exists', way: 'email' }) && usersNamed(NAME).length === 0, 'Create account, Google');
    seed();
    const email = await signUpFlow({ way: 'email', subject: 'tal.work@gmail.com', address: 'tal.work@gmail.com' });
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-tal', address: 'tal.work@gmail.com' }));
    assert(show(await view(email)) === show({ exists: 'google' }), `GET ${show(await view(email))}`);
    assert(show(await body(await create(email, { name: NAME }))) === show({ ok: false, status: 'exists', way: 'google' }) && usersNamed(NAME).length === 0, 'Create account, email');
  });

  await check('S14 Create account from another site, or with no Origin, is refused (403) before anything is read, and the record stays', async () => {
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow();
    for (const origin of ['https://evil.example', null]) {
      const res = await create(cookie, { name: NAME }, { origin });
      assert(res.status === 403 && usersNamed(NAME).length === 0, `${origin}: ${res.status}`);
    }
    assert(show(await view(cookie)) === show({ way: 'google', address: DANA.email }), 'the record was used');
  });

  await check('S15 a sign-up record under the cookie is not a Google or Telegram flow: the Google callback says restart and leaves it for /signup', async () => {
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow();
    world.claims = { ...DANA, emailVerified: true };
    const res = await callbackRoute.GET(request('/api/auth/google/callback?code=c&state=s', { cookie }));
    assert(location(res) === 'https://famcal.bot/en/signin?status=restart', `location ${location(res)}`);
    assert(show(await view(cookie)) === show({ way: 'google', address: DANA.email }), 'the sign-up record was used');
  });

  await check('S16 a browser already signed in (a valid session cookie) but with no sign-up record: GET is restart, and Create account is restart with no account, no way and no new session cookie', async () => {
    seed();
    const users = DB.user.length;
    const ways = DB.signInIdentity.length;
    const session = `${SESSION_COOKIE_NAME}=${createSessionToken(TAL, 'google', Date.now())}`;
    assert(show(await view(session)) === show({ restart: true }), `GET ${show(await view(session))}`);
    const res = await create(session, { name: NAME });
    assert(show(await body(res)) === show({ ok: false, status: 'restart' }), `Create account ${show(await body(res))}`);
    assert(DB.user.length === users && DB.signInIdentity.length === ways && !res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME), 'an account, a way or a session cookie was made');
  });

  await check('S17 the new-accounts cap with its store failing (Redis down at the count): status=failed (503), not limit; no account, no session, the flow cookie cleared', async () => {
    seed();
    const cookie = await signUpFlow({ way: 'email', subject: 'rivka@example.com', address: 'rivka@example.com' });
    const realEval = fakeRedis.eval;
    fakeRedis.eval = async (script: string, keys: string[], args: string[]) => {
      if (String(keys[0]).includes('accounts-ip-day')) throw new Error('Redis is down (smoke)');
      return realEval(script, keys, args);
    };
    try {
      const res = await create(cookie, { name: 'Rivka' });
      assert(res.status === 503 && show(await body(res)) === show({ ok: false, status: 'failed' }), `${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
      assert(usersNamed('Rivka').length === 0 && !sessionOf(res) && flowCleared(res), 'an account, a session, or the flow cookie kept');
    } finally {
      fakeRedis.eval = realEval;
    }
  });

  await check('S18 a Sentry error event of POST /api/auth/signup holds no name: its body as an object or a JSON string loses the name, cut-off JSON and a form have it scrubbed; the language stays', async () => {
    const { scrubServerEvent } = await load('src/lib/sentry-scrub.ts');
    const dataOf = (data: unknown) => scrubServerEvent({ request: { url: 'https://famcal.bot/api/auth/signup', method: 'POST', data } }).request.data;
    const object = dataOf({ name: NAME, locale: 'he' });
    assert(show(object) === show({ locale: 'he' }), `object ${show(object)}`);
    const json = dataOf(JSON.stringify({ name: NAME, locale: 'he' }));
    assert(json === JSON.stringify({ locale: 'he' }), `JSON ${show(json)}`);
    const cut = dataOf(`{"locale":"he","name":"${NAME}","x":"a`);
    assert(String(cut) === '{"locale":"he","name":"[scrubbed]","x":"a', `cut-off JSON ${show(cut)}`);
    const form = dataOf(`name=${encodeURIComponent(NAME)}&locale=he`);
    assert(form === 'name=[scrubbed]&locale=he', `form ${show(form)}`);
  });

  await check('S19 no console line or Sentry report of the run holds an address, a Google sub, a name or a famcal_signin value', () => {
    const secrets = [DANA.email, DANA.sub, NAME, 'Rivka', 'rivka@example.com', 'tal.work@gmail.com', 'noa@example.com', 'p1@example.com'];
    const lines = [...everyLog, ...everyCapture.map(c => `${c.context} ${c.message} ${show(c.extra)}`)];
    const leaked = lines.filter(l => secrets.some(s => l.includes(s)) || /famcal_signin=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}/.test(l));
    assert(leaked.length === 0, `leaked ${show(leaked.slice(0, 5))}`);
  });

  report();
}

main().catch(err => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```ts
/** Reads this browser's email flow without using it up (GET): a wrong code leaves it for the next try. */
export async function peekFlow(request: NextRequest, kind: 'email'): Promise<EmailFlow | null> {
  const flowId = flowIdOf(request, kind);
  if (!flowId) return null;
  const flow = asFlow(await redis.get(recordKey(flowId)));
  if (!flow || flow.kind !== kind) {
    console.warn(`[signin-flow] ${kind}: no email sign-in under the cookie (used, or over 10 minutes)`);

  }

}
```

```ts
/**
 * Reads this browser's email flow or sign-up without using it up (GET): a wrong code leaves the email flow for the
 * next try, and /signup reads the sign-up as often as it is opened (Create account takes it, with takeFlow).
 */
export async function peekFlow(request: NextRequest, kind: 'email'): Promise<EmailFlow | null>;
export async function peekFlow(request: NextRequest, kind: 'signup'): Promise<SignUpFlow | null>;
export async function peekFlow(request: NextRequest, kind: 'email' | 'signup'): Promise<EmailFlow | SignUpFlow | null> {
  const flowId = flowIdOf(request, kind);
  if (!flowId) return null;
  const flow = asFlow(await redis.get(recordKey(flowId)));
  if (!flow || flow.kind !== kind) {
    console.warn(`[signin-flow] ${kind}: no ${kind === 'email' ? 'email sign-in' : 'sign-up'} under the cookie (used, or over 10 minutes)`);
    return null;
  }
  return flow as EmailFlow | SignUpFlow;
}
```

Before (`src/services/web-signin/google-signin.ts`, the whole file):

```ts
/**
 * Who a Google sign-in is (web sign-in spec §3, §2.17): the account that added this Google account (google, sub), else
 * the account whose calendar is connected from it (calendar-account.ts). The one call site for the Google callback's
 * account lookup.
 */

import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import type { GoogleClaims } from './oidc';
import { findUserByIdentity } from './identities';
import { matchCalendarAccount } from './calendar-account';

export type GoogleSignInResult = { user: UserConfig } | { status: 'no-account' | 'several' | 'failed' };

export async function resolveGoogleSignIn(claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<GoogleSignInResult> {
  const user = await findUserByIdentity('google', claims.sub);
  if (user) return { user };
  // No way added for this sub: the Google account a calendar is connected from (spec §2.17)

```

After:

```ts
/**
 * Who a Google sign-in is (web sign-in spec §3, §2.17; web sign-up spec §2.2, §2.8, §3.3): the account that added this
 * Google account (google, sub), else the account whose calendar is connected from it (calendar-account.ts), else
 * nobody, and then whether a new account may be made for it. The one call site for the Google callback's account
 * lookup.
 *
 * - 'blocked': the Google account (its sub) or its verified address is on the blocklist, for a sign-in and a sign-up
 *   alike (an account found by its sub is refused here, before finishSignIn's own check of its ways).
 * - 'new': no account holds this Google account in any way (no Google way with this sub, no calendar key for its
 *   address) and no way of another account shows the verified address: the callback starts the sign-up.
 * - 'exists' (way 'email'): the verified address is another account's email way. Its page says to sign in with a code
 *   and add Google in Settings. A check on an address Google just proved, never a sign-in by address.
 * - A Google way of another sub that shows the address stays 'no-account' (that page's words fit; "use Google" would
 *   be what the person just did).
 * No log line holds the sub or the address: the outcome and a user id only.
 */

import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import type { GoogleClaims } from './oidc';
import { isIdentifierBlocked } from '../../lib/user-moderation';
import { normalizeEmail } from './email-address';
import { findUserByIdentity, findWayByAddress } from './identities';
import { matchCalendarAccount } from './calendar-account';

export type GoogleSignInResult =
  | { user: UserConfig }
  | { status: 'no-account' | 'several' | 'failed' | 'blocked' | 'new' }
  | { status: 'exists'; way: 'email' };

export async function resolveGoogleSignIn(claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<GoogleSignInResult> {
  const address = claims.emailVerified ? normalizeEmail(claims.email) : null;
  if (await isIdentifierBlocked({ googleSub: claims.sub, email: address })) {
    console.warn('[signin] google: this Google account or its verified address is on the blocklist');
    return { status: 'blocked' };
  }
  const user = await findUserByIdentity('google', claims.sub);
  if (user) return { user };
  // No way added for this sub: the Google account a calendar is connected from (spec §2.17)
  const match = await matchCalendarAccount(claims);
  if (!('status' in match) || match.status !== 'new') return match;
  if (!address) {
    console.warn('[signin] google: the verified address is not one FamCal can keep; no sign-up');
    return { status: 'no-account' };
  }
  const held = await findWayByAddress(address);
  if (held?.kind === 'email') {
    console.log(`[signin] google: the verified address is user ${held.userId}'s email way; no sign-up`);
    return { status: 'exists', way: 'email' };
  }
  if (held) {
    console.warn(`[signin] google: the verified address shows on user ${held.userId}'s Google way of another Google account; no sign-up`);
    return { status: 'no-account' };
  }
  console.log('[signin] google: no FamCal account holds this Google account; the sign-up is offered');
  return { status: 'new' };
}
```

```ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { handleOidcCallback } from '@/src/services/web-signin/oidc-route';
import { resolveGoogleSignIn } from '@/src/services/web-signin/google-signin';
import { finishAddGoogle } from '@/src/services/web-signin/add-google';
import { finishSignIn, signInPageUrl } from '@/src/lib/web-session';

/**
 * GET /api/auth/google/callback: Google sends the browser back here, for "Continue with Google" on /signin and for
 * Settings' Add Google (an 'add-google' flow, web sign-in spec §2.9). Google must have verified the account's address
 * (for every kind of Google flow, so this check stays first). Then:
 *   - 'google' (sign in): the account is resolveGoogleSignIn's (the added Google account, else the one the calendar is
 *     connected from, §2.17), and finishSignIn signs it in or shows its page;
 *   - 'add-google': the Google account is attached to the account that made the link, the chat gets the notice, and
 *     this browser is signed in as that account (finishAddGoogle).
 */
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  return handleOidcCallback('google', request, ['google', 'add-google'], async (claims, flow) => {
    if (!claims.emailVerified || !claims.email) {
      console.warn(`[signin] google: the account's address is not verified (${flow.kind} flow)`);
      return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'failed'));
    }
    if (flow.kind === 'add-google') return finishAddGoogle(flow, claims);
    const found = await resolveGoogleSignIn(claims);
    if ('status' in found) return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, found.status));
    return finishSignIn(found.user, 'google');
  });
}
```
