Notes on the words: the Settings path in the guidance is the real labels (`settings.title`, `settings.signIn.title`, `settings.signIn.googleAdd` / `emailAdd`) in each language; "briefings" is the app's own word for the summaries (`settings.sections.summaries`: סיכומים, Сводки). Hebrew addresses the person in the plural imperative (חברו, פתחו, בחרו, הזינו, בקשו, נסו), as the bot does everywhere; Russian is formal (Подключайте, откройте, выберите, введите, получите, Попробуйте). `expired` doesn't name the Connect Telegram button (Task 9 words it), it says "get a new link". The name and the address go in through `fillHtml` (escaped) inside Unicode isolates (`isolateAuto` for the name, `isolateLtr` for the address), so an English address keeps its order in a Hebrew line.

- [ ] **Step 8: One welcome (`src/services/telegram/welcome.ts`, new)**

```ts
/**
 * The bot's welcome with the dashboard button: what /start answers when no deep link takes over, and the first message
 * after Connect Telegram (src/services/telegram-connect.ts). One builder, so both say the same and open the same page.
 *
 * - An admin gets both boards.
 * - With no place yet, the onboarding welcome with the Settings button: the place is the only setup that gates good
 *   summaries (everyone has FamCal, and Google is optional).
 * - Otherwise the welcome with the dashboard button.
 *
 * Every welcome ends with the Privacy Policy and the Terms, with no link preview (the notice that comes with the first
 * request for data). The name is the person's own and is escaped for HTML (a function replacement, so "$&" in a name stays text).
 */

import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import { buildUrl } from '../../config/urls';
import { getBotMessages } from '../../lib/bot-messages';
import { policyLinks } from '../../lib/plan-disclosure';
import { escapeHtml } from '../../utils/html';
import { MessagingPlatform, MessageFormat } from '../messaging/types';
import { getMessagingService } from './bot';

export async function sendWelcome(
  chatId: number | string,
  user: UserConfig,
  platform: MessagingPlatform = MessagingPlatform.TELEGRAM,
): Promise<void> {
  // The name is the person's own text and goes into HTML: escaped, so an "&" or a "<" in it can't make Telegram refuse the welcome
  const name = escapeHtml(user.name || 'there');
  const locale = user.language || 'en';
  const t = await getBotMessages(locale);
  const service = getMessagingService();
  const links = policyLinks(t.policy, locale, 'html');
  const dashboardUrl = buildUrl(`/${locale}/dashboard?user_id=${user.telegramId ?? user.id}`);
  const welcome = t.start.welcome.replace('{name}', () => name);

  if (user.isAdmin) {
    const adminUrl = buildUrl(`/${locale}/admin-panel?user_id=${user.telegramId ?? user.id}`);
    const message = `${welcome}\n\n${t.start.chooseBoard}\n\n${links}`;

    await service.sendMessage(chatId, message, {
      format: MessageFormat.HTML,
      disablePreview: true,
      replyMarkup: {
        inline_keyboard: [
          [{ text: t.start.userDashboard, web_app: { url: dashboardUrl } }],
          [{ text: t.start.adminPanel, web_app: { url: adminUrl } }]
        ]
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  if (!user.location) {
    const settingsUrl = buildUrl(`/${locale}/settings?user_id=${user.telegramId ?? user.id}`);
    const platformName = platform === MessagingPlatform.TELEGRAM ? 'Telegram' : 'WhatsApp';
    const nativeWelcome = t.onboarding.nativeWelcome
      .replace('{platform}', platformName)
      .replace('{name}', () => name);
    await service.sendMessage(chatId, `${nativeWelcome}\n\n${links}`, {
      format: MessageFormat.HTML,
      disablePreview: true,
      replyMarkup: {
        inline_keyboard: [[
          { text: t.onboarding.nativeLocationButton, web_app: { url: settingsUrl } }
        ]]
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  // Returning user: simple dashboard button
  const message = `${welcome}\n\n${t.start.tapButton}\n\n${links}`;

  await service.sendMessage(chatId, message, {
    format: MessageFormat.HTML,
    disablePreview: true,
    replyMarkup: {
      inline_keyboard: [[
        { text: t.start.dashboard, web_app: { url: dashboardUrl } }
      ]]
    }
  });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: `src/services/telegram-connect.ts` (new)**

```ts
/**
 * Connect Telegram (web sign-up spec §2.9, §3.6): an account made on famcal.bot, with no chat, takes on a Telegram id,
 * so reminders, briefings, Send to chat and Stars payments start working. The browser stays signed in.
 *
 * 1. The link. POST /api/telegram-connect makes it (createConnectLink): only for an account with no chat, only within
 *    an hour of signing in on this browser (a copied old session can't attach a Telegram, which can't be removed), at
 *    most 5 an hour per account. t.me/<bot>?start=w_<token>: 16 random bytes, kept 10 minutes as the sha256 of the
 *    token (REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnect), never in clear and never in a log line.
 * 2. /start w_<token> (handleConnectStart, called by /start before auto-registration and its breadcrumb): it reads the
 *    link without using it up. A Telegram with no FamCal account gets the question, naming the account and its FULL
 *    address (a masked one is easy to imitate), with Connect and Cancel; the buttons carry a random press id kept 10
 *    minutes and bound to the Telegram id asked (REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnectPress). A Telegram that has an account gets
 *    the guidance (Add Google or Add email there, by the browser account's way) and nothing is joined.
 * 3. Connect (handleConnectPress): both records are taken (GETDEL) and everything is checked again; the Telegram id is
 *    written onto the browser account (only while it still has no chat), then the menu button, feature access, the
 *    reminder cache, the welcome, and the notice to the ways the account had before (sendSignInNotice).
 *
 * Every reply is the answer to the person's own action, so the Shabbat pause doesn't hold it (scripts/smoke-pause.ts
 * lists this file as NOT_PAUSED). No log line names a token, a name or an address: the user id, the Telegram id and
 * the outcome only.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import enMessages from '../../messages/en.json';
import heMessages from '../../messages/he.json';
import ruMessages from '../../messages/ru.json';
import { redis } from '../utils/redis';
import { prisma } from '../utils/prisma';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '../config/redis-keys';
import { buildUrl } from '../config/urls';
import { normalizeLocale, type Locale } from '../utils/locale';
import { fillHtml } from '../utils/html';
import { isolateAuto, isolateLtr } from '../lib/bidi-isolate';
import { DEFAULT_BOT_USERNAME } from '../lib/gate-links';
import { hasChat } from '../lib/has-chat';
import type { WebSession } from '../lib/session-auth';
import { signInRefusal } from '../lib/web-session';
import { isIdentifierBlocked } from '../lib/user-moderation';
import type { UserConfig } from '../types';
import { getUserById, getUserByTelegramId } from './user-service';
import { MessageFormat, type MessageOptions } from './messaging/types';
import { syncReminderCacheEntry } from './reminder-cache';
import { invalidateDueGate } from './native-reminders/due-gate';
import { countWithin } from './web-signin/limits';
import { signinHash } from './web-signin/email-address';
import { identitiesOf, type IdentityKind } from './web-signin/identities';
import { sendSignInNotice } from './web-signin/notice';
import { captureSignInFailure, safeErrorSummary } from './web-signin/safe-error';

/** The link and the question both wait 10 minutes. */
const TTL_SECONDS = 10 * 60;
/** A link is made only this soon after signing in on the browser that asks. */
const RECENT_SIGN_IN_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
const LINKS_PER_HOUR = 5;
const HOUR_SEC = 60 * 60;
/** 16 random bytes as base64url */
const TOKEN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}$/;
/** 12 random bytes as base64url: `tgc:<id>` and `tgc-no:<id>` stay well inside Telegram's 64 bytes of callback data */
const PRESS_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16}$/;

type ConnectCopy = typeof enMessages.bot.connect.web;
const COPY: Record<Locale, ConnectCopy> = {
  en: enMessages.bot.connect.web,
  he: heMessages.bot.connect.web,
  ru: ruMessages.bot.connect.web,
};

const tokenHash = (token: string) => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex');

/** The reply language: the first account that has one, else Telegram's own language code. */
function localeOf(users: Array<UserConfig | null | undefined>, languageCode?: string): Locale {
  const user = users.find(u => u?.language);
  if (user) return normalizeLocale(user.language);
  if (languageCode?.startsWith('he')) return 'he';
  if (languageCode?.startsWith('ru')) return 'ru';
  return 'en';
}

/** A stored record, or null for none. Upstash may hand back the parsed object or the JSON text. */
function parseRecord(raw: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  if (raw === null || raw === undefined) return null;
  try {
    const value = typeof raw === 'string' ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw;
    return value && typeof value === 'object' ? (value as Record<string, unknown>) : null;
  } catch {
    console.warn('[tg-connect] a stored record is not JSON; read as none');
    return null;
  }
}

function readLink(raw: unknown): { userId: number } | null {
  const record = parseRecord(raw);
  return record && typeof record.userId === 'number' ? { userId: record.userId } : null;
}

function readPress(raw: unknown): { userId: number; telegramId: number; linkHash: string } | null {
  const record = parseRecord(raw);
  if (!record || typeof record.userId !== 'number' || typeof record.telegramId !== 'number' || typeof record.linkHash !== 'string') return null;
  return { userId: record.userId, telegramId: record.telegramId, linkHash: record.linkHash };
}

/** One message in the chat, in HTML. A failed send is logged and captured, never thrown: the outcome stands. */
async function reply(chatId: number | string, text: string, options: MessageOptions = {}): Promise<void> {
  try {
    // Loaded here, as google-connect.ts does: the bot module pulls in the whole Telegram client
    const { getMessagingService } = await import('./telegram/bot');
    await getMessagingService().sendMessage(chatId, text, { format: MessageFormat.HTML, ...options });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[tg-connect] a reply in chat ${chatId} was not sent: ${safeErrorSummary(error)}`);
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'tg-connect-reply');
  }
}

/**
 * The Connect Telegram link for an account with no chat, signed in on this browser within the hour (a WhatsApp link's
 * session never counts). 'limit' past 5 links an hour; 'unavailable' when Redis or the sign-in key fails (logged).
 */
export async function createConnectLink(
  user: UserConfig,
  session: WebSession,
): Promise<{ ok: true; url: string } | { ok: false; error: 'has-chat' | 'stale-sign-in' | 'limit' | 'unavailable' }> {
  if (hasChat(user)) {
    console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${user.id}: link refused: the account has a chat`);
    return { ok: false, error: 'has-chat' };
  }
  if (session.userId !== user.id || session.method === 'wa' || Date.now() - session.signedInAt >= RECENT_SIGN_IN_MS) {
    console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${user.id}: link refused: the ${session.method} sign-in is not recent`);
    return { ok: false, error: 'stale-sign-in' };
  }
  try {
    const made = await countWithin(REDIS_KEYS.signinLimit('tg-connect-hour', signinHash('account', String(user.id))), HOUR_SEC);
    if (made > LINKS_PER_HOUR) {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${user.id}: link refused: ${LINKS_PER_HOUR} links this hour`);
      return { ok: false, error: 'limit' };
    }
    const token = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64url');
    await redis.set(REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnect(tokenHash(token)), JSON.stringify({ userId: user.id }), { ex: TTL_SECONDS });
    console.log(`[tg-connect] user ${user.id}: a connect link was made`);
    const bot = process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME || DEFAULT_BOT_USERNAME;
    return { ok: true, url: `https://t.me/${bot}?start=w_${token}` };
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'tg-connect-link', { user_id: user.id });
    return { ok: false, error: 'unavailable' };
  }
}

/**
 * The guidance for a Telegram that already has its own account: bring the browser account in from Settings there, by
 * Add Google or Add email (the browser account's first way). Nothing is joined here.
 */
async function sendGuidance(
  chatId: number | string,
  sender: UserConfig,
  ownerId: number,
  way: { kind: IdentityKind; address: string } | undefined,
): Promise<void> {
  const locale = normalizeLocale(sender.language);
  const copy = COPY[locale];
  if (!way) {
    console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${ownerId}: no way to name in the guidance`);
    await reply(chatId, copy.failed);
    return;
  }
  const text = fillHtml(way.kind === 'google' ? copy.hasAccountGoogle : copy.hasAccountEmail, { address: isolateLtr(way.address) });
  const settingsUrl = buildUrl(`/${locale}/settings?user_id=${sender.telegramId ?? sender.id}`);
  await reply(chatId, text, { replyMarkup: { inline_keyboard: [[{ text: copy.openSettings, web_app: { url: settingsUrl } }]] } });
  console.log(`[tg-connect] user ${ownerId}: this Telegram has its own account (user ${sender.id}); the guidance was sent and nothing was joined`);
}

/**
 * /start w_<token>. The link is read, not used up: a person who opened it in the wrong Telegram can cancel and open it
 * again in the right one. It never makes an account.
 */
export async function handleConnectStart(
  chatId: number | string,
  telegramId: number,
  token: string,
  languageCode?: string,
): Promise<void> {
  let ownerId: number | undefined;
  try {
    const hash = TOKEN.test(token) ? tokenHash(token) : null;
    const link = hash ? readLink(await redis.get(REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnect(hash))) : null;
    const owner = link ? await getUserById(link.userId) : null;
    ownerId = owner?.id;
    const sender = await getUserByTelegramId(telegramId);
    if (!hash || !link || !owner || hasChat(owner)) {
      const why = !hash ? 'not a link' : !link ? 'the link expired or was used' : !owner ? `account ${link.userId} is gone` : `user ${owner.id} has a chat now`;
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] start from Telegram ${telegramId} refused: ${why}`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([sender, owner], languageCode)].expired);
      return;
    }
    const refusal = await signInRefusal(owner);
    if (refusal) {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${owner.id}: start refused: the account is ${refusal}`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([owner], languageCode)].refused);
      return;
    }
    const way = (await identitiesOf(owner.id))[0];
    if (sender) {
      await sendGuidance(chatId, sender, owner.id, way);
      return;
    }
    const copy = COPY[normalizeLocale(owner.language)];
    if (!way) {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${owner.id}: start refused: the account has no way to show`);
      await reply(chatId, copy.failed);
      return;
    }
    const pressId = crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('base64url');
    await redis.set(REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnectPress(pressId), JSON.stringify({ userId: owner.id, telegramId, linkHash: hash }), { ex: TTL_SECONDS });
    await reply(chatId, fillHtml(copy.question, { name: isolateAuto(owner.name), address: isolateLtr(way.address) }), {
      replyMarkup: {
        inline_keyboard: [[
          { text: copy.connect, callback_data: `tgc:${pressId}` },
          { text: copy.cancel, callback_data: `tgc-no:${pressId}` },
        ]],
      },
    });
    console.log(`[tg-connect] user ${owner.id}: Telegram ${telegramId} was asked to connect`);
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'tg-connect-start', { user_id: ownerId });
    await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([], languageCode)].failed);
  }
}

/** Writes the Telegram id onto the account while it still has no chat and is not suspended: one UPDATE ... WHERE. */
async function attachTelegram(userId: number, telegramId: number): Promise<'attached' | 'gone' | 'taken'> {
  try {
    const { count } = await prisma.user.updateMany({
      where: { id: userId, telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null, whatsappBsuid: null, suspendedAt: null },
      data: { telegramId: BigInt(telegramId), messagingPlatform: 'telegram' },
    });
    return count === 1 ? 'attached' : 'gone';
  } catch (error) {
    // Another account took this Telegram id in between (its /start): the unique telegramId refuses the write
    if ((error as { code?: unknown } | null)?.code === 'P2002') return 'taken';
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * After the Telegram id is written: feature access and the reminder pass see the chat, the menu button opens the
 * dashboard, the person is told and welcomed, and the notice goes to the ways the account had before (`before` is the
 * row read before the write, with no chat, so it goes by email: Task 8's routing). Never throws: the connect has
 * happened, so no "nothing was connected" may follow it.
 */
async function afterConnect(chatId: number | string, before: UserConfig, telegramId: number): Promise<void> {
  console.log(`[tg-connect] user ${before.id}: Telegram ${telegramId} connected`);
  try {
    const { invalidateFeatureAccessCache } = await import('./subscription-service');
    await invalidateFeatureAccessCache(before.id);
    // The account's own reminders now have a chat to ping
    invalidateDueGate();
    const user = await getUserById(before.id);
    const locale = normalizeLocale(user?.language ?? before.language);
    const { setUserMenuButton } = await import('./telegram/bot');
    await setUserMenuButton(telegramId, locale);
    // Who belongs in the reminder cache is the hourly sync's rule
    if (user) await syncReminderCacheEntry(user);
    await reply(chatId, COPY[locale].connected);
    if (user) {
      const { sendWelcome } = await import('./telegram/welcome');
      await sendWelcome(chatId, user);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'tg-connect-after', { user_id: before.id });
  }
  await sendSignInNotice(before, { kind: 'telegram', via: 'connected' });
}

/** The Connect button: `tgc:<pressId>`. The caller has answered the button's spinner. */
export async function handleConnectPress(
  chatId: number | string,
  telegramId: number,
  pressId: string,
  languageCode?: string,
): Promise<void> {
  let ownerId: number | undefined;
  try {
    const press = PRESS_ID.test(pressId) ? readPress(await redis.getdel(REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnectPress(pressId))) : null;
    if (!press) {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] a Connect press from Telegram ${telegramId} found no question (expired or used)`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([await getUserByTelegramId(telegramId)], languageCode)].expired);
      return;
    }
    ownerId = press.userId;
    if (press.telegramId !== telegramId) {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${press.userId}: a Connect press came from another Telegram (${telegramId}); nothing was connected`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([await getUserByTelegramId(telegramId)], languageCode)].notYours);
      return;
    }
    const link = readLink(await redis.getdel(REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnect(press.linkHash)));
    const owner = await getUserById(press.userId);
    if (!link || link.userId !== press.userId || !owner || hasChat(owner)) {
      const why = !link || link.userId !== press.userId ? 'the link expired or was used' : !owner ? 'the account is gone' : 'the account has a chat now';
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${press.userId}: Connect refused: ${why}`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([owner], languageCode)].expired);
      return;
    }
    const refusal = (await signInRefusal(owner)) ?? ((await isIdentifierBlocked({ telegramId })) ? 'blocked' : null);
    if (refusal) {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${owner.id}: Connect refused: ${refusal}`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([owner], languageCode)].refused);
      return;
    }
    const sender = await getUserByTelegramId(telegramId);
    if (sender) {
      await sendGuidance(chatId, sender, owner.id, (await identitiesOf(owner.id))[0]);
      return;
    }
    const attached = await attachTelegram(owner.id, telegramId);
    if (attached === 'taken') {
      const holder = await getUserByTelegramId(telegramId);
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${owner.id}: Connect refused: Telegram ${telegramId} got its own account in between`);
      if (holder) await sendGuidance(chatId, holder, owner.id, (await identitiesOf(owner.id))[0]);
      else await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([owner], languageCode)].failed);
      return;
    }
    if (attached === 'gone') {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${owner.id}: Connect refused: the account changed in between`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([owner], languageCode)].expired);
      return;
    }
    await afterConnect(chatId, owner, telegramId);
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'tg-connect-press', { user_id: ownerId });
    await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([], languageCode)].failed);
  }
}

/** The Cancel button: `tgc-no:<pressId>`. The question and its link are dropped; only the Telegram asked can cancel. */
export async function handleConnectCancel(
  chatId: number | string,
  telegramId: number,
  pressId: string,
  languageCode?: string,
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const key = PRESS_ID.test(pressId) ? REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnectPress(pressId) : null;
    const press = key ? readPress(await redis.get(key)) : null;
    const locale = localeOf([press ? await getUserById(press.userId) : null], languageCode);
    if (!key || !press) {
      await reply(chatId, COPY[locale].expired);
      return;
    }
    if (press.telegramId !== telegramId) {
      console.warn(`[tg-connect] user ${press.userId}: a Cancel press came from another Telegram (${telegramId})`);
      await reply(chatId, COPY[locale].notYours);
      return;
    }
    await redis.del(key, REDIS_KEYS.telegramConnect(press.linkHash));
    console.log(`[tg-connect] user ${press.userId}: Telegram ${telegramId} cancelled the connect`);
    await reply(chatId, COPY[locale].cancelled);
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'tg-connect-cancel');
    await reply(chatId, COPY[localeOf([], languageCode)].failed);
  }
}
```

What each refusal answers, and why the order is this one:
- `/start w_` reads the link with GET (not GETDEL): a person who opened it in the wrong Telegram can press Cancel and open it again in the right one. The press takes the question first (GETDEL); a press from another Telegram id stops there, before the link is touched, so a stranger with the button can't use up the owner's link. Then the link (GETDEL): of two questions made from one link, the first press wins.
- Checked again at the press: the account exists, has no chat, isn't suspended or banned (`signInRefusal`, Task 2's ways included), the pressing Telegram id isn't banned (the webhook drops a banned id's updates first, but polling mode doesn't), and no account has this Telegram id. Then the conditional write.
- After the write nothing can answer "nothing was connected": `afterConnect` catches and captures its own failures, and the notice never throws.

- [ ] **Step 10: The route (`app/api/telegram-connect/route.ts`, new)**

```ts
// Connect Telegram (web sign-up spec §2.9, §3.6): the one-time link that opens the bot for an account made on
// famcal.bot.
//
// POST /api/telegram-connect?user_id=…  body {}
//   → { url }: t.me/<bot>?start=w_<token>, valid 10 minutes, usable once.
//   → 409 { error: 'has-chat' }: the account has Telegram or WhatsApp.
//   → 403 { error: 'stale-sign-in' }: signed in on this browser more than an hour ago, or by a WhatsApp link (the page
//     says "Sign in again to connect Telegram").
//   → 429 { error: 'limit' }: 5 links an hour.
//   → 503 { error: 'unavailable' }: the store failed. A throw is 500 { error: 'unavailable' }.
//   → 401 with no session (verifyUserAuth's own answer, as for its other refusals); 403 { error: 'cross_site' } and
//     415 { error: 'json_only' } from refuseCrossSite.
//
// Security: Origin and JSON first (refuseCrossSite), then verifyUserAuth by the session cookie only (no initData: an
// account inside Telegram has Telegram already) with the settings limiter; the route acts on the proved user only. No
// log line holds the token or the link.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { settingsRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { captureSignInFailure } from '@/src/services/web-signin/safe-error';
import { createConnectLink } from '@/src/services/telegram-connect';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

const STATUS = { 'has-chat': 409, 'stale-sign-in': 403, limit: 429, unavailable: 503 } as const;

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id'), null, settingsRateLimiter, 'telegram-connect');
    if (!auth.success) return auth.response;
    userId = auth.user.id;
    // Without initData only the cookie can prove the user, so this is a session; the check narrows the type
    if (auth.via !== 'session') return NextResponse.json({ error: 'has-chat' }, { status: STATUS['has-chat'] });
    const made = await createConnectLink(auth.user, auth.session);
    if (!made.ok) return NextResponse.json({ error: made.error }, { status: STATUS[made.error] });
    return NextResponse.json({ url: made.url });
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'telegram-connect', { user_id: userId });
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'unavailable' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

```ts
/** A Telegram Bot API path, /bot<id>:<token> ('%3A' when the colon is encoded). */
```

after:
```ts
/** A Telegram Bot API path, /bot<id>:<token> ('%3A' when the colon is encoded). */
const BOT_TOKEN_PATH = /\/bot\d+(?::|%3A)[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/gi;
/**
 * Connect Telegram's one-time token, w_<22 base64url characters> (src/services/telegram-connect.ts): in the /start text
 * of the Telegram webhook's body, and in any breadcrumb or URL that quotes it.
 */
const CONNECT_TOKEN = /\bw_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])/g;
/**
 * The Google connect's pending id, gc_<32 base64url characters> (src/services/google-connect.ts): it rides in the same
 * /start text, and in a WhatsApp message, so it is scrubbed the same way.
 */
const GOOGLE_CONNECT_ID = /\bgc_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])/g;
/** Both ids out of a string. gc_ first: a w_ pattern could match inside a gc_ id that holds "-w_" and leave the rest. */
function scrubConnectIds(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(GOOGLE_CONNECT_ID, `gc_${SCRUBBED}`).replace(CONNECT_TOKEN, `w_${SCRUBBED}`);
}
```

```ts
/** Drops the credential header attributes; scrubs initData, secret query values and a bot token from any string. */
```

```ts
/**
 * Connect Telegram's token and the Google connect's pending id out of a request body of any shape: the Telegram
 * webhook's update carries them deep inside (message.text), where the field rules above don't look. A body that can't
 * be written out as JSON is left as it is.
 */
function scrubConnectBody(data: unknown): unknown {
  if (typeof data === 'string') return scrubConnectIds(data);
  if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return data;
  try {
    const text = JSON.stringify(data);
    const scrubbed = scrubConnectIds(text);
    return scrubbed === text ? data : JSON.parse(scrubbed);
  } catch {
    console.warn('[sentry-scrub] a request body could not be read for a Connect Telegram token');
    return data;
  }
}

/** Drops the credential header attributes; scrubs initData, secret query values and a bot token from any string. */
```

## Part E: Task 7 (Join) and Task 8 (notices to the ways that were there before; the last way)

### Task 7: Join: an account made on famcal.bot joins the account that proves its way

#### Notes for Tasks 7–8 (read first)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md` (§2.9, §2.11, §2.12, §3.6, §3.9, §8 "Join", "The last way", "Notices"). Contract: `plan/contract.md`. Code read at edd9d72e; every before-block is the file as the earlier tasks (1–6, then 7) leave it.

Rulings that apply here (rulings.md):
- **#1:** "has a chat" is one rule, `hasChat(user)` from `src/lib/has-chat.ts` (Task 1): `join.ts`'s `joinRefusal`, `identities.ts`'s `chat: hasChat(user)` and `notice.ts`'s choice between the chat and the email call it; the chat send itself still reads `telegramId` / `getWhatsAppChatId`. Why: one code path; a `UserConfig` holds a missing WhatsApp id as `undefined`.
- **#9:** every single-smoke run is `$RUN <name>` (the header's runner, written by Task 1 Step 1.0). Why: one runner that blanks the Turnstile names too.
- **#10:** Step 10 is written on Task 2 Step 2.6's text: in `finishAddGoogle`, `signInRefusal`, then the blocklist check, then `addIdentity`, then on `taken` `identityHolder` and `offerJoin`; in the email confirm route the 403 `blocked` comes before the 409 `join`. Why: a blocked way must never reach the Join question.
- **#12:** `signinNotice.telegramConnected` is Task 6's key and wording; these tasks add only `joinedGoogle`, `joinedEmail` (Task 7) and `emailSubject`, `emailSubjectTelegram`, `emailWhy` (Task 8), and #54 reads Task 6's words. Why: one key, one wording.
- **#14:** `chat: boolean` stays on `SignInMethodsView`; Task 9 reads it (no `hasChat` prop). Why: one carrier of the fact.
- **#16:** `sendNoticeEmail` calls `takeNoticeSend(userId)` (3 a UTC day per account, then the day's 10); `notice.ts` logs each refusal as its SECURITY line: `(the account's notices are spent)` and `(the day's notices are spent)`. Why: spec §1, one account can't use up everyone's security notices.
- **Rf3 (email half):** `smoke-signin-methods` #55 pins that a name holding `<b>&"x"</b>` arrives escaped in the notice email's HTML.

Contract notes (corrections against the real code; later parts use these):

1. **`MergePlan.google` is `'moves' | 'stays' | 'none'`.** A W with no Google Calendar connection has nothing to move or leave behind, and the question shows no Google line then. (The contract had only `'moves' | 'stays'`.) `MergePlan.ways` is sorted.
2. **The merge's exports** (`src/services/account-linking.ts`): `mergePlan(w: MergeSide, t: MergeSide): MergePlan` (pure, the one rule set), `interface MergeSide { id; hasGoogle; pairingId; pairing; subscription; wayKinds; calendars; events }`, `mergeIntoAccount(tx, wUserId, tUserId): Promise<MergeOutcome>` with `MergeOutcome = { pairingId: string | null; reconnectGoogle: boolean; languageChanged: boolean; plan: MergePlan }`, `previewMerge(wUserId, tUserId): Promise<MergePlan>` (the dry run: the same `readMergeSide` + `mergePlan`, read outside a transaction), `mergeAccounts(wUserId, tUserId): Promise<MergeOutcome>` (W's cache keys, the transaction, `afterMerge`: the one path `redeemLinkCode` and `runJoin` both take), and `class MergeRefusedError` (thrown before any write: W has Telegram, or a WhatsApp W meets a T with no Telegram).
3. **"W's trial never replaces T's subscription", exactly:** W's subscription moves when T has none, or when it is not a trial (`accessRank` kind 1) and `runsLonger`. A trial into a T with no subscription row still moves: it replaces nothing (and T would otherwise start a fresh 14-day trial at first use, `getOrCreateSubscription`). The rule holds for the WhatsApp merge too; no existing check of `smoke-account-merge.ts` changes (none had W's trial outlast T's).
4. **`afterMerge`'s menu-button step already runs only when T has Telegram** (`if (languageChanged && t.telegramId)`, `account-linking.ts:563`): no change there.
5. **The question's id travels as `token`**: in the Join POST body (`{ token }`, not `{ joinId }`) and in the add-Google landing's URL, because the log and Sentry scrubber already drops `token` and not `joinId` (`src/lib/sentry-scrub.ts:53-60`). The email confirm route's JSON answer keeps the name `joinId` (answers are not scrubbed or logged).
6. **The two answers that offer a Join:**
   - The email confirm route answers `{ ok: false, error: 'join', joinId, summary }` with HTTP 409 (the route's answers are `{ ok, error }`; the contract wrote `{ status: 'join', … }`).
   - `finishAddGoogle` is Google's callback, a redirect: it signs the browser in as T (method `google`, as an added Google way does) and lands on `/{locale}/signin/add-google/join?token=<joinId>` through `finishSignIn(user, 'google', { page: { join: joinId } })`. So **`FinishPage` gains `{ join: string }` here, in Task 7**, beside Task 11's `{ invite: string }`. The path comes from a new `addGoogleJoinHref(locale, joinId)` in `src/site/signin.ts` (`smoke-web-session.ts` #18 refuses a `/signin` literal in `web-session.ts`). If Task 5 or Task 11 already added `{ invite }` when this lands, keep both members and both branches of `appPageUrl`.
7. **New in `identities.ts` (Task 7): `identityHolder(kind, subject): Promise<number | null>`**: `addIdentity` answers only `'taken'`, and Join needs the holder. The contract's `identitiesOf` is not needed: the merge reads W's and T's way kinds inside its own transaction (`account-linking.ts` is the merge exception `smoke-signin-setup.ts` allows).
8. **`join.ts` exports** `offerJoin(tUser: UserConfig, wUserId: number, way: { kind: IdentityKind; subject: string; address: string })`, `runJoin(tUserId: number, joinId: unknown)`, `peekJoin(tUserId: number, joinId: unknown): Promise<JoinSummary | null>` (new: the add-Google landing reads the question for the session's account without using it up), and `type JoinSummary`. `offerJoin` also returns null when the way is no longer W's. The Redis key is `REDIS_KEYS.signinJoin(sha256 of the id)` (as `signinAddGoogle`), 600 s.
9. **The question's words live once, in `settings.signIn.join.*`** (the question, what moves, what closes, the buttons and the outcomes). The site's client provider gets only the `site` namespace (`src/site/messages.ts`), so the add-Google landing renders the question on the server (`getTranslations`) and its client (`JoinClient`) reads only `site.signin.addGoogle.join.*` (its buttons and outcomes). The list is one client-safe helper, `src/lib/join-summary.ts`: `joinLines(plan)`, `joinDateText(iso, locale)` (Israel's zone: an account made on famcal.bot has no place yet, so the default zone is its zone) and `isJoinSummary(value)`.
10. **Task 8: `SignInMethodsView` gains `chat: boolean` too** (beside `lastWay`, from `hasChat(user)`; Task 9's `SignInMethods` reads `methods.chat`): Settings words the "added" line by it (`settings.signIn.noticeSentEmail` when false). `type DurableWay = 'telegram' | 'whatsapp' | IdentityKind` is exported. `removeSignInMethod` returns `'removed' | 'last-way' | 'none'`; its one caller besides the route is `smoke-signin-calendar-match.ts` #22 (updated).
11. **Task 8: `noticeAddress(userId, gained: IdentityKind | null): Promise<{ kind: IdentityKind; address: string } | null>`** is new in `identities.ts` (the notice email's recipient: the email way, else the Google way, never the kind just added; `identities.ts` stays the only `SignInIdentity` reader).
12. **Task 8: `sendNoticeEmail(args: { to: string; locale: string; subject: string; lines: string[]; userId: number }): Promise<'sent' | NoticeRefusal>`**: `NoticeRefusal` is `takeNoticeSend(userId)`'s reason (`'notice-account-day' | 'notice-budget' | 'store-down'`) when Task 4's budget refuses, a throw when Resend refuses or gives up. `notice.ts` writes the one `[signin-notice] SECURITY: notice for user <id> not sent (<why>)` line and `captureError(…, 'signin-notice', { user_id, purpose }, 'warning')` for every notice that doesn't go out: no address, the budget, the mail failing, and the chat send failing too (so `smoke-signin-methods.ts` #13 changes). `email-send.ts` gets one shared Resend call (`postEmail`) and HTML frame (`emailHtml`) for the code and the notice; the code email's HTML is byte-identical.
13. **A Telegram connect's notice never goes to the chat** (`{ kind: 'telegram', via: 'connected' }`): that chat is the way just added. It goes by email, with its own subject.

```ts
/**
 * The ON DELETE CASCADE relations the account merge (smoke-join.ts) leans on, as the migrations declare them: a deleted
 * user takes its sign-in ways, open invites, copies to Google, payments and pings; a deleted calendar its events; a
 * deleted event its instances and reminder states. Other relations are not modelled (smoke-account-merge.ts has the
 * full set).
 */
const CASCADE: Record<string, [table: string, fk: string][]> = {
  user: [['signInIdentity', 'userId'], ['pairingInvite', 'inviterUserId'], ['googleSyncLink', 'userId'], ['payment', 'userId'], ['nativeReminderPing', 'userId']],
  nativeCalendar: [['nativeEvent', 'calendarId']],
  nativeEvent: [['nativeEventInstance', 'seriesEventId'], ['nativeReminderState', 'seriesEventId']],
};
function cascade(name: string, gone: Row[]): void {
  for (const [table, fk] of CASCADE[name] ?? []) {
    const rows = (DB[table] ?? []).filter(r => gone.some(g => same(r[fk], g.id)));
    if (rows.length === 0) continue;
    DB[table] = (DB[table] ?? []).filter(r => !rows.includes(r));
    cascade(table, rows);
  }
}

function model(name: string): Row {
  const t = () => (DB[name] ??= []);
```

```ts
  await check('#3 no question, still taken: the holder has Telegram (Noa) or WhatsApp; the two are partners; the holder is suspended or banned (its Google account on the blocklist)', async () => {
    const cases: Array<[string, () => void, Row]> = [
      ['the holder has Telegram', () => undefined, { sub: 'g-noa', email: 'noa@gmail.com', emailVerified: true }],
      ['the holder has WhatsApp', () => { userRow(DANA)!.whatsappPhone = '+972500000021'; }, danaGoogle],
      ['the two are partners', () => {
        DB.pairing.push(pairing('pair-td', TAL, DANA));
        userRow(TAL)!.pairingId = 'pair-td';
        userRow(DANA)!.pairingId = 'pair-td';
      }, danaGoogle],
      ['the holder is suspended', () => { userRow(DANA)!.suspendedAt = new Date(); }, danaGoogle],
      ['the holder is banned', () => { DB.blockedIdentifier = [{ id: 1, telegramId: null, whatsappPhone: null, googleSub: 'g-dana', email: null, createdAt: new Date() }]; }, danaGoogle],
    ];
    for (const [name, setUp, claims] of cases) {
      seed();
      setUp();
      const res = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, claims);
      assert(location(res).includes('status=taken') && joinKeys().length === 0 && sent.length === 0, `${name}: ${location(res)} keys ${show(joinKeys())}`);
      assert(logs.some(l => l.startsWith('[join] user 9: no join offered for user')), `${name}: logs ${show(logs)}`);
    }
    seed();
    userRow(DANA)!.suspendedAt = new Date();
    const res = await addEmail(TAL_TG, tal, 'dana@example.com');
    assert(res.status === 409 && (await body(res)).error === 'taken' && joinKeys().length === 0, `email: ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
  });

  await check('#4 nothing is joined without a question: a wrong code asks nothing; an id never offered, a malformed one and none are expired (410); another site is 403 and no credential 401, each before any merge', async () => {
    seed();
    const wrong = await addEmail(TAL_TG, tal, 'dana@example.com', '000000');
    assert(wrong.status === 400 && joinKeys().length === 0, `wrong ${wrong.status} ${show(await body(wrong))}`);
    for (const token of [crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64url'), 'not-an-id', undefined]) {
      const res = await answer(TAL_TG, tal, token);
      assert(res.status === 410 && (await body(res)).error === 'expired', `${show(token)}: ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
    }
    const question = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, danaGoogle);
    const id = joinIdOf(question);
    const evil = await answer(TAL_TG, tal, id, { origin: 'https://evil.example' });
    const nobody = await answer(TAL_TG, {}, id);
    assert(evil.status === 403 && nobody.status === 401 && userRow(DANA) && joinKeys().length === 1, `evil ${evil.status} nobody ${nobody.status}`);
  });

  // ---- The answer ----

  await check('#5 Join merges: the answer lists Tal\'s ways; Dana\'s row is gone; her calendars, events and ways are Tal\'s (her email too: Tal had none); Tal keeps its Telegram id and messagingPlatform, and its own trial (Dana\'s longer trial never replaces it); the notice goes to Tal\'s chat; the question is then used up', async () => {
    seed();
    const question = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, danaGoogle);
    const id = joinIdOf(question);
    const browser = cookieOf(question);
    const res = await answer(TAL, browser, id);
    const b = await body(res);
    assert(res.status === 200 && b.ok === true && b.methods?.google?.address === 'dana@gmail.com' && b.methods?.email?.address === 'dana@example.com', `answer ${res.status} ${show(b)}; captured ${show(captured)}`);
    assert(!userRow(DANA), 'Dana is still there');
    assert(show(waysOf(TAL)) === show(['email:dana@example.com', 'google:g-dana']), `Tal's ways ${show(waysOf(TAL))}`);
    const talCalendars = DB.nativeCalendar.filter(c => c.ownerUserId === TAL).map(c => c.id);
    for (const ev of ['ev-w1', 'ev-w2', 'ev-w3']) {
      const row = DB.nativeEvent.find(e => e.id === ev);
      assert(row && talCalendars.includes(row.calendarId) && row.creatorUserId === TAL, `${ev}: ${show(row)}`);
    }
    const t = userRow(TAL)!;
    assert(String(t.telegramId) === String(TAL_TG) && t.messagingPlatform === 'telegram' && t.whatsappPhone === null && t.name === 'Tal', `Tal ${show(t)}`);
    const subs = DB.subscription.filter(s => s.userId === TAL);
    assert(subs.length === 1 && subs[0].id === 'sub-t' && !DB.subscription.some(s => s.id === 'sub-w'), `subscriptions ${show(DB.subscription)}`);
    assert(sent.length === 1 && sent[0].platform === 'telegram' && sent[0].chatId === String(TAL_TG), `notices ${show(sent)}`);
    assert(sent[0].text.includes('d•••@gmail.com') && !sent[0].text.includes('dana@gmail.com') && sent[0].text.includes('privacy@famcal.bot'), `notice ${sent[0].text}`);
    const again = await answer(TAL, browser, id);
    assert(again.status === 410 && (await body(again)).error === 'expired', `again ${again.status}`);
  });

  await check('#6 Dana\'s sessions end with Dana: her browser\'s cookie names no account after the join (404, cookie cleared)', async () => {
    seed();
    const danaBrowser: Auth = { cookie: await sessionCookie(DANA, 'google') };
    const before = await methodsRoute.GET(request(`/api/signin-methods?user_id=${DANA}`, danaBrowser));
    assert(before.status === 200, `before ${before.status}`);
    const question = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, danaGoogle);
    const res = await answer(TAL, cookieOf(question), joinIdOf(question));
    assert(res.status === 200, `answer ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
    const after = await methodsRoute.GET(request(`/api/signin-methods?user_id=${DANA}`, danaBrowser));
    assert(after.status === 404 && after.headers.get('set-cookie')?.includes(`${SESSION_COOKIE_NAME}=;`), `after ${after.status} ${after.headers.get('set-cookie')}`);
  });

  // ---- The dry run equals the merge ----

  type Scenario = { name: string; setUp: () => void; via: 'google' | 'email'; want: Row };
  const scenarios: Scenario[] = [
    {
      name: 'both paired (Dana with Paz, Tal with Qai)',
      via: 'email',
      setUp: () => {
        DB.pairing.push(pairing('pair-dp', DANA, PAZ), pairing('pair-tq', QAI, TAL));
        Object.assign(userRow(DANA)!, { pairingId: 'pair-dp' });
        Object.assign(userRow(PAZ)!, { pairingId: 'pair-dp' });
        Object.assign(userRow(TAL)!, { pairingId: 'pair-tq' });
        Object.assign(userRow(QAI)!, { pairingId: 'pair-tq' });
      },
      want: { partner: 'ends' },
    },
    {
      name: 'only Dana paired',
      via: 'email',
      setUp: () => {
        DB.pairing.push(pairing('pair-dp', DANA, PAZ));
        Object.assign(userRow(DANA)!, { pairingId: 'pair-dp' });
        Object.assign(userRow(PAZ)!, { pairingId: 'pair-dp' });
      },
      want: { partner: 'moves' },
    },
    {
      name: 'only Tal paired',
      via: 'google',
      setUp: () => {
        DB.pairing.push(pairing('pair-tq', QAI, TAL));
        Object.assign(userRow(TAL)!, { pairingId: 'pair-tq' });
        Object.assign(userRow(QAI)!, { pairingId: 'pair-tq' });
      },
      want: { partner: 'none' },
    },
    {
      name: 'both with Google Calendar',
      via: 'google',
      setUp: () => {
        userRow(DANA)!.googleRefreshToken = 'enc-rt-dana';
        userRow(TAL)!.googleRefreshToken = 'enc-rt-tal';
      },
      want: { google: 'stays' },
    },
    {
      name: 'only Dana with Google Calendar',
      via: 'email',
      setUp: () => { userRow(DANA)!.googleRefreshToken = 'enc-rt-dana'; },
      want: { google: 'moves' },
    },
    {
      name: 'ways of the same kind (Tal has an email way of its own)',
      via: 'google',
      setUp: () => { DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'email', subject: 'tal@example.com', address: 'tal@example.com' })); },
      want: { ways: ['google'] },
    },
    {
      name: 'Dana pays for a plan that runs longer',
      via: 'email',
      setUp: () => { DB.subscription = DB.subscription.filter(s => s.id !== 'sub-w').concat(paid('sub-w', DANA, 20)); },
      want: { plan: 'moves' },
    },
  ];

  /** What the merge did, read from the rows before and after, in the plan's own terms. */
  const observe = (before: Row, after: Row): Row => {
    const talCalendars = after.calendars.filter((c: Row) => c.ownerUserId === TAL).map((c: Row) => c.id);
    const wEvents = before.events.filter((e: Row) => before.wCalendars.includes(e.calendarId) && !e.isDeleted).map((e: Row) => e.id);
    const landed = wEvents.filter((id: string) => talCalendars.includes(after.events.find((e: Row) => e.id === id)?.calendarId));
    const wPairing = before.dana.pairingId;
    return {
      calendars: before.wCalendars.length,
      events: landed.length === wEvents.length ? wEvents.length : -1,
      ways: after.talWays.filter((k: string) => !before.talWays.includes(k)),
      google: !before.dana.googleRefreshToken ? 'none' : after.tal.googleRefreshToken === before.dana.googleRefreshToken ? 'moves' : 'stays',
      partner: !wPairing ? 'none' : after.tal.pairingId === wPairing ? 'moves' : after.pairings.find((p: Row) => p.id === wPairing)?.status === 'UNLINKED' ? 'ends' : '?',
      plan: after.subs.find((s: Row) => s.userId === TAL)?.id === before.wSub ? 'moves' : 'stays',
    };
  };
  const snapshot = () => ({
    dana: { ...(userRow(DANA) ?? {}) },
    tal: { ...userRow(TAL)! },
    wCalendars: DB.nativeCalendar.filter(c => c.ownerUserId === DANA && !c.isDeleted).map(c => c.id),
    events: DB.nativeEvent.map(e => ({ ...e })),
    calendars: DB.nativeCalendar.map(c => ({ ...c })),
    talWays: (DB.signInIdentity ?? []).filter(i => i.userId === TAL).map(i => i.kind).sort(),
    pairings: DB.pairing.map(p => ({ ...p })),
    subs: DB.subscription.map(s => ({ ...s })),
    wSub: DB.subscription.find(s => s.userId === DANA)?.id,
  });

  await check('#7 the question shows what the merge then does, in every case: both paired, either paired, both with Google, only Dana with Google, ways of the same kind, a paid plan that runs longer', async () => {
    const problems: string[] = [];
    for (const s of scenarios) {
      seed();
      s.setUp();
      let summary: Row;
      let id: string;
      let auth: Auth;
      if (s.via === 'google') {
        const res = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, danaGoogle);
        id = joinIdOf(res);
        summary = JSON.parse(String(redisStore.get(joinKeys()[0]))).summary;
        auth = cookieOf(res);
      } else {
        const res = await addEmail(TAL_TG, tal, 'dana@example.com');
        const b = await body(res);
        id = b.joinId;
        joinIds.push(id);
        summary = b.summary;
        auth = tal;
      }
      const before = snapshot();
      const res = await answer(s.via === 'google' ? TAL : TAL_TG, auth, id);
      if (res.status !== 200) {
        problems.push(`${s.name}: answer ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
        continue;
      }
      const did = observe(before, snapshot());
      if (show(did) !== show(summary.plan)) problems.push(`${s.name}: asked ${show(summary.plan)}, did ${show(did)}`);
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(s.want)) {
        if (show(summary.plan[key]) !== show(value)) problems.push(`${s.name}: ${key} ${show(summary.plan[key])}, want ${show(value)}`);
      }
    }
    assert(problems.length === 0, problems.join('; '));
  });

  // ---- What T keeps ----

  await check('#8 T keeps its own chat: a WhatsApp-only Shir keeps her phone and messagingPlatform, has no Telegram, and gets the notice on WhatsApp in Hebrew; a Tal on both chats stays on both', async () => {
    seed();
    const shir: Auth = { cookie: await sessionCookie(SHIR, 'wa') };
    const res = await addEmail(SHIR, shir, 'dana@example.com');
    const b = await body(res);
    assert(res.status === 409 && b.error === 'join', `confirm ${res.status} ${show(b)}`);
    const done = await answer(SHIR, shir, b.joinId);
    joinIds.push(b.joinId);
    assert(done.status === 200, `answer ${done.status} ${show(await body(done))}`);
    const row = userRow(SHIR)!;
    assert(row.whatsappPhone === SHIR_PHONE && row.messagingPlatform === 'whatsapp' && row.telegramId === null && !userRow(DANA), `Shir ${show(row)}`);
    assert(sent.length === 1 && sent[0].platform === 'whatsapp' && sent[0].chatId === SHIR_PHONE && /[֐-׿]/.test(sent[0].text), `sent ${show(sent)}`);
    seed();
    Object.assign(userRow(TAL)!, { whatsappPhone: '+972500000009', messagingPlatform: 'all' });
    const both = await addEmail(TAL_TG, tal, 'dana@example.com');
    const joined = await answer(TAL_TG, tal, (await body(both)).joinId);
    assert(joined.status === 200 && userRow(TAL)!.whatsappPhone === '+972500000009' && userRow(TAL)!.messagingPlatform === 'all', `Tal ${show(userRow(TAL))}`);
  });

  // ---- Refused at the answer ----

  await check('#9 refused at the answer (409), nothing joined: another account answers Tal\'s question (and uses it up, so Tal\'s answer is then 410); Dana got Telegram meanwhile; the two paired meanwhile', async () => {
    seed();
    const question = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, danaGoogle);
    const id = joinIdOf(question);
    const noa = await answer(NOA_TG, { initData: initDataFor(NOA_TG) }, id);
    assert(noa.status === 409 && (await body(noa)).error === 'refused' && userRow(DANA), `Noa ${noa.status}`);
    const late = await answer(TAL, cookieOf(question), id);
    assert(late.status === 410, `Tal after Noa ${late.status}`);
    for (const meanwhile of ['telegram', 'paired'] as const) {
      seed();
      const q = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, danaGoogle);
      if (meanwhile === 'telegram') userRow(DANA)!.telegramId = BigInt(555555555);
      else {
        DB.pairing.push(pairing('pair-td', TAL, DANA));
        userRow(TAL)!.pairingId = 'pair-td';
        userRow(DANA)!.pairingId = 'pair-td';
      }
      const res = await answer(TAL, cookieOf(q), joinIdOf(q));
      assert(res.status === 409 && (await body(res)).error === 'refused' && userRow(DANA) && show(waysOf(TAL)) === '[]', `${meanwhile}: ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
    }
  });

  await check('#10 the add-Google page reads the question for Tal\'s session only, without using it up: peekJoin answers the summary for Tal, null for Noa and for a bad id, and the question still works', async () => {
    seed();
    const question = await addGoogle(TAL_TG, tal, danaGoogle);
    const id = joinIdOf(question);
    const forTal = await join.peekJoin(TAL, id);
    assert(forTal?.name === 'Dana' && forTal.plan?.calendars === 2 && forTal.plan?.events === 3, `Tal ${show(forTal)}`);
    assert((await join.peekJoin(NOA, id)) === null && (await join.peekJoin(TAL, 'x')) === null, 'another account or a bad id read it');
    assert((await join.peekJoin(TAL, id))?.name === 'Dana' && joinKeys().length === 1, 'the peek used it up');
  });

  // ---- The words ----

  await check('#11 the question\'s words are in all three catalogues with the same keys: settings.signIn.join (the question, what moves) and site.signin.addGoogle.join (the page\'s buttons); the joined notices name Settings\' path and privacy@famcal.bot', async () => {
    const read = (lang: string): Row => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'messages', `${lang}.json`), 'utf8'));
    const en = read('en');
    const settingsKeys = Object.keys(en.settings.signIn.join).sort();
    const siteKeys = Object.keys(en.site.signin.addGoogle.join).sort();
    for (const key of ['calendars', 'wayGoogle', 'wayEmail', 'google', 'googleStays', 'partner', 'partnerEnds', 'plan', 'question', 'closes', 'join', 'joining', 'done', 'expired', 'refused', 'title', 'movesTitle']) {
      assert(settingsKeys.includes(key), `settings.signIn.join.${key} is missing`);
    }
    const path3: Record<string, string> = { en: 'Settings → Sign in on the web → Remove', he: 'הגדרות ← כניסה מהדפדפן ← הסרה', ru: '«Настройки» → «Вход через браузер» → «Убрать»' };
    for (const lang of ['en', 'he', 'ru']) {
      const m = read(lang);
      assert(show(Object.keys(m.settings.signIn.join).sort()) === show(settingsKeys) && show(Object.keys(m.site.signin.addGoogle.join).sort()) === show(siteKeys), `${lang}: other keys`);
      for (const arg of ['{name}', '{date}', '{kind,']) assert(String(m.settings.signIn.join.question).replace(/\{kind, /, '{kind,').includes(arg), `${lang} question lacks ${arg}`);
      for (const key of ['joinedGoogle', 'joinedEmail']) {
        const text = String(m.signinNotice[key]);
        assert(text.includes(path3[lang]) && text.includes('privacy@famcal.bot') && text.includes('{address}'), `${lang}.signinNotice.${key}: ${text}`);
      }
    }
  });

  await check('#12 no console line and no capture holds an email address, a question id or Dana\'s name', () => {
    const text = [...everyLog, ...everyCapture.map(c => `${c.context} ${c.message} ${show(c.extra)}`)].join('\n');
    const lower = text.toLowerCase();
    const addresses = ['dana@gmail.com', 'dana@example.com', 'noa@gmail.com', 'tal@example.com'].filter(a => lower.includes(a));
    const ids = joinIds.filter(id => id && text.includes(id));
    const names = /\bDana\b/.test(text);
    assert(addresses.length === 0 && ids.length === 0 && !names, `leaked: ${show({ addresses, ids, names })}`);
  });

  report();
}

// The harness captures console.*, so a crash is written straight to stdout.
main().catch(err => {
  process.stdout.write(`${err instanceof Error ? err.stack : String(err)}\n`);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 6: One rule set for the merge (`mergePlan`), and the three changes**

`mergeWhatsAppUser` becomes the exported `mergeIntoAccount`. It refuses a W with Telegram, and a WhatsApp W into a T with no Telegram, before writing anything. It reads both sides once (`readMergeSide`) and takes every decision from `mergePlan`: the pairing (`plan.partner`), the copies' queued work and the Google move (`plan.google`), the subscription (`plan.plan`, with the trial rule), and the ways (`plan.ways`). The conditional writes stay, so a race still ends as before. WhatsApp ids and `messagingPlatform: 'all'` are written only for a WhatsApp W. `mergeAccounts` is the one path both callers take; `previewMerge` is the dry run.

```ts
}

/** One side of a merge as its rules read it: W (the account that closes) or T (the one that stays). */
export interface MergeSide {
  id: number;
  /** A Google Calendar connection (a refresh token is stored) */
  hasGoogle: boolean;
  /** User.pairingId as read, and that pairing's row (null when there is none) */
  pairingId: string | null;
  pairing: Pick<Pairing, 'id' | 'status' | 'inviterUserId'> | null;
  subscription: Subscription | null;
  /** The kinds of the account's web sign-in ways */
  wayKinds: IdentityKind[];
  /** The live calendars, and the live events and reminders in them */
  calendars: number;
  events: number;
}

/**
 * What a merge of W into T does, from the two sides as read. The one set of rules: mergeIntoAccount follows it, and
 * the Join question's dry run (previewMerge) shows it.
 * - calendars, events: W's live calendars and the live events and reminders in them, all of which end up T's (folded
 *   into a calendar of T's or moved over);
 * - ways: the kinds of W's sign-in ways T has none of (one of each kind per person); W's others close with W;
 * - google: W's Google Calendar connection moves when T has none ('stays' behind with W otherwise, and T is told to
 *   reconnect); 'none' when W has no connection;
 * - partner: W's ACTIVE pairing moves to a T with no pairing, and ends otherwise; 'none' when W has no active one;
 * - plan: W's subscription moves when T has none, or when it runs longer (runsLonger) and is not a trial: W's trial
 *   never replaces T's subscription, since an account (an email address) costs nothing to make.
 */
export interface MergePlan {
  calendars: number;
  events: number;
  ways: IdentityKind[];
  google: 'moves' | 'stays' | 'none';
  partner: 'moves' | 'ends' | 'none';
  plan: 'moves' | 'stays';
}

export function mergePlan(w: MergeSide, t: MergeSide): MergePlan {
  const wSub = w.subscription;
  const tSub = t.subscription;
  const isTrial = (sub: Subscription) => accessRank(sub)[0] === 1;
  return {
    calendars: w.calendars,
    events: w.events,
    ways: w.wayKinds.filter(kind => !t.wayKinds.includes(kind)).sort(),
    google: !w.hasGoogle ? 'none' : t.hasGoogle ? 'stays' : 'moves',
    partner: w.pairing?.status !== 'ACTIVE' ? 'none' : t.pairingId === null ? 'moves' : 'ends',
    plan: wSub && (!tSub || (!isTrial(wSub) && runsLonger(wSub, tSub))) ? 'moves' : 'stays',
  };
}

/** A side of a merge, read with `db` (the merge's transaction, or the root client for the dry run). */
async function readMergeSide(db: Prisma.TransactionClient, user: Pick<User, 'id' | 'googleRefreshToken' | 'pairingId'>): Promise<MergeSide> {
  const pairing = user.pairingId
    ? await db.pairing.findUnique({ where: { id: user.pairingId }, select: { id: true, status: true, inviterUserId: true } })
    : null;
  const subscription = await db.subscription.findUnique({ where: { userId: user.id } });
  const ways = await db.signInIdentity.findMany({ where: { userId: user.id }, select: { kind: true } });
  const calendarIds = (await db.nativeCalendar.findMany({ where: { ownerUserId: user.id, isDeleted: false }, select: { id: true } })).map(c => c.id);
  const events = calendarIds.length ? await db.nativeEvent.count({ where: { calendarId: { in: calendarIds }, isDeleted: false } }) : 0;
  return {
    id: user.id,
    hasGoogle: !!user.googleRefreshToken,
    pairingId: user.pairingId,
    pairing,
    subscription,
    wayKinds: ways.map(way => way.kind as IdentityKind),
    calendars: calendarIds.length,
    events,
  };
}

/** The merge of W into T as it would run now (the Join question's dry run): the same rules, read outside a transaction. */
export async function previewMerge(wUserId: number, tUserId: number): Promise<MergePlan> {
  const [w, t] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.user.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: wUserId } }),
    prisma.user.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: tUserId } }),
  ]);
  return mergePlan(await readMergeSide(prisma, w), await readMergeSide(prisma, t));
}

/** A merge refused before it wrote anything: W has Telegram, or a WhatsApp W met a T without Telegram. The message names no identifier. */
export class MergeRefusedError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'MergeRefusedError';
  }
}

export interface MergeOutcome {
  /** T's pairing after the merge */
  pairingId: string | null;
  /** W's Google connection stayed behind (T had its own): the user is told to reconnect */
  reconnectGoogle: boolean;
  /** T took W's language */
  languageChanged: boolean;
  /** The decisions the merge followed */
  plan: MergePlan;
}

const hasWhatsApp = (u: Pick<User, 'whatsappPhone' | 'whatsappBsuid'>) => !!u.whatsappPhone || !!u.whatsappBsuid;
```

- [ ] **Step 8: `src/services/web-signin/join.ts`**

`src/services/web-signin/join.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Join (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.9, §3.6): one account (T) takes in a FamCal account made on famcal.bot (W).
 *
 * A join is offered only where the person has just proved, in a flow they started from T, that they hold W's way:
 * Settings' Add Google (finishAddGoogle, after Google's answer) and Add email (the confirm route, after the right code)
 * find the way held by W. Anything less would let someone talk a person into joining a stranger's account into theirs.
 * It is offered only for a W with no chat (no Telegram, no WhatsApp) that isn't T's partner, with neither account
 * suspended or banned; otherwise the caller answers 6b's `taken`.
 *
 * The question lists what moves, from previewMerge: the merge's own rules (mergePlan, account-linking.ts) read now, so
 * it can't promise what the merge won't do. Its id (16 random bytes, base64url) is kept 10 minutes in Redis only as
 * its sha256, bound to T, and used once (GETDEL): an answer from another account uses it up and joins nothing.
 * runJoin checks everything again before it merges, then T gets the notice for the way it gained (sendSignInNotice),
 * and W's sessions end with W (its row is gone). No log line holds the id, an address or a name.
 *
 * account-linking is loaded when a join runs, as notice.ts loads the bot: it pulls in the Telegram client.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import { redis } from '../../utils/redis';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '../../config/redis-keys';
import { signInRefusal } from '../../lib/web-session';
import { hasChat } from '../../lib/has-chat';
import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import type { MergePlan } from '../account-linking';
import { getUserById } from '../user-service';
import { invalidateFeatureAccessCache } from '../subscription-service';
import { identityHolder, listSignInMethods, type IdentityKind, type SignInMethodsView } from './identities';
import { sendSignInNotice } from './notice';

const JOIN_TTL_SEC = 10 * 60;
/** 16 random bytes as base64url */
const JOIN_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}$/;

/** What the question shows: W's name, when it was made, and what the merge would do. */
export type JoinSummary = { name: string; createdAt: string; plan: MergePlan };

type JoinRecord = {
  tUserId: number;
  wUserId: number;
  /** The way the person proved: the one T gains, which the notice names */
  way: { kind: IdentityKind; subject: string; address: string };
  summary: JoinSummary;
};

const keyOf = (joinId: string) => REDIS_KEYS.signinJoin(crypto.createHash('sha256').update(joinId).digest('hex'));

/** Why W can't join T, or null. Read the same way when the question is made and when it is answered. */
async function joinRefusal(t: UserConfig, w: UserConfig | null, way: JoinRecord['way']): Promise<string | null> {
  if (!w) return 'the other account is gone';
  if (w.id === t.id) return 'the same account';
  if (hasChat(w)) return 'the other account has a chat';
  if (w.pairingId !== null && w.pairingId === t.pairingId) return 'the two are partners';
  if ((await identityHolder(way.kind, way.subject)) !== w.id) return `the ${way.kind} way is no longer the other account's`;
  const refusals = await Promise.all([signInRefusal(t), signInRefusal(w)]);
  if (refusals[0]) return `this account is ${refusals[0]}`;
  if (refusals[1]) return `the other account is ${refusals[1]}`;
  return null;
}

function readRecord(raw: unknown): JoinRecord | null {
  if (!raw) return null;
  const record = (typeof raw === 'string' ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw) as Partial<JoinRecord>;
  return typeof record.tUserId === 'number' && typeof record.wUserId === 'number' && record.way && record.summary ? (record as JoinRecord) : null;
}

/**
 * The Join question for T, after T proved `way`, which W holds: its one-time id and what it shows, or null when there
 * is no join to offer (W has a chat, is T's partner, is gone, or either account is suspended or banned). Each null is
 * logged with the reason.
 */
export async function offerJoin(tUser: UserConfig, wUserId: number, way: JoinRecord['way']): Promise<{ joinId: string; summary: JoinSummary } | null> {
  const w = await getUserById(wUserId);
  const refusal = await joinRefusal(tUser, w, way);
  if (refusal || !w) {
    console.warn(`[join] user ${tUser.id}: no join offered for user ${wUserId} (${refusal})`);
    return null;
  }
  const { previewMerge } = await import('../account-linking');
  const summary: JoinSummary = { name: w.name, createdAt: w.createdAt.toISOString(), plan: await previewMerge(w.id, tUser.id) };
  const joinId = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64url');
  const record: JoinRecord = { tUserId: tUser.id, wUserId: w.id, way, summary };
  await redis.set(keyOf(joinId), JSON.stringify(record), { ex: JOIN_TTL_SEC });
  console.log(`[join] user ${tUser.id}: offered to join user ${w.id} (${way.kind})`);
  return { joinId, summary };
}

/** The question an id names, for T only, without using it up (the add-Google page shows it); null for a late, used, bad or another account's id. */
export async function peekJoin(tUserId: number, joinId: unknown): Promise<JoinSummary | null> {
  if (typeof joinId !== 'string' || !JOIN_ID.test(joinId)) return null;
  const record = readRecord(await redis.get(keyOf(joinId)));
  return record && record.tUserId === tUserId ? record.summary : null;
}

/**
 * The answer Join: the question is used up (GETDEL) whoever answers. 'expired' for a late, used or bad id; 'refused'
 * for another account's id, or when a check fails now (W got a chat, the two paired, a way moved, a suspension, a ban,
 * or the merge refused). Then W merges into T, T's feature access is read again, T gets the notice for the way it
 * gained, and the answer is T's ways now.
 */
export async function runJoin(tUserId: number, joinId: unknown): Promise<{ ok: true; methods: SignInMethodsView } | { ok: false; error: 'expired' | 'refused' }> {
  if (typeof joinId !== 'string' || !JOIN_ID.test(joinId)) {
    console.warn(`[join] user ${tUserId}: a Join answer with no valid question id`);
    return { ok: false, error: 'expired' };
  }
  const record = readRecord(await redis.getdel(keyOf(joinId)));
  if (!record) {
    console.warn(`[join] user ${tUserId}: the Join question expired or was used`);
    return { ok: false, error: 'expired' };
  }
  if (record.tUserId !== tUserId) {
    console.warn(`[join] user ${tUserId}: answered a Join question made for user ${record.tUserId}; used up, nothing joined`);
    return { ok: false, error: 'refused' };
  }
  const [t, w] = await Promise.all([getUserById(tUserId), getUserById(record.wUserId)]);
  const refusal = t ? await joinRefusal(t, w, record.way) : 'this account is gone';
  if (refusal || !t) {
    console.warn(`[join] user ${tUserId}: Join of user ${record.wUserId} refused (${refusal})`);
    return { ok: false, error: 'refused' };
  }
  const { mergeAccounts, MergeRefusedError } = await import('../account-linking');
  try {
    await mergeAccounts(record.wUserId, tUserId);
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof MergeRefusedError)) throw error;
    console.warn(`[join] user ${tUserId}: the merge refused user ${record.wUserId}: ${error.message}`);
    return { ok: false, error: 'refused' };
  }
  console.log(`[join] user ${record.wUserId} joined into user ${tUserId}`);
  await invalidateFeatureAccessCache(tUserId);
  const after = (await getUserById(tUserId)) ?? t;
  await sendSignInNotice(after, { kind: record.way.kind, address: record.way.address, via: 'joined' });
  return { ok: true, methods: await listSignInMethods(after) };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: The answer's route**

`app/api/signin-methods/join/route.ts`:

```ts
// Join (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.9, §3.6): the answer to the question Add Google or Add email ended on.
//
// POST /api/signin-methods/join?user_id=…  body { token } (the question's id: `token` so the log and Sentry scrubber
//   drops it)
//   → { ok: true, methods }: the other account is joined into this one, which gets the notice for the way it gained.
//   → { ok: false, error }: expired (410: late, used or not an id), refused (409: another account's question, or a
//     check failed now), failed (500).
//
// Security: Origin and JSON first, then verifyUserAuth (Telegram initData in the Mini App, the session cookie in a
// browser) with the settings limiter; the question must have been made for the proved account (runJoin). No log line
// holds the id.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { settingsRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { captureSignInFailure } from '@/src/services/web-signin/safe-error';
import { runJoin } from '@/src/services/web-signin/join';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    // A body that is not JSON is read as no body; the fact is logged, never the parse message
    const body = await request.json().catch(() => {
      console.warn('[signin-methods] the body is not JSON');
      return null;
    });
    const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id'), requestInitData(request, body), settingsRateLimiter, 'signin-methods-join');
    if (!auth.success) return auth.response;
    userId = auth.user.id;
    const result = await runJoin(auth.user.id, body?.token);
    if (result.ok) return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, methods: result.methods });
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: result.error }, { status: result.error === 'expired' ? 410 : 409 });
  } catch (error) {
    captureSignInFailure(error, 'signin-methods-join', { user_id: userId });
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: 'failed' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 13: The question's lines, one helper for both screens**

`src/lib/join-summary.ts`:

```ts
// The Join question's words (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.9): what moves, as lines of settings.signIn.join, from the
// dry run's plan (join.ts offerJoin). Settings' email sheet (a client) and the add-Google page (a server page) both
// render these, so the two show the same list. Client-safe: type imports only.

import type { MergePlan } from '../services/account-linking';
import type { JoinSummary } from '../services/web-signin/join';

export type { JoinSummary };

/** A line of the question: a key of settings.signIn.join and its numbers. */
export type JoinLine = {
  key: 'calendars' | 'wayGoogle' | 'wayEmail' | 'google' | 'googleStays' | 'partner' | 'partnerEnds' | 'plan';
  values?: { calendars: number; events: number };
};

/** What comes over, and what doesn't, in the order the question lists it. */
export function joinLines(plan: MergePlan): JoinLine[] {
  const lines: JoinLine[] = [{ key: 'calendars', values: { calendars: plan.calendars, events: plan.events } }];
  for (const kind of plan.ways) lines.push({ key: kind === 'google' ? 'wayGoogle' : 'wayEmail' });
  if (plan.google === 'moves') lines.push({ key: 'google' });
  if (plan.google === 'stays') lines.push({ key: 'googleStays' });
  if (plan.partner === 'moves') lines.push({ key: 'partner' });
  if (plan.partner === 'ends') lines.push({ key: 'partnerEnds' });
  if (plan.plan === 'moves') lines.push({ key: 'plan' });
  return lines;
}

/**
 * The day the other account was made, in words ("3 November 2026"), in Israel's time: an account made on famcal.bot
 * has no place yet, so the default zone is its zone. The same text on the server and in the browser.
 */
export function joinDateText(iso: string, locale: string): string {
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'Asia/Jerusalem' }).format(new Date(iso));
}

const isCount = (value: unknown) => typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0;

/** The shape the email confirm route answers a join with. */
export function isJoinSummary(value: unknown): value is JoinSummary {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return false;
  const v = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const plan = v.plan as Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined;
  return typeof v.name === 'string' && typeof v.createdAt === 'string' && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(v.createdAt))
    && !!plan && isCount(plan.calendars) && isCount(plan.events) && Array.isArray(plan.ways)
    && plan.ways.every(w => w === 'google' || w === 'email')
    && ['moves', 'stays', 'none'].includes(String(plan.google)) && ['moves', 'ends', 'none'].includes(String(plan.partner))
    && ['moves', 'stays'].includes(String(plan.plan));
}
```

```ts
export async function confirmEmail(
  userId: number,
  code: string,
): Promise<{ kind: 'ok'; methods: SignInMethodsView } | { kind: 'join'; joinId: string; summary: JoinSummary } | { kind: 'error'; code: ConfirmEmailError }> {
  const r = await post('/api/signin-methods/email/confirm', userId, { code });
  if (!r) return { kind: 'error', code: 'failed' };
  if (r.ok && r.body?.ok === true && isMethodsView(r.body.methods)) return { kind: 'ok', methods: r.body.methods };
  const error = r.body?.error;
  if (error === 'join' && typeof r.body?.joinId === 'string' && isJoinSummary(r.body.summary)) return { kind: 'join', joinId: r.body.joinId, summary: r.body.summary };
  if (error === 'wrong' || error === 'taken' || error === 'restart' || error === 'has-one') return { kind: 'error', code: error };
  if (error === 'limit') return { kind: 'error', code: 'codeLimit' };
  return { kind: 'error', code: statusError(r.status) };
}

/** Join: the answer to the question an Add email ended on. The question's id goes as `token` (the scrubber drops it). */
export async function joinAccount(userId: number, joinId: string): Promise<{ kind: 'ok'; methods: SignInMethodsView } | { kind: 'error'; code: JoinError }> {
  const r = await post('/api/signin-methods/join', userId, { token: joinId });
  if (!r) return { kind: 'error', code: 'failed' };
  if (r.ok && r.body?.ok === true && isMethodsView(r.body.methods)) return { kind: 'ok', methods: r.body.methods };
  const error = r.body?.error;
  if (error === 'expired' || error === 'refused') return { kind: 'error', code: error };
  return { kind: 'error', code: statusError(r.status) };
}
```
