- [ ] **Step 15: The add-Google landing asks it in the browser**

The page is a server component (dynamic, noindex), so it reads the session cookie and the question, and renders the question in `settings.signIn.join`'s words; only the buttons are a client. Mobile first: the panel and the 44 px buttons of the sign-in pages, a plain list with logical padding (RTL correct), no hover.

`app/[locale]/(site)/signin/add-google/join/page.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';
import { getTranslations, setRequestLocale } from 'next-intl/server';
import { SitePage } from '@/components/site/SitePage';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { joinDateText, joinLines, type JoinSummary } from '@/src/lib/join-summary';
import { SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, validateSessionToken } from '@/src/lib/session-auth';
import { peekJoin } from '@/src/services/web-signin/join';
import { siteMetadata } from '@/src/site/seo';
import { JoinClient } from './JoinClient';

// /signin/add-google/join?token= (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.9, §3.6): where Add Google lands when the Google
// account belongs to an account made on famcal.bot with no chat. Google's callback has signed this browser in as the
// account that made the Add Google link (finishAddGoogle), so the question is shown only to that session: peekJoin
// reads the question for the session's account and never uses it up. The question and what moves are
// settings.signIn.join's words (the Settings sheet asks the same), the buttons are JoinClient's. A late, used or bad id,
// or another browser, says to start again. Rendered per request, kept out of search. The id is never logged.

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

type Props = {
  params: Promise<{ locale: string }>;
  searchParams: Promise<Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>>;
};

export async function generateMetadata({ params }: { params: Promise<{ locale: string }> }): Promise<Metadata> {
  const { locale } = await params;
  const t = await getTranslations({ locale });
  const meta = siteMetadata({ locale, path: '/signin/add-google/join', title: t('site.signin.addGoogle.join.metaTitle'), description: t('site.signin.metaDescription'), imageAlt: t('landing.meta.ogImageAlt') });
  delete meta.alternates;
  return { ...meta, robots: { index: false, follow: false } };
}

type Question = { kind: 'ok'; userId: number; summary: JoinSummary } | { kind: 'gone' } | { kind: 'failed' };

/** The question this browser's session may answer: one cookie check and one Redis read, only when a person opens it. */
async function readQuestion(token: string | null): Promise<Question> {
  if (!token) return { kind: 'gone' };
  try {
    const cookie = (await cookies()).get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value;
    const session = cookie ? validateSessionToken(cookie) : null;
    if (!session) return { kind: 'gone' };
    const summary = await peekJoin(session.userId, token);
    return summary ? { kind: 'ok', userId: session.userId, summary } : { kind: 'gone' };
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'join-page', { service: 'web-signin' });
    return { kind: 'failed' };
  }
}

export default async function JoinPage({ params, searchParams }: Props) {
  const { locale } = await params;
  setRequestLocale(locale);
  const raw = (await searchParams).token;
  const token = typeof raw === 'string' ? raw : null;
  const question = await readQuestion(token);
  const t = await getTranslations({ locale });
  return (
    <SitePage locale={locale} path="/signin">
      <main id="main" className="site-section site-page-main">
        <div className="site-wrap site-signin">
          {question.kind === 'gone' ? (
            <>
              <h1 className="site-h1 site-page-title">{t('site.signin.addGoogle.join.expiredTitle')}</h1>
              <p className="site-lead">{t('site.signin.addGoogle.join.expired')}</p>
            </>
          ) : question.kind === 'failed' ? (
            <>
              <h1 className="site-h1 site-page-title">{t('settings.signIn.join.title')}</h1>
              <p className="site-signin-notice" role="alert">
                {t('site.signin.addGoogle.loadFailed')}
              </p>
            </>
          ) : (
            <>
              <h1 className="site-h1 site-page-title">{t('settings.signIn.join.title')}</h1>
              <div className="site-signin-panel">
                <p>{t('settings.signIn.join.question', { kind: 'google', name: question.summary.name, date: joinDateText(question.summary.createdAt, locale) })}</p>
                <p className="site-signin-moves-title">{t('settings.signIn.join.movesTitle')}</p>
                <ul className="site-signin-moves">
                  {joinLines(question.summary.plan).map((line) => (
                    <li key={line.key}>{t(`settings.signIn.join.${line.key}`, line.values)}</li>
                  ))}
                </ul>
                <p>{t('settings.signIn.join.closes')}</p>
              </div>
              {token ? <JoinClient userId={question.userId} token={token} /> : null}
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      </main>
    </SitePage>
  );
}
```

```tsx
'use client';

// The Join question's buttons on /signin/add-google/join (web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §3.6): Join posts the question's
// id (as `token`, which the scrubber drops) to /api/signin-methods/join with this browser's session cookie; Cancel joins
// nothing and changes nothing (the question expires by itself). After either, Open your calendar goes to the account's
// calendar. A late or used question (410) and a refused one (409) have their words; any other failure says so and the
// button works again. The id is never logged.

import { useState } from 'react';
import { useLocale, useTranslations } from 'next-intl';
import { Loader2 } from 'lucide-react';
import { readJsonBody } from '@/src/lib/read-json';
import { localeHref } from '@/src/site/zmanim/links';
import { normalizeLocale } from '@/src/utils/locale';

const TAG = '[join]';

type State = 'idle' | 'busy' | 'done' | 'cancelled' | 'expired' | 'refused' | 'failed';

export function JoinClient({ userId, token }: { userId: number; token: string }) {
  const t = useTranslations('site.signin.addGoogle.join');
  const locale = useLocale();
  const [state, setState] = useState<State>('idle');
  const calendar = localeHref(normalizeLocale(locale), `/dashboard?user_id=${userId}`);

  const join = async () => {
    if (state === 'busy') return;
    setState('busy');
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/signin-methods/join?user_id=${userId}`, {
        method: 'POST',
        credentials: 'same-origin',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ token }),
      });
      const body = await readJsonBody(res, `${TAG} answer`);
      if (res.ok && body?.ok === true) {
        setState('done');
        return;
      }
      console.warn(`${TAG} the answer was ${res.status}`);
      setState(res.status === 410 ? 'expired' : res.status === 409 ? 'refused' : 'failed');
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`${TAG} the answer failed:`, error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error);
      setState('failed');
    }
  };

  if (state === 'done' || state === 'cancelled' || state === 'expired' || state === 'refused') {
    return (
      <div className="site-signin-panel">
        <p role="status">{t(state)}</p>
        <a className="site-signin-way site-signin-continue" data-way="submit" href={calendar}>
          {t('openCalendar')}
        </a>
      </div>
    );
  }
  const busy = state === 'busy';
  return (
    <div className="site-signin-panel">
      {state === 'failed' ? (
        <p className="site-field-error" role="alert">
          {t('failed')}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      <button type="button" className="site-signin-way site-signin-continue" data-way="submit" disabled={busy} aria-busy={busy || undefined} onClick={() => void join()}>
        {busy ? <Loader2 className="site-icon site-spin" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" /> : null}
        {busy ? t('joining') : t('join')}
      </button>
      <div className="site-signin-links">
        <button type="button" className="site-signin-link" disabled={busy} onClick={() => setState('cancelled')}>
          {t('cancel')}
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Row locks in the shared smoke world**

A transaction's client now holds the user rows it locks with `SELECT id FROM "User" WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` until it ends, and a second transaction asking for the same row waits, as Postgres does; `lockWaits` records each wait. Any other raw query is refused, so a smoke shows what it needs. Without the lock in the code, two removals at once both read two ways and both delete (#52 sees no way left).

with:

```ts
}

/**
 * Row locks, as Postgres holds them: `SELECT … FROM "User" WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` inside an interactive transaction
 * waits while another open transaction holds that row, and the lock is let go when its transaction ends. Every other
 * raw query the code sends is refused, so a smoke shows what it needs.
 */
const rowLocks = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
export const lockWaits: string[] = [];
async function queryRaw(held: (() => void)[] | null, strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]): Promise<Row[]> {
  const sql = strings.join('?').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  prismaCalls.push(`$queryRaw ${sql}`);
  if (!/^SELECT "?id"? FROM "User" WHERE "?id"? = \? FOR UPDATE$/i.test(sql)) throw new Error(`the fake Prisma does not know this raw query: ${sql}`);
  const key = `User:${String(values[0])}`;
  if (held) {
    while (rowLocks.has(key)) {
      lockWaits.push(key);
      await rowLocks.get(key);
    }
    let release!: () => void;
    rowLocks.set(key, new Promise<void>(resolve => { release = resolve; }));
    held.push(() => { rowLocks.delete(key); release(); });
  }
  return (DB.user ?? []).filter(u => same(u.id, values[0])).map(u => ({ id: u.id }));
}
```

```ts
      return async (arg: unknown) => {
        prismaCalls.push('$transaction');
        if (typeof arg !== 'function') return Promise.all(arg as Promise<unknown>[]);
        // The callback's client: the same tables, and the locks it takes held until it returns or throws
        const held: (() => void)[] = [];
        const tx = new Proxy({} as Row, {
          get: (_x, p) => (p === '$queryRaw' ? (s: TemplateStringsArray, ...v: unknown[]) => queryRaw(held, s, ...v) : fakePrisma[p as string]),
        });
        try {
          return await arg(tx);
        } finally {
          for (const release of held) release();
        }
      };
    }
    if (prop === '$queryRaw') return (s: TemplateStringsArray, ...v: unknown[]) => queryRaw(null, s, ...v);
```

```ts
}

/** The durable ways of an account, from its row and the kinds of its sign-in ways. */
function durableWays(user: { telegramId: unknown; whatsappPhone?: string | null; whatsappBsuid?: string | null }, kinds: string[]): DurableWay[] {
  const ways: DurableWay[] = [];
  if (user.telegramId !== null && user.telegramId !== undefined) ways.push('telegram');
  if (user.whatsappPhone || user.whatsappBsuid) ways.push('whatsapp');
  for (const kind of ['google', 'email'] as const) if (kinds.includes(kind)) ways.push(kind);
  return ways;
}

/**
 * Where a notice goes for an account with no chat (notice.ts): its email way's address, else its Google way's, skipping
 * the kind just added (`gained`: the notice must reach a way that was there before). null when there is none.
 */
export async function noticeAddress(userId: number, gained: IdentityKind | null): Promise<{ kind: IdentityKind; address: string } | null> {
  const rows = await prisma.signInIdentity.findMany({ where: { userId }, select: { kind: true, address: true } });
  for (const kind of ['email', 'google'] as const) {
    const row = kind === gained ? undefined : rows.find(r => r.kind === kind);
    if (row) return { kind, address: row.address };
  }
  return null;
}
```

```ts
 * person in; the lawyer review, finding 10). A removal that changed something ends every web
 * session: sessionsValidAfter is now (the route gives the device it came from a fresh cookie). One that found nothing
 * to remove (no such way, the calendar switch already off) changes nothing and signs nobody out. Returns whether
 * something changed.
 */
export async function removeSignInMethod(userId: number, which: RemovableWay): Promise<boolean> {
  return prisma.$transaction(async tx => {
    const deleted = which === 'calendar-google' ? 0 : (await tx.signInIdentity.deleteMany({ where: { userId, kind: which } })).count;
    const user = await tx.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId }, select: { googleCalendarSignIn: true } });
    const switchWasOn = which !== 'email' && user?.googleCalendarSignIn === true;
    if (deleted === 0 && !switchWasOn) return false;
    await tx.user.update({
      where: { id: userId },
      data: { sessionsValidAfter: new Date(), ...(which === 'email' ? {} : { googleCalendarSignIn: false, googleAccountKey: null }) },
    });
    return true;
  }).then(changed => {
    console.log(`[signin] user ${userId}: the ${which} way was ${changed ? 'removed; every web session ends' : 'not there; nothing changed'}`);
    return changed;
  });
}
```

with:

```ts
 * person in; the lawyer review, finding 10). A removal that changed something ends every web
 * session: sessionsValidAfter is now (the route gives the device it came from a fresh cookie). One that found nothing
 * to remove (no such way, the calendar switch already off) changes nothing and signs nobody out.
 *
 * The account's only durable way (DurableWay; web sign-up spec §2.12) is never removed: 'last-way'. The account's row
 * is locked first (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), so a second removal at the same moment waits for this one and then counts
 * what is left: two removals at once can't take the last two ways. The calendar's row ('calendar-google') is no
 * durable way and is always removable.
 */
export async function removeSignInMethod(userId: number, which: RemovableWay): Promise<'removed' | 'last-way' | 'none'> {
  const outcome = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx): Promise<'removed' | 'last-way' | 'none'> => {
    await tx.$queryRaw`SELECT id FROM "User" WHERE id = ${userId} FOR UPDATE`;
    const user = await tx.user.findUnique({
      where: { id: userId },
      select: { telegramId: true, whatsappPhone: true, whatsappBsuid: true, googleCalendarSignIn: true },
    });
    if (!user) return 'none';
    const kinds = (await tx.signInIdentity.findMany({ where: { userId }, select: { kind: true } })).map(r => r.kind);
    const holds = which !== 'calendar-google' && kinds.includes(which);
    const switchWasOn = which !== 'email' && user.googleCalendarSignIn === true;
    if (!holds && !switchWasOn) return 'none';
    if (holds && durableWays(user, kinds).length <= 1) return 'last-way';
    if (holds) await tx.signInIdentity.deleteMany({ where: { userId, kind: which } });
    await tx.user.update({
      where: { id: userId },
      data: { sessionsValidAfter: new Date(), ...(which === 'email' ? {} : { googleCalendarSignIn: false, googleAccountKey: null }) },
    });
    return 'removed';
  });
  const said = { removed: 'removed; every web session ends', 'last-way': 'not removed: it is the last way to sign in', none: 'not there; nothing changed' };
  console.log(`[signin] user ${userId}: the ${which} way was ${said[outcome]}`);
  return outcome;
}
```

```ts
/** The notice email: the subject as its heading, the notice's lines, the footer, in `locale`. */
export function noticeEmail(subject: string, lines: string[], locale: string): CodeEmail {
  const lang = normalizeLocale(locale);
  const footer = WORDS[lang].footer;
  const text = [subject, ...lines, footer].join('\n\n');
  const html = emailHtml(lang, subject, heading(subject) + lines.map(line => paragraph(line)).join('') + paragraph(footer, 'font-size:13px'));
  return { subject, text, html };
}

/**
 * One email to Resend, `what` naming it in the log lines (never the address): the Resend id once it took it. Throws
 * when it refused (any 4xx, at once), or a 429/5xx or no answer ran out of retries, after one line with the user id and
 * status.
 */
async function postEmail(args: { apiKey: string; to: string; email: CodeEmail; idempotencyKey: string; what: string; userId: number }): Promise<string> {
  const { subject, text, html } = args.email;
  const response = await fetchWithRetry(
    RESEND_EMAILS_URL,
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${args.apiKey}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        // One key per email, the same on every retry of it: Resend keeps it 24 hours and sends once.
        'Idempotency-Key': args.idempotencyKey,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ from: SIGNIN_FROM, to: [args.to], reply_to: SIGNIN_REPLY_TO, subject, text, html }),
    },
    {
      label: '[signin-email]',
      onGiveUp: (error, { retried, why }) => {
        const status = error instanceof HttpStatusError ? `status ${error.status}` : 'no answer';
        console.error(`[signin-email] gave up on the ${args.what} for user ${args.userId}: ${status}, ${why} (${retried} retries)`);
      },
    }
  );
  let id = 'unknown';
  try {
    const answer = (await response.json()) as { id?: unknown };
    if (typeof answer.id === 'string') id = answer.id;
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn(`[signin-email] Resend took the ${args.what} for user ${args.userId}, but its answer was unreadable: ${safeErrorSummary(error)}`);
  }
  console.log(`[signin-email] sent the ${args.what} for user ${args.userId} (Resend id ${id})`);
  return id;
}
```

```ts
/** Why a notice email was not sent before Resend was asked: takeNoticeSend's refusal (Task 4). */
export type NoticeRefusal = 'notice-account-day' | 'notice-budget' | 'store-down';

/**
 * Mails a security notice (notice.ts) to `to`: an address the account already signs in with, never typed text, never
 * the way just added. It takes from the notices' own budget first (takeNoticeSend(userId), apart from the codes' 90):
 * the account's 3 a UTC day, then the day's 10 in all. When that refuses, nothing is sent and the answer is the reason:
 * 'notice-account-day' (this account's are spent), 'notice-budget' (the day's 10 are spent) or 'store-down' (Redis
 * failed). 'sent' once Resend took it; throws when it refused or ran out of retries (logged here), so the caller reports
 * the notice as not sent.
 */
export async function sendNoticeEmail(args: { to: string; locale: string; subject: string; lines: string[]; userId: number }): Promise<'sent' | NoticeRefusal> {
  const apiKey = process.env.RESEND_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) throw new SafeSignInError('RESEND_API_KEY is not set: no notice email can be sent');
  const taken = await takeNoticeSend(args.userId);
  if (!taken.ok) return taken.reason;
  await postEmail({
    apiKey,
    to: args.to,
    email: noticeEmail(args.subject, args.lines, args.locale),
    idempotencyKey: `signin-notice-${crypto.randomUUID()}`,
    what: 'notice',
    userId: args.userId,
  });
  return 'sent';
}
```

Replace the whole file:

`src/services/web-signin/notice.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The notice that a way into the account was added (web sign-in spec §2.10, web sign-up spec 2026-11-03 §2.11): a
 * Google or email way added in Settings, the calendar's Google account used for the first time (§2.17), the ways a
 * Join brought in, or Telegram connected to an account made on famcal.bot. So a stolen session can't add a way
 * quietly, it goes to the ways that were there BEFORE the change, never to the one just added:
 * - an account with a chat: the chat, Telegram when it has it, else WhatsApp (the phone, else the BSUID), as in 6b;
 * - an account with no chat (hasChat, src/lib/has-chat.ts), and every Telegram connect (the chat is the new way): by
 *   email to the account's email way, else to its Google way's address, never the way of the kind just added
 *   (sendNoticeEmail, with the notices' own budget: 3 a day per account, then 10 a day in all).
 * A Google or email notice names the way with the address masked (maskEmail) and says where to remove it; Telegram
 * can't be removed in Settings, so its notice says to write to privacy@famcal.bot.
 *
 * It is the answer to the person's own action, so the Shabbat pause doesn't hold it (CLAUDE.md; scripts/smoke-pause.ts
 * lists this file and email-send.ts as NOT_PAUSED). On WhatsApp a free-form text outside the person's 24-hour window is
 * accepted by Meta and rejected later (131047), which the webhook's status handler logs. A notice that can't go out
 * (no address to send to, the account's or the day's notices spent, the mail or the chat refused) is a security event: one
 * `[signin-notice] SECURITY:` line and a captured warning. It never throws: the way is made either way. No log line
 * holds an address.
 */

import enMessages from '../../../messages/en.json';
import heMessages from '../../../messages/he.json';
import ruMessages from '../../../messages/ru.json';
import { captureError } from '../../lib/error-capture';
import { hasChat } from '../../lib/has-chat';
import { SafeSignInError, safeErrorSummary } from './safe-error';
import { normalizeLocale, type Locale } from '../../utils/locale';
import { getWhatsAppChatId } from '../user-service';
import { getWhatsAppService } from '../messaging';
import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import { maskEmail } from './email-address';
import { sendNoticeEmail, type NoticeRefusal } from './email-send';
import { noticeAddress, type IdentityKind } from './identities';

export type SignInNoticeEvent =
  | {
      kind: IdentityKind;
      /** The way's address, as stored; the notice shows it masked */
      address: string;
      /** added: from Settings; calendar: the first sign-in with the calendar's Google account; joined: the way came with the account Join brought in */
      via: 'added' | 'calendar' | 'joined';
    }
  | { kind: 'telegram'; via: 'connected' };

type NoticeCopy = typeof enMessages.signinNotice;
const WORDS: Record<Locale, NoticeCopy> = {
  en: enMessages.signinNotice,
  he: heMessages.signinNotice,
  ru: ruMessages.signinNotice,
};

/** The notice's text in the person's language. */
function noticeText(copy: NoticeCopy, event: SignInNoticeEvent): string {
  if (event.kind === 'telegram') return copy.telegramConnected;
  const template = event.via === 'calendar' ? copy.calendarGoogle
    : event.via === 'joined' ? (event.kind === 'google' ? copy.joinedGoogle : copy.joinedEmail)
    : event.kind === 'google' ? copy.addedGoogle : copy.addedEmail;
  return template.replace('{address}', maskEmail(event.address));
}

/** Each refusal of the notices' budget, as the SECURITY line says it. */
const REFUSED: Record<NoticeRefusal, string> = {
  'notice-account-day': "the account's notices are spent",
  'notice-budget': "the day's notices are spent",
  'store-down': "the notices' count could not be read",
};

/** A notice that did not go out: the security line and a captured warning, with the user id and why only. */
function dropped(user: UserConfig, what: string, why: string): void {
  console.error(`[signin-notice] SECURITY: notice for user ${user.id} not sent (${why})`);
  captureError(new SafeSignInError(`signin-notice not sent: ${why}`), 'signin-notice', { user_id: user.id, purpose: what }, 'warning');
}

export async function sendSignInNotice(user: UserConfig, event: SignInNoticeEvent): Promise<void> {
  const what = `${event.kind} (${event.via})`;
  try {
    const copy = WORDS[normalizeLocale(user.language)];
    const text = noticeText(copy, event);

    // The chat, when it was there before: never for a Telegram connect, whose chat is the way just added
    if (event.kind !== 'telegram' && hasChat(user)) {
      if (user.telegramId) {
        // Loaded here, as google-connect.ts does: the bot module pulls in the whole Telegram client
        const { getMessagingService } = await import('../telegram/bot');
        await getMessagingService().sendMessage(user.telegramId, text);
        console.log(`[signin-notice] user ${user.id}: the ${what} notice was sent on Telegram`);
        return;
      }
      // hasChat without Telegram is WhatsApp: the phone, else the BSUID
      const chatId = getWhatsAppChatId(user);
      if (chatId) {
        await getWhatsAppService().sendMessage(chatId, text);
        console.log(`[signin-notice] user ${user.id}: the ${what} notice was sent on WhatsApp`);
        return;
      }
    }

    // No chat before: the account's email way, else its Google way's address, never the kind just added
    const to = await noticeAddress(user.id, event.kind === 'telegram' ? null : event.kind);
    if (!to) {
      dropped(user, what, 'no address to send it to');
      return;
    }
    const subject = event.kind === 'telegram' ? copy.emailSubjectTelegram : copy.emailSubject;
    const outcome = await sendNoticeEmail({ to: to.address, locale: user.language, subject, lines: [text, copy.emailWhy], userId: user.id });
    if (outcome !== 'sent') {
      dropped(user, what, REFUSED[outcome]);
      return;
    }
    console.log(`[signin-notice] user ${user.id}: the ${what} notice was emailed to the ${to.kind} way`);
  } catch (error) {
    dropped(user, what, safeErrorSummary(error));
  }
}
```

```ts
export async function removeMethod(userId: number, which: RemoveWhich): Promise<{ kind: 'ok'; methods: SignInMethodsView } | { kind: 'error'; code: RemoveError }> {
  const r = await post('/api/signin-methods/remove', userId, { which });
  if (r?.ok && r.body?.ok === true && isMethodsView(r.body.methods)) return { kind: 'ok', methods: r.body.methods };
  if (r?.body?.error === 'last-way') return { kind: 'error', code: 'last-way' };
  return { kind: 'error', code: r ? statusError(r.status) : 'failed' };
}
```

### Task 9: What a browser-only account sees

#### Notes for Task 9 (read first)

**Contract notes (corrections and additions against the real code, and the rulings for this part):**

1. **`hasChat(user)` is Task 1's** (`src/lib/has-chat.ts`, ruling #1). Task 9 imports it in page-data and writes no "has a chat" helper or test of its own. Why: one rule; a `UserConfig` has `undefined`, not `null`, for a missing WhatsApp id.
2. **`hasChat` on the client is `hasChat?: boolean`**: `false` means no chat, and absent means "as before". This applies to `CalendarHomeProps`, `SettingsClient` and `SubscriptionClient`. About twenty existing smoke fixtures build these props without the field and keep passing unchanged. `DashboardPageProps.hasChat` is required, and page-data always sends it for the dashboard, Settings and Plans.
3. **`SignInMethods` reads `view.chat`** (ruling #14): Task 8 adds `chat: boolean` to `SignInMethodsView`, and `isMethodsView` requires it (and `lastWay`), so every `GET /api/signin-methods` fixture here carries both. There is no `hasChat` prop on `SignInMethods`. Why: one fact, one way to Settings' sign-in group.
4. **`openTelegramConnect(userId)` returns `'opened' | 'stale-sign-in' | 'limit' | 'failed'`.** The contract has no `'limit'`, but the 5-links-an-hour refusal needs its own words. The same file also exports `type ConnectPhase`, `useTelegramConnect(userId, locale)`, `connectButtonKey(phase)` and `connectLineKey(phase)`, the one state machine the three surfaces share. It reads Task 6's route as Task 6 answers (ruling #26): `200 { url }`; `409 { error: 'has-chat' }`; `403 { error: 'stale-sign-in' }`; `429 { error: 'limit' }`; `503 { error: 'unavailable' }` (`500 { error: 'unavailable' }` on a throw); `401` with no session. The client reads the status and `body.error`: `stale-sign-in` or a 401 is `'stale-sign-in'`, `limit` or a 429 is `'limit'`, anything else is `'failed'`.
5. **Sign in again means signing out first.** `/signin` sends a browser that holds a valid-looking cookie straight to its calendar (`app/[locale]/(site)/signin/page.tsx:24`), so a bare link would loop. `src/lib/sign-in-again.ts` (new) posts `/api/auth/signout`, which clears the cookie with no DB query, and then opens `signInHref(locale)`. Both the stale-sign-in Connect button and the "Your sign-in has ended" lines use it.
6. **The browser words have their own keys.** The new ones are `calendarHome.send.signedOutBrowser` and `calendarsPage.errors.reopenBrowser`, chosen by `sessionEndedKey(isInTelegram())` in `sign-in-again.ts`. The Sign in button reuses `pageGate.signIn`. The button is added where the failure shows in a Notice: the Send sheet, the Calendars delete step and the Select calendars status bar. A SaveBar or field error keeps the text only. A reload there reaches the page gate, whose card leads with Sign in.
7. **The page gate's browser card gets its own words**, `pageGate.signInTitle` and `pageGate.signInBody`. `pageGate.browserTitle`, `browserBody` and `browserTelegramHint` stay as they are, because `/refresh-token`'s gate also reads them (`app/(connect)/refresh-token/RefreshTokenClient.tsx:105`). `smoke-miniapp-gate` #7 and `smoke-app-ui` #9 are updated to the new keys.
8. **The missing-link card in a browser** (ruling #20): `MissingParameterCard` (`components/app-ui/StateCard.tsx`, shown by Settings, Calendars, Select calendars, Pair, Feedback, the admin panel, share-story and `/refresh-token` opened without `user_id`) shows `ui.missingParameter.bodyBrowser` with Sign in (`pageGate.signIn`, a link to `signInHref(locale)`) outside Telegram. It reads the place with `useSyncExternalStore(…, isInTelegram, () => true)`, as `CalendarHome` does, so the server's markup and the first render that hydrates it are the card as it was, and the existing server-render checks (`smoke-app-ui` #7b, `smoke-miniapp-gate` #20, `smoke-connect-screens`) are unchanged. `smoke-share-story` H3b mounts it with no SDK and is updated. Why: spec §2.13, a browser-only account sees no copy that sends it back to a chat. A signed-in browser that presses Sign in lands on its calendar, because `/signin` sends it there.
9. **One namespace, `telegramConnect.*`, holds the Connect words**: `action`, `opening`, `signInAgain`, `opened`, `limit` and `failed`. The banner, Settings (the note card and Sign in on the web) and Plans all read it. The banner's title is `telegramConnect.action`, so there is no `calendarHome.banner.connectTelegram`. Its own keys are `calendarHome.banner.connectTelegramBody` and `calendarHome.banner.close`.
10. **The "editor hint" is the empty home's hint** (`AgendaView`'s `EmptyState`). The editor has no bot copy. `HomeHints` gains `addByTap?: boolean`, which the home sets from `hasChat` (`shownHints`). page-data's `hints` stay `{ reminders, voiceEvents }`, because `smoke-page-auth` #11 pins their keys.
11. **The Settings events card with no chat.** The reminder-time row still shows when `nativeRemindersSupported`: a no-chat account whose partner has Telegram gets pings through the partner (`support.ts` `canReceiveReminderPings`). The Events section shows only then. The note card has no section label of its own, because the card's title says it all.
12. **`SignInMethods.tsx` and the `settings.signIn` words are the files as Tasks 7–8 leave them.** Task 9 touches only the header comment, the import line (Task 8's, with `type RemoveError`), the hooks after `status`, the hint row, the Telegram row block and one Notice after `status`. Tasks 7–8 own the join sheet, the `lastWay` rows, the remove sheet and the keys after `added`; Task 9's two `settings.signIn` keys sit above all of them.
13. **The Settings sign-in hint with no chat** says only "Open FamCal in any browser at famcal.bot." (`settings.signIn.hintNoChat`). The old hint ends "Telegram and WhatsApp keep working as they do", which makes no sense for an account that has neither.
14. **The invite page is Task 11's alone** (ruling #7): Task 9 doesn't edit `InviteClient.tsx`, adds no `invite.*` key and no invite check. Why: Task 11 replaces the whole file and adds `invite.errorGenericWeb`.
15. **One runner** (ruling #9): every single smoke runs as `$RUN <name>`, the header's `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-razielgershoni-development-famcalbot/0d239296-a217-49f9-8833-757c9d9a2df6/scratchpad/6c1/run-smoke.sh <name>`.
16. **Before-blocks** (ruling #8) are main at edd9d72e plus Tasks 1–8's edits. Re-read each file before an edit; when a block doesn't match, make the same change on the current text and keep the earlier tasks' code.

**Design (frontend-design, applied inside the app's existing look):**

- **No new palette or type.** Everything uses the home's and the kit's tokens: `--ch-accent-soft` (the Telegram banner's ground, as the old banner), `--ch-accent`, `--ch-muted`, `--ch-danger`, `--ch-surface`. The font is inherited, and every size is in px and at least 11.
- **The Connect banner keeps the old Telegram banner's shape**, so the home does not change character. It has the paper-plane icon (Lucide `Send`, flipped in RTL), a title and a one-line reason ("For reminders and briefings").
  - It is the only banner with a close: a quiet 44 px Lucide `X` at the end edge.
  - The whole banner can't be one `<button>` with a close inside, so it is a `div.ch-banner` holding two buttons.
  - A press shows Lucide `Loader2` spinning where the chevron was.
  - The outcome line sits under the banner: muted for "Finish in Telegram…", the danger colour as an alert for a refusal.
- **Settings' note card is the kit's own parts.** A `FormRow` carries the title and body, with the accent action row ("Connect Telegram") under it, the same as Add Google and Add email in Sign in on the web. There are no new classes.
- **Plans has one static Notice** with its action. The line under it uses the same words as everywhere else.
- **The missing-link card** (`MissingParameterCard`) keeps its look: in a browser its body is the browser's words and its one action is the kit's primary link, Sign in.
- **Accessibility and layout:**
  - Every tap target is 44 px.
  - There are no hover styles, and only logical properties.
  - The close has an `aria-label`.
  - `aria-busy` is set while a request runs.
  - The spinner is `ch-spin`, which the screen CSS already slows for reduced motion.
  - No emoji anywhere.

```ts
const settle = () =>
  act(async () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
  });

// ---- Fixtures ----

const settingsValues = (locale: Locale) => ({
  language: locale,
  gender: 'male',
  location: 'Tel Aviv',
  messagingPlatform: 'telegram',
  culture: 'jewish',
  textSummaryEnabled: true,
  voiceSummaryEnabled: false,
  weatherEnabled: true,
  includeLookaheadInTomorrow: false,
  lookaheadAlways7Days: false,
  preferredMorningHour: 7,
  preferredEveningHour: 20,
  dailySummaryDays: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
  tomorrowSummaryDays: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6],
  remindersEnabled: true,
  defaultReminderMinutes: 15,
  reminderTime: '09:15',
  pickupRemindersEnabled: false,
  voiceInputEnabled: false,
  pauseOnShabbat: true,
  zmanimCommunity: 'sephardi',
});
/** Settings for a browser-only account on a trial whose plan has no alerts (the chat account sees the Pro notice). */
const settingsProps = (locale: Locale, over: Row = {}): Row => ({
  userId: 1,
  currentSettings: settingsValues(locale),
  weekStart: 0,
  remindersGloballyEnabled: true,
  googleConnected: false,
  nativeRemindersSupported: false,
  subscriptionInfo: { effectivePlan: 'BASIC', textSummariesUsed: 0, textSummariesLimit: -1, voiceSummariesUsed: 0, voiceSummariesLimit: -1, remindersAllowed: false, isTrialing: false },
  bothChannels: false,
  hasChat: false,
  ...over,
});
/** Plans on a trial (both cards can be chosen), for a browser-only account. */
const planProps = (locale: Locale, over: Row = {}): Row => ({
  userId: 41,
  locale,
  subscription: { plan: 'FREE', status: 'TRIALING', effectivePlan: 'PRO', currentPeriodEnd: null, cancelAtPeriodEnd: false },
  usage: { textSummaries: 0, voiceSummaries: 0, voiceEvents: 0, reminders: 0, cycleStartDate: '2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z' },
  trial: { isTrialing: true, daysRemaining: 9, trialEndsAt: '2026-11-18T10:00:00.000Z' },
  isEarlyAdopter: false,
  calendarsUsed: 1,
  telegramLinked: false,
  hasChat: false,
  ...over,
});
const LINKS = { whatsapp: 'https://wa.me/972500000000?text=settings', telegram: 'https://t.me/test_bot?start=dashboard' };

/** The new keys of this task. */
const NEW_KEYS = [
  'calendarHome.banner.connectTelegramBody',
  'calendarHome.banner.close',
  'calendarHome.empty.hintBrowser',
  'calendarHome.send.signedOutBrowser',
  'calendarsPage.errors.reopenBrowser',
  'pageGate.signInTitle',
  'pageGate.signInBody',
  'ui.missingParameter.bodyBrowser',
  'subscription.screen.connectTelegram',
  'settings.noChat.title',
  'settings.noChat.body',
  'settings.signIn.hintNoChat',
  'settings.signIn.telegramConnectHint',
  'telegramConnect.action',
  'telegramConnect.opening',
  'telegramConnect.signInAgain',
  'telegramConnect.opened',
  'telegramConnect.limit',
  'telegramConnect.failed',
];
/** The words a browser reads in place of the chat's: none may send it to the bot. */
const BROWSER_KEYS = ['calendarHome.empty.hintBrowser', 'calendarHome.send.signedOutBrowser', 'calendarsPage.errors.reopenBrowser', 'pageGate.signInTitle', 'pageGate.signInBody', 'ui.missingParameter.bodyBrowser', 'settings.signIn.hintNoChat'];

async function main() {
  const connectClient = await import('../src/lib/telegram-connect-client');
  const signInAgainModule = await import('../src/lib/sign-in-again');
  const { homeBanners } = await import('../app/[locale]/(app)/dashboard/HomeBanners');
  const storage = await import('../src/lib/calendar-view/home-storage');
  const Settings = (await import('../app/[locale]/(app)/settings/SettingsClient')).default as unknown as (props: Row) => ReactElement;
  const Subscription = (await import('../app/[locale]/(app)/subscription/SubscriptionClient')).default as unknown as (props: Row) => ReactElement;
  const { NoCredentialCard } = (await import('../app/[locale]/(app)/PageGate')) as unknown as { NoCredentialCard: (props: Row) => ReactElement };
  const { MissingParameterCard } = await import('../components/app-ui/StateCard');
  const { openTelegramConnect, connectButtonKey, connectLineKey } = connectClient;
  const { signInAgain, sessionEndedKey } = signInAgainModule;

  const inApp = (locale: Locale, el: ReactElement) =>
    createElement(AppRouterContext.Provider, { value: router }, createElement(NextIntlClientProvider, { locale, messages: messages[locale], timeZone: 'Asia/Jerusalem' } as never, el));
  const mountIn = (locale: Locale, component: (p: Row) => ReactElement, props: Row): Mounted => mount(inApp(locale, createElement(component, props)));

  await check('B1 the pure parts: the Connect Telegram banner for no chat outside Telegram until closed, Open FamCal in Telegram still for WhatsApp-only; the close flag per account on the device (a storage that throws reads as not closed); the Connect words by phase; the session-ended words by place', () => {
    const base = { googleState: 'none' as const, googleConnected: false, reconnect: null, inTelegram: false };
    const cases: [Row, string[]][] = [
      [{ hasTelegram: false, hasChat: false }, ['connectTelegram']],
      [{ hasTelegram: false, hasChat: false, connectClosed: true }, []],
      [{ hasTelegram: false, hasChat: false, inTelegram: true }, []],
      [{ hasTelegram: false, hasChat: true }, ['openInTelegram']],
      // Not told whether there is a chat (an older fixture, a page cached before this deploy): as before
      [{ hasTelegram: false }, ['openInTelegram']],
      [{ hasTelegram: true, hasChat: true }, []],
      [{ trialDaysLeft: 3, hasLocation: false, hasTelegram: false, hasChat: false }, ['trial', 'location', 'connectTelegram']],
    ];
    for (const [facts, want] of cases) {
      const got = homeBanners({ ...base, ...facts } as never);
      assert(show(got) === show(want), `${show(facts)}: ${show(got)}, want ${show(want)}`);
    }

    installWindow();
    fakeWindow.localStorage = memoryStorage();
    assert(storage.connectBannerKey(7) === 'famcal:connectBanner:v1:7', storage.connectBannerKey(7));
    assert(storage.readConnectBannerClosed(7) === false, 'not closed yet');
    storage.writeConnectBannerClosed(7);
    assert(fakeWindow.localStorage.getItem('famcal:connectBanner:v1:7') === '1' && storage.readConnectBannerClosed(7) === true, 'closed and remembered');
    assert(storage.readConnectBannerClosed(8) === false, 'another account on the device keeps its banner');
    fakeWindow.localStorage = { getItem: () => { throw new Error('blocked'); }, setItem: () => { throw new Error('blocked'); }, removeItem: () => undefined };
    assert(storage.readConnectBannerClosed(7) === false, 'a storage that throws reads as not closed');
    storage.writeConnectBannerClosed(7);
    fakeWindow.localStorage = memoryStorage();

    const phases = ['idle', 'busy', 'leaving', 'opened', 'stale', 'limit', 'failed'] as const;
    assert(show(phases.map(connectButtonKey)) === show(['action', 'opening', 'signInAgain', 'action', 'signInAgain', 'action', 'action']), `button words ${show(phases.map(connectButtonKey))}`);
    assert(show(phases.map(connectLineKey)) === show([null, null, null, { key: 'opened', problem: false }, null, { key: 'limit', problem: true }, { key: 'failed', problem: true }]), `lines ${show(phases.map(connectLineKey))}`);
    assert(sessionEndedKey(true) === 'errors.reopen' && sessionEndedKey(false) === 'errors.reopenBrowser', 'the session-ended words');
  });

  await check('B2 openTelegramConnect: one POST /api/telegram-connect?user_id=<id> (same origin, JSON {}, no initData) and the bot link in this tab; a stale sign-in (its code or a 401), the limit (its code or a 429), has-chat, unavailable, a link that is not Telegram\'s, a body that is not JSON and no answer each say their kind and are logged; no log line holds the link or its token', async () => {
    reset();
    assert((await openTelegramConnect(7)) === 'opened', 'opened');
    const [call, ...more] = callsTo('/api/telegram-connect');
    assert(call && more.length === 0 && call.url === '/api/telegram-connect?user_id=7' && call.method === 'POST' && call.credentials === 'same-origin', `the request ${show(calls)}`);
    assert(call.headers['Content-Type'] === 'application/json' && show(call.body) === '{}' && !('X-Telegram-Init-Data' in call.headers), `headers and body ${show(call)}`);
    assert(fakeWindow.location.href === CONNECT_URL, `the tab went to ${show(fakeWindow.location.href)}`);
    assert(appLogs.length === 0, `logged on success: ${show(appLogs)}`);

    const cases: [string, () => Response, string][] = [
      ['stale-sign-in', () => json({ error: 'stale-sign-in' }, 403), 'stale-sign-in'],
      ['401', () => json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, 401), 'stale-sign-in'],
      ['limit', () => json({ error: 'limit' }, 429), 'limit'],
      ['429 without a code', () => json({}, 429), 'limit'],
      ['has-chat', () => json({ error: 'has-chat' }, 409), 'failed'],
      ['unavailable', () => json({ error: 'unavailable' }, 503), 'failed'],
      ['a link that is not Telegram\'s', () => json({ url: 'https://example.com/w_x' }), 'failed'],
      ['not JSON', () => new Response('<html>', { status: 500 }), 'failed'],
      ['no answer', () => { throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch'); }, 'failed'],
    ];
    for (const [what, answer, want] of cases) {
      reset();
      world.connect = answer;
      const got = await openTelegramConnect(7);
      assert(got === want, `${what}: ${got}, want ${want}`);
      assert(fakeWindow.location.href === 'https://famcal.bot/settings?user_id=1', `${what}: the tab moved to ${show(fakeWindow.location.href)}`);
      assert(appLogs.some((l) => l.startsWith('[telegram-connect]')), `${what}: not logged`);
      assert(!appLogs.some((l) => l.includes(CONNECT_TOKEN) || l.includes('t.me') || l.includes('example.com')), `${what}: a log holds a link: ${show(appLogs)}`);
    }
  });

  await check('B3 signInAgain: POST /api/auth/signout (same origin, JSON {}), then /signin in the page\'s language; a refused or failed sign-out stays on the page and is logged', async () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      reset();
      assert((await signInAgain(locale)) === true, `${locale}: true`);
      const [call] = callsTo('/api/auth/signout');
      assert(call && call.method === 'POST' && call.credentials === 'same-origin' && show(call.body) === '{}' && call.headers['Content-Type'] === 'application/json', `${locale}: the sign-out ${show(calls)}`);
      assert(show(assigned) === show([signInPath(locale)]), `${locale}: went to ${show(assigned)}`);
    }
    for (const [what, answer] of [['500', () => json({}, 500)], ['no answer', () => { throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch'); }]] as [string, () => Response][]) {
      reset();
      world.signout = answer;
      assert((await signInAgain('he')) === false && assigned.length === 0, `${what}: stays`);
      assert(appLogs.some((l) => l.startsWith('[sign-in-again]')), `${what}: not logged`);
    }
  });

  await check('B4 Settings with no chat (en, he, ru): the place card without the Shabbat pause; no Summaries, no Timing; the Telegram note card ("Briefings and reminders come in Telegram") with Connect Telegram; no voice input, no alerts, no Pro notice; the Events section only for the reminder time', async () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      for (const reminders of [false, true]) {
        reset();
        const m = mountIn(locale, Settings, settingsProps(locale, { nativeRemindersSupported: reminders }));
        await settle();
        try {
          const where = `${locale} reminders=${reminders}`;
          const want = [at(locale, 'settings.sections.place'), ...(reminders ? [at(locale, 'settings.sections.events')] : []), at(locale, 'settings.signIn.title')];
          assert(show(sectionLabels(m)) === show(want), `${where}: the sections ${show(sectionLabels(m))}, want ${show(want)}`);
          for (const key of ['pause.label', 'text.label', 'voice.label', 'weather.label', 'voiceInput.label', 'alerts.label', 'pickup.label']) {
            assert(!switches(m).some((s) => s.startsWith(at(locale, `settings.${key}`))), `${where}: the ${key} switch shows`);
          }
          const text = page(m);
          assert(text.includes(at(locale, 'settings.noChat.title')) && text.includes(at(locale, 'settings.noChat.body')), `${where}: the note card`);
          assert(!text.includes(at(locale, 'settings.alerts.proOnly')) && !text.includes(at(locale, 'settings.morning.label')), `${where}: the Pro notice or the timing shows`);
          assert(buttonsNamed(m.container, at(locale, 'telegramConnect.action')).length === 2, `${where}: Connect Telegram in the note card and in Sign in on the web: ${show(buttonsOf(m.container).map(flat))}`);
          const reminderRow = formRows(m).some((r) => flat(r).startsWith(at(locale, 'settings.reminderTime')));
          assert(reminderRow === reminders, `${where}: the reminder time ${reminderRow}`);
          // The language, the place, the zmanim community and the calendar stay
          for (const key of ['language.label', 'location.label', 'zmanim.label', 'culture.label']) assert(text.includes(at(locale, `settings.${key}`)), `${where}: ${key} is gone`);
        } finally {
          m.unmount();
        }
      }
    }
  });

  await check('B5 Settings with a chat: the place, summaries, timing and events sections and Sign in on the web; the pause, voice input and alert switches and the Pro notice as before; no note card and no Connect Telegram', async () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      reset(CHAT_VIEW);
      const m = mountIn(locale, Settings, settingsProps(locale, { hasChat: true, nativeRemindersSupported: true }));
      await settle();
      try {
        const want = ['place', 'summaries', 'timing', 'events'].map((k) => at(locale, `settings.sections.${k}`)).concat(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.title'));
        assert(show(sectionLabels(m)) === show(want), `${locale}: the sections ${show(sectionLabels(m))}`);
        for (const key of ['pause.label', 'text.label', 'voiceInput.label', 'alerts.label']) assert(switches(m).some((s) => s.startsWith(at(locale, `settings.${key}`))), `${locale}: no ${key} switch`);
        const text = page(m);
        assert(text.includes(at(locale, 'settings.alerts.proOnly')), `${locale}: the Pro notice`);
        assert(!text.includes(at(locale, 'settings.noChat.title')) && buttonsNamed(m.container, at(locale, 'telegramConnect.action')).length === 0, `${locale}: the note card shows with a chat`);
      } finally {
        m.unmount();
      }
    }
  });

  await check('B6 the note card\'s Connect Telegram: the link in this tab and "Finish in Telegram..."; a stale sign-in turns the button into "Sign in again to connect Telegram", whose press signs out and opens /signin; the hour\'s limit and a failure are alerts; a second tap while one runs sends nothing', async () => {
    reset();
    const m = mountIn('en', Settings, settingsProps('en'));
    await settle();
    try {
      let hold: (r: Response) => void = () => undefined;
      world.connect = () => new Promise<Response>((resolve) => void (hold = resolve));
      const [note] = buttonsNamed(m.container, at('en', 'telegramConnect.action'));
      m.click(note);
      m.click(note);
      await settle();
      assert(callsTo('/api/telegram-connect').length === 1 && note.getAttribute('aria-busy') === 'true' && flat(note) === at('en', 'telegramConnect.opening'), `one request at a time, said: ${flat(note)}`);
      await act(async () => {
        hold(json({ url: CONNECT_URL }));
        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
      });
      await settle();
      assert(callsTo('/api/telegram-connect')[0].url === '/api/telegram-connect?user_id=1' && fakeWindow.location.href === CONNECT_URL, 'the link opened');
      assert(page(m).includes(at('en', 'telegramConnect.opened')), 'what comes next');
    } finally {
      m.unmount();
    }

    reset();
    world.connect = () => json({ error: 'stale-sign-in' }, 403);
    const stale = mountIn('he', Settings, settingsProps('he'));
    await settle();
    try {
      stale.click(buttonsNamed(stale.container, at('he', 'telegramConnect.action'))[0]);
      await settle();
      const again = buttonsNamed(stale.container, at('he', 'telegramConnect.signInAgain'));
      assert(again.length === 1, `the button says sign in again: ${show(buttonsOf(stale.container).map(flat))}`);
      stale.click(again[0]);
      await settle();
      assert(callsTo('/api/auth/signout').length === 1 && show(assigned) === show(['/he/signin']) && callsTo('/api/telegram-connect').length === 1, `signed out, then /he/signin: ${show(assigned)}`);
    } finally {
      stale.unmount();
    }

    for (const [what, answer, key] of [
      ['limit', () => json({ error: 'limit' }, 429), 'limit'],
      ['no answer', () => { throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch'); }, 'failed'],
    ] as [string, () => Response, string][]) {
      reset();
      world.connect = answer;
      const r = mountIn('ru', Settings, settingsProps('ru'));
      await settle();
      try {
        r.click(buttonsNamed(r.container, at('ru', 'telegramConnect.action'))[0]);
        await settle();
        assert(alerts(r).includes(at('ru', `telegramConnect.${key}`)), `${what}: ${show(alerts(r))}`);
        assert(buttonsNamed(r.container, at('ru', 'telegramConnect.action')).length === 2, `${what}: the button is ready again`);
      } finally {
        r.unmount();
      }
    }
  });

  await check('B7 Sign in on the web with no chat: the browser hint (no word of Telegram and WhatsApp keeping working), a Telegram row "Not connected..." with Connect Telegram under it; with a chat the old hint and Telegram on', async () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      reset();
      const m = mountIn(locale, Settings, settingsProps(locale));
      await settle();
      try {
        const hints = elements(m.container).filter((e) => e.className === 'ch-form-hint').map(flat);
        assert(hints.includes(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.hintNoChat')) && !hints.includes(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.hint')), `${locale}: the hint ${show(hints)}`);
        const telegramRow = formRows(m).find((r) => flat(r).startsWith(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.telegram')));
        assert(telegramRow && flat(telegramRow).includes(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.telegramConnectHint')) && !flat(telegramRow).includes(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.on')), `${locale}: the Telegram row ${telegramRow && flat(telegramRow)}`);
        const connects = buttonsNamed(m.container, at(locale, 'telegramConnect.action'));
        assert(connects.length === 2 && connects[1].className === 'ch-form-row ch-action-row', `${locale}: Connect in the sign-in group`);
        m.click(connects[1]);
        await settle();
        assert(callsTo('/api/telegram-connect').length === 1 && fakeWindow.location.href === CONNECT_URL, `${locale}: the group's Connect opens the link`);
      } finally {
        m.unmount();
      }
      reset(CHAT_VIEW);
      const chat = mountIn(locale, Settings, settingsProps(locale, { hasChat: true }));
      await settle();
      try {
        const hints = elements(chat.container).filter((e) => e.className === 'ch-form-hint').map(flat);
        assert(hints.includes(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.hint')), `${locale}: the old hint`);
        const row = formRows(chat).find((r) => flat(r).startsWith(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.telegram')));
        assert(row && flat(row).includes(at(locale, 'settings.signIn.on')), `${locale}: Telegram on`);
      } finally {
        chat.unmount();
      }
    }
  });

  await check('B8 Plans with no chat: "Plans are paid with Telegram Stars..." with Connect Telegram (which asks for the link), no pay button, no Stars or WhatsApp note; WhatsApp-only keeps "Paying with Telegram Stars needs Telegram"; early access shows neither', async () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      reset();
      const m = mountIn(locale, Subscription, planProps(locale));
      await settle();
      try {
        const text = page(m);
        assert(text.includes(at(locale, 'subscription.screen.connectTelegram')), `${locale}: the line`);
        assert(!text.includes(at(locale, 'subscription.screen.needsTelegram')) && !text.includes(at(locale, 'subscription.screen.starsNote')), `${locale}: the WhatsApp or Stars note`);
        assert(buttonsNamed(m.container, at(locale, 'subscription.screen.agreeAndPay')).length === 0, `${locale}: a pay button`);
        const action = buttonsOf(m.container).find((b) => b.className === 'ch-notice-action' && flat(b) === at(locale, 'telegramConnect.action'));
        assert(action, `${locale}: Connect Telegram ${show(buttonsOf(m.container).map(flat))}`);
        m.click(action);
        await settle();
        assert(callsTo('/api/telegram-connect')[0]?.url === '/api/telegram-connect?user_id=41' && fakeWindow.location.href === CONNECT_URL, `${locale}: the link`);
      } finally {
        m.unmount();
      }
      reset();
      const wa = mountIn(locale, Subscription, planProps(locale, { hasChat: true }));
      try {
        assert(page(wa).includes(at(locale, 'subscription.screen.needsTelegram')) && !page(wa).includes(at(locale, 'subscription.screen.connectTelegram')), `${locale}: WhatsApp-only`);
      } finally {
        wa.unmount();
      }
      const early = mountIn(locale, Subscription, planProps(locale, { isEarlyAdopter: true }));
      try {
        assert(!page(early).includes(at(locale, 'subscription.screen.connectTelegram')) && !page(early).includes(at(locale, 'subscription.screen.needsTelegram')), `${locale}: early access`);
      } finally {
        early.unmount();
      }
    }
  });

  await check('B9 the page gate\'s card in a browser says to sign in ("Sign in to open this page") and leads with Sign in, then WhatsApp and Telegram; it no longer says to open the page from a chat; inside Telegram it is as before', () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      const html = renderToString(inApp(locale, createElement(NoCredentialCard, { inTelegram: false, links: LINKS })));
      const text = textOf(html);
      assert(text.includes(at(locale, 'pageGate.signInTitle')) && text.includes(at(locale, 'pageGate.signInBody')), `${locale}: the words ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);
      assert(!text.includes(at(locale, 'pageGate.browserTitle')) && !text.includes(at(locale, 'pageGate.browserBody')), `${locale}: the chat words`);
      const signIn = html.indexOf(`href="${signInPath(locale)}"`);
      const wa = html.indexOf(`href="${LINKS.whatsapp}"`);
      const tg = html.indexOf(`href="${LINKS.telegram}"`);
      assert(signIn > 0 && signIn < wa && wa < tg, `${locale}: the order ${signIn} ${wa} ${tg}`);
      const telegram = textOf(renderToString(inApp(locale, createElement(NoCredentialCard, { inTelegram: true, links: LINKS }))));
      assert(telegram.includes(at(locale, 'pageGate.telegramTitle')) && !telegram.includes(at(locale, 'pageGate.signInTitle')), `${locale}: inside Telegram`);
    }
  });

  await check('B10 the words: every new key in en, he and ru, none empty, no emoji, Hebrew and Russian in their own letters; the browser words never send anyone to the bot; every telegramConnect key is read by the helper or a screen', () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      for (const key of NEW_KEYS) {
        const value = at(locale, key);
        assert(value.trim() !== '' && !/\p{Extended_Pictographic}/u.test(value), `${locale}: ${key} is empty or has an emoji`);
        if (locale === 'he') assert(/[֐-׿]/.test(value), `he: ${key} has no Hebrew: ${value}`);
        if (locale === 'ru') assert(/[А-Яа-яЁё]/.test(value), `ru: ${key} has no Russian: ${value}`);
      }
      // famcal.bot is the site's address, not the bot
      for (const key of BROWSER_KEYS) assert(!/\bbot\b|בוט|бот/i.test(at(locale, key).replace(/famcal\.bot/g, '')), `${locale}: ${key} names the bot: ${at(locale, key)}`);
      assert(show(Object.keys(messages[locale].telegramConnect).sort()) === show(['action', 'failed', 'limit', 'opened', 'opening', 'signInAgain']), `${locale}: telegramConnect ${show(Object.keys(messages[locale].telegramConnect))}`);
    }
    const sources = ['src/lib/telegram-connect-client.ts', 'app/[locale]/(app)/dashboard/HomeBanners.tsx', 'app/[locale]/(app)/settings/SettingsClient.tsx', 'app/[locale]/(app)/settings/SignInMethods.tsx', 'app/[locale]/(app)/subscription/SubscriptionClient.tsx']
      .map((f) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, f), 'utf8'))
      .join('\n');
    for (const key of Object.keys(messages.en.telegramConnect)) assert(sources.includes(`'${key}'`), `telegramConnect.${key} is read by nothing`);
  });

  await check('B11 the wiring: page-data sends hasChat (Task 1\'s hasChat) for the home, Settings and Plans; PageGate hands it to the home; the home gives the header Send only with a chat, the banners hasChat and their close, the empty state its hint; Sign in on the web reads view.chat and takes no hasChat prop; Calendars and Select calendars choose the session-ended words by place', () => {
    const src = (f: string) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, f), 'utf8');
    const pageData = src('src/lib/page-data.ts');
    assert((pageData.match(/hasChat: hasChat\(user\)/g) ?? []).length === 3 && pageData.includes("import { hasChat } from '@/src/lib/has-chat';"), 'page-data: hasChat for the dashboard, settings and subscription, from src/lib/has-chat');
    assert(/hasChat: p\.hasChat/.test(src('app/[locale]/(app)/PageGate.tsx')), 'PageGate: the home gets hasChat');
    const home = src('app/[locale]/(app)/dashboard/CalendarHome.tsx');
    assert(/onSend=\{hasChat === false \? undefined : \(\) => setSheet\('send'\)\}/.test(home), 'CalendarHome: Send only with a chat');
    assert(/hasChat=\{hasChat\}/.test(home) && /connectClosed=\{connectClosed\}/.test(home) && /onCloseConnect=\{closeConnect\}/.test(home) && /hints=\{shownHints\}/.test(home), 'CalendarHome: the banners and the hint');
    const signIn = src('app/[locale]/(app)/settings/SignInMethods.tsx');
    assert(/view\.chat \? t\('hint'\) : t\('hintNoChat'\)/.test(signIn) && /\{!view\.chat \? \(/.test(signIn) && !/hasChat/.test(signIn), 'Sign in on the web: the hint and the Telegram row by view.chat, and no hasChat prop');
    assert(/<SignInMethods userId=\{userId\} onSheet=/.test(src('app/[locale]/(app)/settings/SettingsClient.tsx')), 'Settings hands Sign in on the web no hasChat');
    assert(/t\(sessionEndedKey\(isInTelegram\(\)\)\)/.test(src('app/[locale]/(app)/calendars/CalendarsClient.tsx')), 'Calendars: the session-ended words by place');
    assert(/page\(sessionEndedKey\(isInTelegram\(\)\)\)/.test(src('app/[locale]/(app)/select-calendars/SelectCalendarsClient.tsx')), 'Select calendars: the session-ended words by place');
    assert(/sendResultKey\(answer, isInTelegram\(\)\)/.test(src('app/[locale]/(app)/dashboard/SendSheet.tsx')), 'the Send sheet: the session-ended words by place');
  });

  await check('B13 the missing-link card (a page opened without user_id): in a browser "Sign in again to open your calendar." with Sign in, one link to /signin in the page\'s language, and no word of the bot; inside Telegram, and in the server\'s markup, the card as before with no Sign in', () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      const title = at(locale, 'ui.missingParameter.title');
      reset();
      const browser = mount(inApp(locale, createElement(MissingParameterCard)));
      try {
        const card = elements(browser.container).find((e) => e.getAttribute('role') === 'alert');
        assert(card && flat(card) === `${title}${at(locale, 'ui.missingParameter.bodyBrowser')}${at(locale, 'pageGate.signIn')}`, `${locale}: the browser card ${card && flat(card)}`);
        const links = elements(card).filter((e) => e.localName === 'a');
        assert(links.length === 1 && links[0].getAttribute('href') === signInPath(locale) && flat(links[0]) === at(locale, 'pageGate.signIn'), `${locale}: Sign in ${show(links.map((a) => a.getAttribute('href')))}`);
      } finally {
        browser.unmount();
      }
      reset();
      fakeWindow.Telegram = { WebApp: fakeTelegram([], '7.7') };
      const inside = mount(inApp(locale, createElement(MissingParameterCard)));
      try {
        const card = elements(inside.container).find((e) => e.getAttribute('role') === 'alert');
        assert(card && flat(card) === `${title}${at(locale, 'ui.missingParameter.body')}` && !elements(card).some((e) => e.localName === 'a'), `${locale}: inside Telegram ${card && flat(card)}`);
      } finally {
        inside.unmount();
        fakeWindow.Telegram = undefined;
      }
      // The server's markup (and so the first render that hydrates it) is the card as it was
      const server = textOf(renderToString(inApp(locale, createElement(MissingParameterCard))));
      assert(server.includes(at(locale, 'ui.missingParameter.body')) && !server.includes(at(locale, 'ui.missingParameter.bodyBrowser')), `${locale}: the server's markup ${server}`);
    }
  });

  await check('B12 React logged no warning', () => {
    assert(reactWarnings.length === 0, show(reactWarnings.slice(0, 5)));
  });

  let failed = 0;
  for (const r of results) {
    console.log(`${r.ok ? 'OK' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name}${r.ok ? '' : ` — ${r.reason}`}`);
    if (!r.ok) failed++;
  }
  console.log(`\n${results.length - failed}/${results.length} passed (process TZ=${process.env.TZ ?? 'unset'})`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
}

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```ts
// - A card needs the app's tokens above it: inside an AppScreen. MissingParameterCard and
```

4.5 Create `src/lib/sign-in-again.ts`:
```ts
// Signing in again from an app screen in a browser (spec 2026-11-03-web-sign-up §2.13, §3.6; plan 6c-1 Task 9). A screen whose
// request was refused because this browser's sign-in ended, and a Connect Telegram button whose sign-in is over an hour old,
// send the person to /signin. /signin sends a browser that still holds a cookie straight to its calendar (it reads only the
// cookie's signature and age), so this browser signs out first (POST /api/auth/signout clears the cookie; no database query),
// then opens /signin in the page's language. Inside Telegram the chat's buttons reopen the Mini App instead, and the screens
// keep their "open it again from the bot" words there (sessionEndedKey).
//
// Client-safe: one import, and the log lines carry a status or an error's name only.

import { signInHref } from '@/src/site/signin';

const TAG = '[sign-in-again]';

/** calendarsPage's words for a request refused because the sign-in ended: the bot's inside Telegram, the browser's outside it. */
export function sessionEndedKey(inTelegram: boolean): 'errors.reopen' | 'errors.reopenBrowser' {
  return inTelegram ? 'errors.reopen' : 'errors.reopenBrowser';
}

/** Signs this browser out, then opens /signin. False (logged; the page stays) when the sign-out or the move failed. */
export async function signInAgain(locale: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const res = await fetch('/api/auth/signout', { method: 'POST', credentials: 'same-origin', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: '{}' });
    if (!res.ok) {
      console.warn(`${TAG} signing out answered ${res.status}`);
      return false;
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`${TAG} signing out got no answer: ${error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error}`);
    return false;
  }
  try {
    window.location.assign(signInHref(locale));
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`${TAG} /signin could not be opened: ${error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error}`);
    return false;
  }
}
```

4.6 Create `src/lib/telegram-connect-client.ts`:
```ts
// Connect Telegram from the browser (spec 2026-11-03-web-sign-up §2.9, §3.6, §4; plan 6c-1 Task 9): the one client helper the
// home's banner, Settings (the note card and Sign in on the web) and Plans share. A press asks POST
// /api/telegram-connect?user_id=<id> (Task 6's route: the session cookie, a sign-in within the hour, 5 links an hour) for a
// one-time bot link and opens it in this tab: on a phone Telegram's app takes it, on a computer t.me's page offers to open it.
// A sign-in over an hour old answers 'stale-sign-in' (or a 401 when the session is gone): the button then says "Sign in again
// to connect Telegram", and its press signs this browser out and opens /signin (signInAgain), so the next sign-in is fresh.
// The link is a credential for 10 minutes: no log line holds it or its token; a failure logs the status and a known error code.
//
// Client-safe. Strings: telegramConnect.* (each screen words them; this file names the keys only).

import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { readJsonBody } from '@/src/lib/read-json';
import { signInAgain } from '@/src/lib/sign-in-again';

const TAG = '[telegram-connect]';
/** The route's refusals (Task 6): the only error codes a log line may name. */
const KNOWN_ERRORS: readonly string[] = ['has-chat', 'stale-sign-in', 'limit', 'unavailable'];

export type ConnectResult = 'opened' | 'stale-sign-in' | 'limit' | 'failed';

/** Asks for the one-time link and opens it in this tab; what came of it. Never throws. */
export async function openTelegramConnect(userId: number): Promise<ConnectResult> {
  let res: Response;
  try {
    res = await fetch(`/api/telegram-connect?user_id=${userId}`, {
      method: 'POST',
      credentials: 'same-origin',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: '{}',
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`${TAG} the request got no answer: ${error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error}`);
    return 'failed';
  }
  const body = await readJsonBody(res, TAG);
  const url = body?.url;
  if (res.ok && typeof url === 'string') {
    if (!url.startsWith('https://t.me/')) {
      console.error(`${TAG} the answer (${res.status}) is not a Telegram link`);
      return 'failed';
    }
    try {
      window.location.href = url;
      return 'opened';
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`${TAG} the link could not be opened: ${error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error}`);
      return 'failed';
    }
  }
  const code = typeof body?.error === 'string' && KNOWN_ERRORS.includes(body.error) ? body.error : null;
  console.warn(`${TAG} answered ${res.status} (${code ?? 'no known code'})`);
  if (code === 'stale-sign-in' || res.status === 401) return 'stale-sign-in';
  if (code === 'limit' || res.status === 429) return 'limit';
  return 'failed';
}

/** Where a Connect Telegram button is. 'leaving' is the sign-out on the way to /signin after a stale sign-in. */
export type ConnectPhase = 'idle' | 'busy' | 'leaving' | 'opened' | 'stale' | 'limit' | 'failed';

/** The button's words for a phase, a key of telegramConnect. */
export function connectButtonKey(phase: ConnectPhase): 'action' | 'opening' | 'signInAgain' {
  if (phase === 'busy') return 'opening';
  if (phase === 'stale' || phase === 'leaving') return 'signInAgain';
  return 'action';
}

/** The line under the button (a key of telegramConnect) and whether it is a problem (an alert); null when there is none. */
export function connectLineKey(phase: ConnectPhase): { key: 'opened' | 'limit' | 'failed'; problem: boolean } | null {
  if (phase === 'opened') return { key: 'opened', problem: false };
  if (phase === 'limit') return { key: 'limit', problem: true };
  if (phase === 'failed') return { key: 'failed', problem: true };
  return null;
}

const PHASE_OF: Record<ConnectResult, ConnectPhase> = { opened: 'opened', 'stale-sign-in': 'stale', limit: 'limit', failed: 'failed' };

/**
 * One Connect Telegram button: its phase and its press. A press asks for the link, or after a stale sign-in signs in again.
 * One request at a time: a second press while one runs, or after the page started leaving for /signin, does nothing.
 */
export function useTelegramConnect(userId: number, locale: string): { phase: ConnectPhase; press: () => void } {
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<ConnectPhase>('idle');
  const running = useRef(false);
  const press = () => {
    if (running.current) return;
    running.current = true;
    if (phase === 'stale') {
      setPhase('leaving');
      void signInAgain(locale).then((left) => {
        // Leaving: the page is on its way to /signin and the button keeps its spinner; a failure lets it be pressed again.
        if (left) return;
        running.current = false;
        setPhase('failed');
      });
      return;
    }
    setPhase('busy');
    void openTelegramConnect(userId).then((result) => {
      running.current = false;
      setPhase(PHASE_OF[result]);
    });
  };
  return { phase, press };
}
```

```tsx
function BannerContent({ id, title, body, action }: { id: BannerId; title: string; body?: string; action?: string }) {
  return (
    <>
      <BannerIcon id={id} />
      <span className="ch-banner-text">
        <span className="ch-banner-title">{title}</span>
        {body ? <span className="ch-banner-body">{body}</span> : null}

    </>
```

```tsx
/**
 * Connect Telegram, for an account with no chat (6c-1): the banner's own button (the bot's one-time link, or Sign in again
 * after a stale sign-in) and its close, side by side in one banner; what came of a press is a line under it.
 */
function ConnectTelegramBanner({ userId, locale, onClose }: { userId: number; locale: string; onClose?: () => void }) {
  const t = useTranslations('calendarHome');
  const c = useTranslations('telegramConnect');
  const { phase, press } = useTelegramConnect(userId, locale);
  const working = phase === 'busy' || phase === 'leaving';
  const line = connectLineKey(phase);
  return (
    <>
      <div className="ch-banner ch-banner-telegram ch-banner-split" data-banner="connectTelegram">
        <button type="button" className="ch-banner-main ch-tap" disabled={working} aria-busy={working || undefined} onClick={press}>
          <Send className="ch-banner-icon ch-flip" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" />
          <span className="ch-banner-text">
            <span className="ch-banner-title">{c(connectButtonKey(phase))}</span>
            <span className="ch-banner-body">{t('banner.connectTelegramBody')}</span>
          </span>
          {working ? <Loader2 className="ch-banner-chevron ch-spin" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" /> : <Chevron />}
        </button>
        {onClose ? (
          <button type="button" className="ch-banner-close ch-tap" aria-label={t('banner.close')} onClick={onClose}>
            <X aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" />
          </button>
        ) : null}
      </div>
      {line ? (
        <p className={line.problem ? 'ch-banner-line is-problem' : 'ch-banner-line'} role={line.problem ? 'alert' : 'status'}>
          {c(line.key)}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}

export function HomeBanners({ userId, locale, onNavigate, onCloseConnect, ...facts }: HomeBannersProps) {
```

## Part G: Task 10 (Google Calendar: Finish here) and Task 11 (the partner invite on the web)

### Task 10: Google Calendar: Finish here

#### Notes for Tasks 10–11 (read first)

1. **Builds on:** Task 1 (`hasChat`, `src/lib/has-chat.ts`), Task 3 (the email request's Turnstile `token`, `SignInClient`'s `turnstileSiteKey` prop), Task 4 (`src/lib/invite-token.ts` with `cleanInviteToken`, `inviteOf` in `flow.ts`, `SignUpFlow`, the verify route's `signIn`/`signUpNext`, `signUpPageUrl`), Task 5 (`invite?` on `OidcFlow`/`EmailFlow`, the Google callback's sign-up branch, `completeSignUp` in `src/services/web-signin/signup.ts`, `POST /api/auth/signup`, `smoke-signup`), Task 6 (`stubModule`, the scrubber's `CONNECT_TOKEN`/`GOOGLE_CONNECT_ID`), Task 7 (`FinishPage`'s `{ join }` and `addGoogleJoinHref`). `$RUN` is the header's runner. `scripts/ci-smokes.sh` runs every `scripts/smoke-*.ts` by glob, so the two new smokes need no entry. All commands run from `/Users/razielgershoni/development/famcalbot`.
2. **The waiting connection's id never rides a URL our server sees (ruling #27):** the check is `POST /api/oauth/claim { token, peek: true }` → `{ mine }`, the claim `POST /api/oauth/claim { token }`; there is no GET. Why: a query string can reach Railway's HTTP logs, and the finish page keeps the id in the fragment on purpose (`finishPageUrl`). `token` is already a body name the Sentry scrubber drops (`src/lib/sentry-scrub.ts:53-60`), and no line logs the id.
3. **The claim's answer:** `{ ok: true, page, userId, redirect }`, `page` = `'select-calendars'` for a connect, `'calendars'` for a copy-to-Google (`sync`) consent, as the chat claim leads (`google-connect.ts:402-425`); `redirect` is `appPageUrl(owner.language, page, owner.id)`, so the page never builds an app URL. Errors add `'failed'` (500) for a commit that throws half-way (`tryClaim`, `:365-372`).
4. **The claim's order:** the session is checked in full (`readSession`, then `verifyUserAuth(…, 'oauth-claim')`) before `claimPendingGoogleToken`, so a press with no session or an ended one leaves the entry for the chat claim; another account's live session uses it up and connects nothing (`not_owner`), as the chat claim from someone else does. The check runs `verifyUserAuth` only when the cookie's id equals the entry's owner, so an ended session never shows Finish here.
5. **No chat button and not "mine"** (a browser-only owner whose consent browser isn't signed in): a "Sign in to finish" card, not "This link is incomplete … from the FamCal bot". F3's `#p=<valid>&b=` case moves to F5.
6. **`cleanInviteToken` and `inviteOf` are Task 4's (ruling #3):** Task 11 imports them and checks that every flow kind reads `inviteOf`; it adds no second one. Task 4's smoke holds the `cleanInviteToken` checks, so `smoke-invite-web` W1 checks only the landing.
7. **One landing rule (ruling #4):** `FinishPage = 'dashboard' | 'select-calendars' | 'calendars' | { invite: string } | { join: string }`; `appPageUrl` lands `{ invite }` on `/{locale}/invite/{token}` (no `user_id`: the invite page reads the session cookie) and `{ join }` on Task 7's `addGoogleJoinHref`. Every finish passes `page: landingPage(flow.invite)`: the Telegram and Google callbacks, the email verify's `signIn(userId, address, invite?)` (ruling #5, both callers pass `flow.invite`) and `completeSignUp`'s `finishSignIn` line, whose `done()` stays (ruling #13).
8. **Task 11 owns the invite page alone (ruling #7):** `invite.errorGenericWeb` and the `smoke-invite-render` V checks are here; Task 9 doesn't touch `app/[locale]/(app)/invite/[token]/*`.
9. **The invite page reads no `hasChat` (ruling #22):** an account with no chat is never inside Telegram, so `isInTelegram` (the client's `viaTelegram`) already covers spec §3.11's reader.
10. **Sentry:** besides the `invite` query and body name, the invite page's own path `/invite/<64 hex>` is scrubbed (URLs, transaction names, breadcrumbs): since a cookie can now accept, the token in a Sentry URL is worth as much as in a query.
11. **`refuseCrossSite` on the pair routes** (POST `/api/pair/accept`, POST and DELETE `/api/pair/invite`) breaks three smokes that call them with no Origin (`smoke-pairing-accept`, `smoke-auth-identity` #9/#10, `smoke-initdata-header`); Task 11 gives them the app's Origin (`http://localhost:3000` under the fake env). The Mini App's own POST/DELETE are same-origin `fetch` with a JSON body, which send `Origin`.
12. **`notifyInviterOfAccept`** uses `hasChat` (Task 1); its silent returns log, and the accept route's `PairingError` branch logs its code.
13. **`/signin?invite=` with a valid session** redirects to the invite page, not the calendar. `InviteClient`'s new prop is `sessionUserId: number | null`, read as `props.sessionUserId ?? null`, so smokes that mount it without the prop behave as signed out.
14. **Review Focus 4 (Rf4)** is `smoke-invite-web` W13: an invite revoked, or accepted by someone else, while its visitor signs up still lands the new, unpaired account on the invite, whose page shows its invalid card.

```ts
/** Every waiting-connection id this run made, for the log check */
```
