Dispatch one fresh agent on **Opus, high effort**. It is a legal review of binding text, so not a cheap model. It reads and reports, and it never edits. Prompt:

```text
You are reviewing a change to FamCal's Privacy Policy and Terms (a family-calendar assistant run by a sole trader in
Israel; users in Israel, the EU/UK and elsewhere). The texts are binding in all three languages, and the Hebrew and
Russian bind their readers as the English does. READ-ONLY: do not edit any file and do not run git commands that change
anything.

Read, in /Users/razielgershoni/development/famcalbot:
1. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md, section 7 (the approved English wording) and sections 2-5
   (what the product does, so you can check the text against it).
2. The diff of the three files: git diff main -- messages/en.json messages/he.json messages/ru.json src/site/legal.ts
   (only the legal.* keys; ignore site.cta).
3. The whole legal.privacy and legal.terms of each file, for context.

Report, as a numbered list, each finding with its language, its key path (legal.<doc>.sections.<id>.blocks[...]), the
current text and the exact replacement you propose:
- English: any place that is not spec §7's wording exactly, and any §7 item that is missing.
- Hebrew and Russian: any sentence whose meaning differs from the English (added, lost or changed obligations, scope,
  durations, conditions, the 18+ rule, who receives what), anything that reads as translated word for word rather than
  as natural legal Hebrew or Russian, Hebrew that addresses the reader in a gendered form, and Russian that is not the
  formal «вы».
- Consistency: the new text against the rest of each document (retention periods, Cookies, Your rights, the providers
  list, Legal grounds), and against what the product does per the spec.
- One open point to rule on: the two new 10-minute items sit in the "Short-lived copies" list under the lead-in
  "The longest are:" (as spec §7 places them). Say whether that reads correctly, and if not, propose the smallest fix
  that keeps the list's block position.
Say "no findings" for a language with none. Keep the report under 800 words.
```

Then fix every valid finding, in all three languages at once. Change the English only where it departs from spec §7. A change of meaning beyond §7 goes to the owner first (CLAUDE.md). After each fix, update `SAYS_SIGNUP` or `SAYS` in `smoke-signin-legal.ts` if a pinned sentence changed, and rerun Step 5's loop.

After `:132` (the Resend setup step), the next heading, before:
```markdown
### Install & run
```
after:
```markdown
### Web sign-up

A new person creates a FamCal account on famcal.bot with Google or an email code and uses it in any browser, with no Telegram and no WhatsApp (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-web-sign-up-design.md`). Sign-up is the end of a sign-in that found no account: the proved identity waits 10 minutes in a one-time `signup` record behind `famcal_signin`, and `/signup` takes a name and the consent (18 or older, the Terms and the Privacy Policy). The account is made by `createAccount` (`src/services/user-service.ts`), the same step /start and a first WhatsApp message use: the ban check, the user and its way in one transaction, the first FamCal calendar.

- **Email:** with `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` and `TURNSTILE_SECRET` set, every code request needs Cloudflare Turnstile's pass, and an address on no account gets a sign-up code (30 a UTC day inside the 90 codes, 3 a day per IP address). Without them email sign-up is off and email sign-in works as before.
- **Google:** a Google account that no account holds in any way (no Google way with its `sub`, no calendar key for its address) is offered sign-up.
- **Stopped or warned:** a proved address that already signs in another way gets that way's guidance and no form (`findWayByAddress`); the sign-up page warns a Telegram or WhatsApp user not to make a second account.
- **Limits:** 5 new accounts a day per IPv4 address or IPv6 /48; security notices by email have their own 10 a day.
- **No chat:** a browser-only account sees nothing that needs a chat. **Connect Telegram** (a one-time `w_` bot link, 10 minutes, made within an hour of signing in) writes the Telegram id onto it. An accidental second account is joined into the first only after Add Google or Add email proves its way (`mergePlan`, one rule set for the question and the merge). The Google Calendar finish page offers **Finish here** to the session of the account that started the consent.

One-time setup: Cloudflare → Turnstile → Add widget "FamCal sign-in", hostname `famcal.bot`, widget mode Managed, pre-clearance off; its site key goes in `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` and its secret key in `TURNSTILE_SECRET`. Production startup logs `[startup] web sign-up with an email code is off` until both are set. Run 6b's `x-real-ip` probe before announcing sign-up: the per-address limits count by that header. Also before announcing: a family whose Google Calendar was connected before 6b has no `googleAccountKey`, so "Continue with Google" offers them sign-up (with the second-account warning) until they press **Turn on** in Settings; ask them to press it once.

### Install & run
```
